definition_en: the science of water on Earth: its movement, distribution, storage and interaction with land, air and life

sceneCN: 这里指「研究地球上水的分布与运动的学科」（第 1 个义项：以水文循环、径流、蒸发与储水为对象的科学）；句意为水文学解释了为什么雨停数日之后河水才上涨。场景物件：水位尺、河谷、循环图、雨量筒。

senses.title: The scientific discipline
senses.definition: the science of water on Earth: its movement, distribution, storage and interaction with land, air and life
senses.definitionCN: 研究地球上水的运动、分布、储存及与陆地、空气和生命相互作用的科学
senses.example: Hydrology explains why the river rises days after the rain has stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 水文学解释了为什么雨停数日之后河水才上涨。
senses.why: Hydro- is water and -logy is reasoned study, so the word names the disciplined study of water rather than water itself.
senses.whyCN: hydro- 是水，-logy 是系统的研究，因此这个词命名的是对水的学科研究，而非水本身。

senses.title: The study of the water cycle
senses.definition: the branch that tracks evaporation, precipitation, runoff and storage as one cycle
senses.definitionCN: 把蒸发、降水、径流与储水作为同一循环追踪的分支
senses.example: Hydrology treats the catchment as one connected cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 水文学把流域看作一个相连的循环。
senses.why: The discipline's central object is the cycle, so the word often means the study of that loop rather than all water science.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的核心对象是循环，因此这个词常指对这一闭环的研究，而非全部水科学。

senses.title: A regional water regime
senses.definition: the actual pattern of water in a place: when it arrives, where it goes and how it varies
senses.definitionCN: 某地水的实际格局：何时到来、流向何处、如何变化
senses.example: The hydrology of the delta changed after the dam was built.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝建成后，三角洲的水文情势改变了。
senses.why: Scientists say the hydrology of a place when they mean its measured regime, not the abstract discipline.
senses.whyCN: 科学家说某地的 hydrology，指的是实测的水文情势，而不是抽象学科。

senses.title: Hydrological processes
senses.definition: the physical processes of infiltration, runoff, evaporation and groundwater flow
senses.definitionCN: 下渗、径流、蒸发与地下水流动等物理过程
senses.example: Hydrology studies how water moves through soil and rock.
senses.exampleCN: 水文学研究水如何穿过土壤与岩石。
senses.why: The discipline is often reduced to its processes, so the word can name the mechanisms rather than the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科常被化约为它的过程，因此这个词可指机制本身，而非整个领域。

senses.title: Water-resource assessment
senses.definition: the applied work of estimating supply, recharge and safe yield
senses.definitionCN: 估算供水、补给与安全开采量的应用工作
senses.example: Hydrology sets how much groundwater can be pumped each year.
senses.exampleCN: 水文学决定每年可抽取多少地下水。
senses.why: Society needs numbers for supply, so the science acquired an applied assessment sense.
senses.whyCN: 社会需要供水的数字，因此这门科学获得了应用评估义。

senses.title: Engineering hydrology
senses.definition: the branch that supplies design floods, spillways and drainage capacity
senses.definitionCN: 为设计洪水、溢洪道与排水能力提供依据的分支
senses.example: Engineering hydrology fixed the spillway width.
senses.exampleCN: 工程水文学确定了溢洪道宽度。
senses.why: Builders need extreme values, so a distinct applied branch took the name of the parent science.
senses.whyCN: 建造者需要极值，于是出现了一个以母学科命名的应用分支。

senses.title: Ecohydrology
senses.definition: the study of how water and living communities shape each other
senses.definitionCN: 研究水与生命群落如何相互塑造的学问
senses.example: Hydrology and ecology meet in the study of wetland plants.
senses.exampleCN: 水文学与生态学在湿地植物研究中相遇。
senses.why: When water is studied through its effects on organisms, the field gains an ecological face.
senses.whyCN: 当水通过其对生物的影响被研究，这门学问就多了一张生态面孔。

senses.title: Planetary hydrology
senses.definition: the study of water and water-like fluids on other planets and moons
senses.definitionCN: 研究其他行星与卫星上的水及类水液体的学问
senses.example: Planetary hydrology compares Earth's rivers with channels on Mars.
senses.exampleCN: 行星水文学把地球的河流与火星的河道相比较。
senses.why: The methods travel beyond Earth, so the word now covers water systems on other worlds.
senses.whyCN: 方法可以离开地球，因此这个词如今涵盖其他世界的水系统。

intro.en: Hydrology joins Greek hydōr 'water' to -logia 'study, reasoned account'. The English word is recorded from the eighteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hydrology 把希腊 hydōr「水」与 -logia「研究、系统论述」组合起来。英语词自十八世纪有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hydōr meant 'water'; its deeper origin is often connected with a reconstructed Indo-European root *wed- 'water', but that root is a reconstruction, not a demonstrated form.
items.cn: hydōr 意为「水」；其更深来源常被联系到重构的印欧词根 *wed-「水」，但那只是重构，不是已证实的形式。

items.en: Logos meant 'word, reason, account', and -logia named a field of reasoned study; legein 'to gather, say' is its verb.
items.cn: logos 意为「言词、理性、论述」，-logia 命名一个系统研究的领域；其动词是 legein「聚集、言说」。

items.en: Modern Latin used hydrologia for the study of water, and English borrowed the pattern in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 近代拉丁用 hydrologia 指对水的研究，英语在十八世纪借用了这一构词模式。

items.en: Early hydrology was mostly descriptive and engineering-oriented, concerned with springs, rivers and water supply.
items.cn: 早期水文学多为描述性与工程导向，关心泉、河流与供水。

items.en: In the twentieth century hydrology became a quantitative science of the whole cycle, using gauges, tracers and models.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，水文学成为研究整个循环的定量科学，使用水位计、示踪剂与模型。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Greek source of hydōr is uncertain, *wed- is a reconstruction, and the first English use of hydrology is not exactly dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：hydōr 的前希腊语来源不确定，*wed- 属重构，hydrology 最早的英语使用没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds the same hydr- stock with different grammatical jobs; group two holds neighbouring water sciences that are often confused with hydrology.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 hydr- 词干、语法角色不同的词；第二组是常与水文学混淆的邻近水科学。

entries.definition: Relating to hydrology; it modifies a noun and cannot stand alone as the name of the science.
entries.definitionCN: 与水文学有关的；它修饰名词，不能独自作为学科名。

entries.definition: A person who practises hydrology; it is the agent, not the field.
entries.definitionCN: 从事水文学的人；它是施事者，不是领域。

entries.definition: The shorter American adjective for the same idea; it differs in spelling, not in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 同一概念的较短美式形容词；差别在拼写，不在意义。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning water; it builds words such as hydrosphere and hydroelectric but is not a word by itself.
entries.definitionCN: 表示水的构词成分；它构成 hydrosphere、hydroelectric 等词，但本身不是独立词。

entries.definition: The measurement and mapping of water bodies for navigation; it describes where water is, not how it moves.
entries.definitionCN: 为航行测量并绘制水体；它描述水在哪里，而不是水如何运动。

entries.definition: The mechanics of fluids in motion and under pressure; it is the physics used by hydrology, not the whole science.
entries.definitionCN: 研究流体运动与受压的力学；它是水文学使用的物理，而不是整个科学。

entries.definition: The geology of groundwater; it is a subfield of hydrology focused on rock and aquifers.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地下水的地质学；它是水文学中聚焦岩石与含水层的子领域。

entries.definition: The study of water in the atmosphere and its transfer to the ground; it is the weather side of the cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 研究大气中的水及其向地面输送；它是循环中天气的一侧。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek parts, real subfields and real measurement terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实希腊构件、真实子领域与真实测量术语。

normal.en: Hydro- is water; -logy is reasoned study.
normal.cn: hydro- 是水；-logy 是系统研究。

normal.en: Hydrology follows the whole cycle, not just rivers.
normal.cn: 水文学追踪整个循环，不只是河流。

normal.en: A hydrograph is the plotted rise and fall of a river.
normal.cn: 水文过程线画的是河流的涨落。

normal.en: Engineering hydrology supplies design floods and spillway sizes.
normal.cn: 工程水文学提供设计洪水与溢洪道尺寸。

normal.en: Ecohydrology and planetary hydrology extend the field to life and to other worlds.
normal.cn: 生态水文学与行星水文学把领域扩展到生命与其他世界。

abstract.en: Picture a river drawn as a loop that returns to the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河被画成一个回到天空的闭环。

abstract.en: Picture rain that arrives today but reaches the river next week.
abstract.cn: 想象今天落下的雨，下周才到达河流。

abstract.en: Picture a gauge on a bank as the pulse of a whole catchment.
abstract.cn: 想象岸边一根水尺，是整个流域的脉搏。

examples.en: Hydrology links rainfall to the water that finally reaches the tap.
examples.cn: 水文学把降雨与最终到达水龙头的水联系起来。

examples.en: The hydrology of the mountain catchment is changing with less snow.
examples.cn: 随着积雪减少，山地流域的水文情势正在改变。

examples.en: Hydrology and economics must be planned together in dry regions.
examples.cn: 在干旱地区，水文学与经济学必须一起规划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「hydro（水）+ -logy（学科）」——研究水的学问 → 水文学

root: 希腊 hydōr「水」（更深来源不确定，*wed- 为重构）+ -logia「研究、论述」← logos「言词、理性」/ legein「聚集、言说」→ hydrology。英语十八世纪起有记录。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one water science: the discipline, the cycle, a regional regime, its processes, resource assessment, engineering, ecology and other planets.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一门水科学展开：学科、循环、区域情势、过程、资源评估、工程、生态与其他行星。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river drawn as a closed loop from mountain rain through runoff and evaporation back to cloud.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条河被画成闭环，从山地降雨经径流与蒸发回到云。

branches.en: CYCLE TO PROCESS: the loop is studied by separating infiltration, runoff and evaporation.
branches.cn: 从循环到过程：把闭环拆成下渗、径流与蒸发来研究。

branches.en: REGIME TO SUPPLY: a place's measured pattern becomes its safe yield.
branches.cn: 从情势到供水：某地实测的格局变成安全开采量。

branches.en: ENGINEERING: estimates of extremes become spillway widths and drainage capacity.
branches.cn: 工程水文：极值估计变成溢洪道宽度与排水能力。

branches.en: THE WETLAND: the same water shapes the plants and animals of wetlands.
branches.cn: 生态水文学：同一股水塑造湿地的动植物。

branches.en: EARTH TO WORLDS: the methods travel to channels and aquifers on other planets.
branches.cn: 从地球到其他世界：方法可迁移到其他行星的河道与含水层。

intro.en: Hydrology is a Greek compound of a water root and a study suffix, and the same root builds a large family of English technical words.
intro.cn: hydrology 是希腊语复合词，由水词根与研究后缀构成，同一词根还构成一大族英语技术词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek rather than Latin, but the Greek root reached scientific Latin as hydro- and then entered English; hydrologic forms often pass through Latinized spellings.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属希腊语而非拉丁语，但希腊词根以 hydro- 进入科学拉丁，再进入英语；水文形容词常经拉丁化拼写。

items.exampleCN: hydōr 是 hydro- 背后的词根。

items.exampleCN: hydro- 开启 hydrosphere 一类词。

items.example: Biology and geology use the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: 生物学与地质学使用同一后缀。

items.example: Hydrology measures the whole cycle.
Hydrological models predict the flood peak.
The hydrologic cycle is the same idea.
The hydrologist read the gauge.

items.meaning: a plotted record of water level or flow
items.meaningCN: 水位或流量的绘制记录
items.example: The hydrograph shows the storm peak.
The hydrosphere links ocean, ice and cloud.
items.exampleCN: 水圈把海洋、冰与云联系起来。

items.example: Hydrogeology maps the aquifer.
items.exampleCN: 水文地质学绘制含水层。

definition_zh: 晒太阳取暖；悠然享受
definition_en: to lie in pleasant warmth; to enjoy attention or pleasure
core_image: 石头上摊开四肢的蜥蜴，晒得懒洋洋
scene: 清晨海滩上，海豹群摊在沙上取暖。 Seals bask in the morning sun.
sceneCN: 这里 bask 指「晒太阳取暖」（第 1 个义项：在暖光中舒展）；句意：海豹在晨光中晒太阳。

derivatives.zh: 姥鲨（常于水面晒日的鲨鱼）

senses.title: To lie in pleasant warmth
senses.definition: to lie or relax in pleasant heat, especially sunshine
senses.definitionCN: 躺卧于宜人的温暖之中，尤指日光
senses.example: Cats bask on the windowsill.
senses.exampleCN: 猫在窗台上晒太阳。
senses.why: Old Norse baðask meant to bathe oneself; warmth is the bath.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语 baðask 意为「给自己沐浴」；温暖即浴。

senses.title: To enjoy favorable attention
senses.definition: to take pleasure in admiration or approval
senses.definitionCN: 从赞美或嘉许中获得愉悦
senses.example: She basked in the applause.
senses.exampleCN: 她沉浸在掌声中。
senses.why: Applause becomes sunshine for the soul.
senses.whyCN: 掌声成了心灵的阳光。

senses.title: To luxuriate in comfort
senses.definition: to delight in ease or plenty
senses.definitionCN: 安乐于闲适或富足
senses.example: He basked in early retirement.
senses.exampleCN: 他早早退休，安享清福。
senses.why: Comfort is a warmth one can lie in.
senses.whyCN: 舒适如暖，可以躺卧其中。

senses.title: Basking shark
senses.definition: of the shark that appears to sun itself at the surface
senses.definitionCN: 指常浮于水面似在晒日的鲨鱼
senses.example: Basking sharks filter plankton as they cruise.
senses.exampleCN: 姥鲨巡游时滤食浮游生物。
senses.why: Sailors saw it basking and named it so.
senses.whyCN: 水手见其晒日，遂以名之。

senses.title: To warm oneself by fire
senses.definition: to warm oneself beside a heat source
senses.definitionCN: 在热源旁取暖
senses.example: The old dog basked by the stove.
senses.exampleCN: 老狗偎在炉边取暖。
senses.why: Fire is the bath of the north country.
senses.whyCN: 炉火是北方人家的浴场。

senses.title: To be exposed to favor
senses.definition: to be bathed in someone's favor or kindness
senses.definitionCN: 沐浴于他人的恩惠或善意
senses.example: New employees basked in her encouragement.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工沐浴在她的鼓励里。
senses.why: Favor, like sun, falls on whoever lies open to it.
senses.whyCN: 恩宠如日，照向坦然仰卧之人。

senses.title: Historical bathing sense
senses.definition: in older English, to bathe or steep oneself
senses.definitionCN: 古英语中指沐浴、浸洗
senses.example: Early texts speak of basking in a warm bath.
senses.exampleCN: 早期文献有「入暖浴」之说。
senses.why: The bathing meaning is the root sense.
senses.whyCN: 沐浴正是词根本义。

senses.title: Figurative warmth of place
senses.definition: to lie in a sheltered, sunny spot
senses.definitionCN: 处于向阳背风的温暖之地
senses.example: The village basks on the south slope.
senses.exampleCN: 村庄偎在向阳的南坡上。
senses.why: Places as well as creatures may bask.
senses.whyCN: 受光的不仅是生物，也有地方。

intro.en: Bask comes from Old Norse baðask, to bathe oneself, formed from bath plus a reflexive ending; the sense slid from bathing in water to bathing in warmth and then in praise.
intro.cn: bask 出自古诺斯语 baðask「为自己沐浴」，由 bath 加反身词尾构成；词义由水中沐浴滑向暖中沐浴，再滑向赞誉中沐浴。

items.en: The bath root named washing in any liquid.
items.cn: 词根 bath 泛指以任何液体洗身。

items.en: baðask joined bath with the middle-voice ending -sk.
items.cn: baðask 由 bath 加中动词尾 -sk 构成。

items.en: Norse settlers' speech gave northern English baske, to wallow or bathe.
items.cn: 诺斯移民的语言给北英格兰带来 baske「沐浴、翻滚」。

items.en: Shakespeare's era widened it to basking in favor and glory.
items.cn: 莎士比亚时代扩为「沐恩」「沐荣」。

items.en: The sunbathe sense now dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 如今「晒太阳」义主导日常。

note.en: Group one holds the bathing family and look-alikes; group two holds the enjoyment field.
note.cn: 第一组收「沐浴」词族与形近词；第二组收「享受」义场。

entries.definition: the washing word that bask grew from.
entries.definitionCN: 沐浴；bask 之源词。

entries.definition: a woven container; no kin to bask.
entries.definitionCN: 篮子；与 bask 词源无关。

entries.definition: to question; Old English ascian, unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 询问；出古英语 ascian，无关。

entries.definition: to lie in the sun deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 特意进行日光浴。

entries.definition: to roll about in, as in mud or luxury.
entries.definitionCN: 打滚；沉溺。

entries.definition: to tremble with cold.
entries.definitionCN: 颤抖；寒冷时发抖，反义对照。

normalIntro.en: bask is bath with a Norse ending: to give yourself a bath of sunshine.
normalIntro.cn: bask 即 bath 加诺斯词尾：给自己洗一场阳光浴。

normal.en: Root: Old Norse baðask, bathe oneself.
normal.cn: 词根：古诺斯语 baðask「自浴」。

normal.en: Kin: bath.
normal.cn: 同族：bath。

normal.en: Basking shark: the sun-lover of the sea.
normal.cn: 姥鲨：海中的爱晒者。

normal.en: Phrase: bask in the limelight.
normal.cn: 短语：bask in the limelight。

normal.en: Rule: lie still to bask.
normal.cn: 要诀：bask 须静卧。

abstract.en: Feel sun crawl up your back like warm water.
abstract.cn: 感阳光如温水漫过背脊。

abstract.en: Bask is comfort with permission to do nothing.
abstract.cn: bask 是被允许什么都不做的舒适。

abstract.en: Applause has temperature too.
abstract.cn: 掌声也有温度。

examples.en: Lizards basked on the warm rocks.
examples.cn: 蜥蜴在暖石上晒太阳。

examples.en: The team basked in its sudden fame.
examples.cn: 球队沉浸在突如其来的名声中。

examples.en: Basking sharks drifted off the Cornish coast.
examples.cn: 姥鲨在康沃尔海岸外缓缓游弋。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「巴斯克」——巴斯克人爱在暖阳下打盹

root: 出自古诺斯语 baðask「为自己沐浴」（bath「浴」+ 反身词尾 -sk），由北英格兰方言进入英语；词义由水浴转为暖浴，再转为沐浴赞誉。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses steep in one warmth: sun, praise, comfort, the shark's name, the fireside, favor, the old bath sense, and the sunny slope.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项浸于同一温暖：日光、赞誉、闲适、鲨名、炉火、恩宠、古义沐浴与向阳山坡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lying open to warmth, letting it soak in.
core.cn: 核心意象：摊开自己，让温暖渗入。

branches.en: Sun and fire are the literal baths.
branches.cn: 日光与炉火是字面上的浴。

branches.en: The old water sense is the root.
branches.cn: 古义水浴是词根。

branches.en: Praise and favor are sunlight for the heart.

definition_zh: 下定决心的；意志坚定的；由某因素所决定的；已确定下来的
definition_en: having firmly decided to do something and unlikely to change one's mind
core_image: 一个人在地图上把终点圈住，把其他岔路一条条划掉，只留一条线
scene: 报名前一天，她划掉了所有备选方案，只在申请书第一行写下目标学校。 She was determined to apply to only one school and to accept no fallback.
sceneCN: 这里 determined 指「已经下定决心、不再更改」（第 1 个义项：决定已作出且不动摇）；句意为她决心只申请一所学校，不接受任何备用选择。图中可辨识物件：被划掉的分支路线、圈住的终点、只写一行的申请书。

pos.zh: 下定决心的；意志坚定的；确定的
determine 的过去式与过去分词：决定；确定；查明

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示行为与结果的名词后缀构成，语义由「定下界限」转为「定下决心的行为与那股劲」
基础动词，来自拉丁语「划定界限」，语义为「确定、决定、查明」
在动词词干后加表示学说的名词后缀构成，语义由「被决定」转为「一切皆由前因决定的主张」
加表示「起作用之物」的后缀构成，语义由「确定」转为「起决定作用的因素」
加否定前缀与形容词后缀构成，语义由「已划定」转为「界限不明、无法确定」
加表示「在前」的前缀构成，语义由「已决定」转为「事先就已定好」

senses.title: Having made a firm decision
senses.titleCN: 已经下定决心，不肯更改
senses.definition: having decided firmly what one will do and refusing to be talked out of it
senses.definitionCN: 已经坚定地决定要做什么，别人劝也劝不动
senses.example: She was determined to apply to only one school and to accept no fallback.
senses.exampleCN: 她决心只申请一所学校，不接受任何备用选择。
senses.why: determine comes from de- plus terminare 'to set a boundary', so being determined is having one's choice fenced in and closed to other options.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自拉丁语「划定界限」，因此「下定决心」就是把选择围起来，对别的选项关上口子。

senses.title: Resolute by temperament
senses.definition: having a character that does not easily give way to doubt, fatigue or discouragement
senses.definitionCN: 性格上不容易被怀疑、疲惫或气馁所动摇
senses.example: A determined captain kept the crew working through the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 一位意志坚定的船长让船员在风暴中继续工作。
senses.why: when this quality belongs to the person rather than to one decision, the adjective describes temperament, not a single act.
senses.whyCN: 当这份品质属于整个人而非某一个决定时，这个形容词描述的是性情，而不是一次行动。

senses.title: Fixed in advance
senses.definition: settled beforehand, so that no further choice or change is possible
senses.definitionCN: 事先已经定好，因此不再有选择或更改的余地
senses.example: The starting date is determined and cannot be moved.
senses.exampleCN: 开始日期已经确定，不能更改。
senses.why: the boundary image is literal here: a line drawn once, with nothing left to redraw.
senses.whyCN: 这里「界限」的意象是字面用法：线已经画好一次，没有可重画的地方。

senses.title: Caused by a factor
senses.definition: decided or produced by a particular cause rather than chosen freely
senses.definitionCN: 由特定原因所决定或产生，而不是自由选择的
senses.example: Crop yields are largely determined by rainfall in this region.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一地区，作物产量在很大程度上由降雨决定。
senses.why: the passive construction marks the boundary as drawn from outside: something else fixes where the outcome falls.
senses.whyCN: 被动结构标出这条界限是由外部画上的：是别的因素定住了结果落在何处。

senses.title: Firm and forceful in execution
senses.definition: done with visible firmness and energy, so that the effort itself is unmistakable
senses.definitionCN: 以看得见的坚定与力度完成，使努力本身一望即知
senses.example: They made a determined effort to finish before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 他们下了决心，要在截止前完成。
senses.why: a decision that has closed off alternatives shows up in how the work is done, and the adjective then describes the effort.
senses.whyCN: 一个已经排除其他可能的决定，会显现在做事的方式上，这个形容词于是用来描述努力本身。

senses.title: Aimed at one definite goal
senses.definition: directed at a single stated aim instead of scattered or exploratory movement
senses.definitionCN: 直指一个明确说出的目标，而非散乱或试探性的移动
senses.example: It was a determined attempt to settle the question once and for all.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一次要一劳永逸解决这个问题的决意尝试。
senses.why: one boundary means one target, which is why the adjective often appears before attempt and effort.
senses.whyCN: 一条界限只对应一个目标，因此这个形容词常出现在「尝试」「努力」这类词之前。

senses.title: Unmoved from a stated position
senses.definition: holding to a public position when pressure, ridicule or loss is applied against it
senses.definitionCN: 在压力、嘲笑或损失袭来时，仍守住公开表明的立场
senses.example: The mayor remained determined despite the hostile press.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管媒体充满敌意，市长仍不动摇。
senses.why: the strength is now social: the boundary is defended against other people pushing on it.
senses.whyCN: 这时的力量是社会性的：这条界限是在别人推挤之下守住。

senses.title: Stubborn past the point of reason
senses.definition: holding on so hard that advice and evidence no longer get a hearing
senses.definitionCN: 抓得太紧，以至于劝告与证据都进不来
senses.example: He was determined to prove the critics wrong, even at ruinous cost.
senses.exampleCN: 他执意要证明批评者是错的，哪怕代价极其惨重。
senses.why: the same closed boundary turns into a vice when nothing at all can cross it, and the word acquires a shade of obstinacy.
senses.whyCN: 同一条封闭的界线，如果什么都进不来，就会变成缺陷，于是这个词带上了固执的色彩。

intro.en: Determined is the past participle of determine, which comes from Latin determinare 'to limit, to fix the end of', built on de- 'completely' and terminare 'to set a boundary', from terminus 'boundary, end'. The origin of terminus itself is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: determined 是 determine 的过去分词，后者来自拉丁语 determinare「限定、定下终点」，由 de-「完全」与 terminare「划定界限」构成，后者又出自动词 terminus「边界、终点」。terminus 本身的来源没有定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Terminus meant 'boundary stone, end, limit'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the connection sometimes drawn to a root meaning 'to cross over' is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: terminus 意为「界石、终点、界限」。其更深来源不确定；有人把它与表示「越过」的词根相联系，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Terminare 'to set a boundary, to bring to an end' turned the stone into an action: you draw the line and the matter stops there.
items.cn: terminare「划定界限、使结束」把这块界石变成了动作：把线一画，事情就停在那里。

items.en: De- 'completely' plus terminare gave determinare 'to limit fully, to settle, to fix', the source of both the English verb and the adjective.
items.cn: de-「完全」加 terminare 构成 determinare「完全限定、定下、确定」，是英语动词与形容词的共同来源。

items.en: Old French determiner passed the verb into Middle English, where it first meant to decide a question or to bring something to an end.
items.cn: 古法语 determiner 把这个动词带入中古英语，最初指裁决一个问题或把某事推向结束。

items.en: The past participle became an adjective in its own right, so that a determined person is one whose choice has already been closed off.
items.cn: 这个过去分词独立成为形容词，因此「一个下定决心的人」就是一个选择已经被关上的人。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin of terminus): no exact date can be given for the adjective's first use, and any Indo-European form proposed for terminus is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（terminus 的来源）：这个形容词最早使用的确切年代无从给出；凡为 terminus 提出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates words that look close to determined but rest on a different root; group two separates adjectives of resolve by what they stress.
note.cn: 第一组区分形近而词根不同的词；第二组按侧重区分表示「坚决」的形容词。

entries.definition: A factor that fixes an outcome; same Latin base, but it names the cause rather than the resolve.
entries.definitionCN: 决定结果的因素；拉丁词干相同，但它指那个原因，而不是那股决心。

entries.definition: To bring something to an end, built directly on terminare without the de- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事结束，直接由 terminare 构成，不带 de- 前缀。

entries.definition: Relating to an end or a boundary, as in terminal station; it keeps the stone image but loses the sense of resolve.
entries.definitionCN: 与终点或界限有关，如终点站；保留了界石的意象，但没有「决心」之义。

entries.definition: The doctrine that every event is fixed by prior causes; the boundary is drawn by the past, not by a person.
entries.definitionCN: 主张一切事件皆由此前原因所决定；界限由过去画出，而不是由人画出。

entries.definition: Ex- 'out' plus terminare 'boundary': to drive something past the boundary, hence to destroy it completely.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ex-「出」加 terminare「界限」构成：把某物赶出界限之外，因而指彻底消灭。

entries.definition: Firm in purpose, with the sense of having solved or settled the question; slightly more formal than determined.
entries.definitionCN: 目标坚定，带「问题已解决、已定下」的意味；比 determined 略正式。

entries.definition: Refusing to change even when change is reasonable; it keeps only the vice of determination.
entries.definitionCN: 即便改变是合理的也不肯改；只保留了「决心」变成缺陷的那一面。

entries.definition: Bound by a pledge to a person, cause or course; the emphasis is on obligation and loyalty.
entries.definitionCN: 因承诺而绑定于某人、某项事业或某条道路；重点在义务与忠诚。

entries.definition: Able to settle a matter quickly and firmly; it describes the speed and finality of the choice.
entries.definitionCN: 能迅速而坚定地定下事情；描述的是选择的速度与终局性。

entries.definition: Firmly fixed and not wavering over time; it stresses continuity more than a single decision.
entries.definitionCN: 牢牢固定、经时不摇；比单次决定更强调时间上的连续性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin de- 'completely' plus terminus 'boundary': a decision that fences the matter in on all sides.
normal.cn: 拉丁 de-「完全」加 terminus「界限」：把这件事四面围起来的决定。

normal.en: The family runs determine, determined, determination, determinant, determinism, indeterminate.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖动词、形容词、名词、因素名词、学说名词与否定形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the resolve: be determined to do, a determined effort, a determined attempt.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这股决心：决心去做、坚决的努力、决意的尝试。

normal.en: The passive phrase determined by shifts the boundary outside the person, so it means caused, not resolute.
normal.cn: 被动说法「由……所决定」把界限移到人之外，因此意思是「由……造成」，而非「坚决」。

normal.en: The same stone appears in terminal and terminate, where an end is reached rather than a will held.
normal.cn: 同一块界石还出现在 terminal 与 terminate 里，那里是走到终点，而不是守住意志。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil line drawn around one square on a map while every other square stays blank.
abstract.cn: 想象在地图上用一个方框圈住一格，其余格子全部留白。

abstract.en: Picture a door with the key turned once and then removed from the lock.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，钥匙转过一次后被从锁里拔走。

abstract.en: Picture a compass needle that has stopped trembling and now points one way only.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚罗盘指针不再抖动，只朝一个方向。

examples.en: The engineers were determined to find the leak before the rainy season.
examples.cn: 工程师决心在雨季之前找到漏点。

examples.en: She gave a determined answer that ended the argument.
examples.cn: 她给出了一个坚决的答复，结束了争论。

examples.en: Water loss is determined by soil type and by wind speed.
examples.cn: 水分损失由土壤类型与风速决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（彻底）+ term（期限/界限）——把期限彻底定死 → 下定决心、确定

root: 拉丁 determinare「限定、定下终点」= de-（完全）+ terminare「划定界限」；terminus「界石、终点」更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: a line is drawn around a choice, and then the line is applied to a person's character, a fixed date, an external cause, a style of work, a single aim, a defended stand and finally to obstinacy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：先在一个选择周围画一条线，再把这条线依次用于人的性情、已定的日期、外部原因、做事风格、单一目标、被捍卫的立场，最后用于固执。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn once around one choice, with every other option left outside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：在一个选择周围画一次线，别的选项都被留在线外。

branches.en: WHO DRAWS THE LINE: a person, a calendar or an outside cause can all be the hand holding the pencil.
branches.cn: 谁来画线：人、日历或外部原因都可以是握笔的那只手。

branches.en: THE CLOSED CHOICE: a single decision hardens into a lasting trait of character.
branches.cn: 被关上的选择：一次决定硬化成长久的人格特征。

branches.en: THE LINE SHOWS IN THE WORK: one aim and a forceful manner are what a closed choice looks like from outside.
branches.cn: 线显现在活里：单一目标与有力的做法，就是「选择已关上」从外面看到的样子。

branches.en: THE DEFENDED LINE: other people push, and the boundary is held anyway.
branches.cn: 被守住的线：别人来推，界线仍然守住。

branches.en: THE LINE THAT BECOMES A WALL: when nothing can cross, firmness turns into a fault.
branches.cn: 变成墙的线：什么都不能通过时，坚定就转成了缺陷。

intro.en: Determined is a Latin participle whose prefix and stem also appear across a wide English family, so the whole group can be read by parts.
intro.cn: determined 是一个拉丁分词，它的前缀与词干还出现在一大串英语词里，因此整组词可以按部件读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin terminus gives terminal, terminate, termination and exterminate; de- 'completely' also appears in declare and demolish, where it marks thoroughness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 terminus 衍生出 terminal、terminate、termination 与 exterminate；de-「完全」也见于 declare 与 demolish，表示彻底。

items.example: Tests determine the cause of the fault.

definition_en: belonging to an earlier time; as a noun, a thing of the past

scene: 阁楼里，老人翻着一本落灰的相册。 She smiled at the fashions of bygone days.
sceneCN: 这里 bygone 是「过去的、往昔的」（第 1 个义项：属于早年时光的）；句意是看到往日时装，她笑了。

pos.zh: 过去的；往昔的；早已过时的

senses.definition: of or relating to a time that has already gone by
senses.definitionCN: 属于已逝去的时光的

senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆重现了往昔的手艺。

senses.whyCN: 复合词由 by 加 gone 构成，意为「已经过去」。

senses.title: A thing of the past (noun)
senses.definition: an event or grievance that belongs to the past and should be forgotten
senses.definitionCN: 属于过去、应当翻篇的事件或嫌隙
senses.example: Let us agree that old quarrels are bygones.
senses.exampleCN: 让我们约定，旧日争执就此翻篇。
senses.why: The adjective stands as a noun for what has gone by.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转指「已过去之物」，成为名词。

senses.title: No longer practised or existing
senses.definition: no longer in use, custom or existence
senses.definitionCN: 不再使用、不再流行或已不复存在的
senses.example: Horse-drawn trams are a bygone mode of city travel.
senses.exampleCN: 马拉街车是早已消失的城市交通方式。
senses.why: What has gone by has also gone away.
senses.whyCN: 「已经过去」自然引申为「已经消失」。

intro.en: Bygone is a plain compound of by and the participle gone, formed in the fifteenth century.
intro.cn: bygone 是由 by 加过去分词 gone 构成的简单复合词，形成于十五世纪。

items.en: by meant past or near, and gone was the participle of go.
items.cn: 中古英语中 by 表示「过去、在旁」，gone 为 go 的过去分词。

items.en: the compound bygone first meant something that has gone by.
items.cn: 十五世纪复合词 bygone 初义为「已过去的事物」。

items.en: Scots law spoke of bygane duties, obligations already past due.
items.cn: 苏格兰法律用语 bygane 指「已到期的」义务。

items.en: the proverb let bygones be bygones fixed the noun use.
items.cn: 十九世纪谚语 let bygones be bygones 使名词义定型。

items.en: bygone now colours any nostalgic reference to earlier times.
items.cn: 如今 bygone 专用于怀旧的语境。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the by- prefix; the near-meaning group lists other words for the past.
note.cn: 形近组共用 by- 前缀；近义组是其他表「过去」的词。

entries.definitionCN: 旁观者，同用 by- 前缀

entries.definition: occurring earlier in time

entries.definition: belonging to ancient or old times
entries.definitionCN: 古旧的；古董的

entries.definition: no longer in use
entries.definitionCN: 废弃不用的

normalIntro.en: The word explains itself: by, gone, already past.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词自释其义：by 加 gone，已成过往。

normal.en: Bygone days means days gone by.
normal.cn: bygone days 即「已逝去的日子」。

normal.en: Let bygones be bygones is the famous idiom.
normal.cn: let bygones be bygones 是著名习语，意为既往不咎。

normal.en: By- here means past, as in bypass.
normal.cn: 这里 by- 表示「过去」，如 bypass。

normal.en: As a noun it takes plural bygones.
normal.cn: 作名词时用复数 bygones。

normal.en: Bygone has a nostalgic tone.
normal.cn: bygone 带有怀旧色彩。

abstract.en: Hear a clock tick a photo album shut.
abstract.cn: 听时钟滴答，一本相册随之合上。

abstract.en: See old letters tied with faded ribbon.
abstract.cn: 看旧信件用褪色的丝带捆好。

definition_zh: 附属物；附加成分；兼职的；辅助的
definition_en: something added to a main thing but not essential to it, or a person or post that supports a main body
core_image: 主干旁边挂着一根细枝，能帮上忙但不是主干
scene: 语言课上，老师把句子主干写在黑板中央，又把时间状语写在旁边的小框里。 The teacher marked the time phrase as an adjunct to the main clause.
sceneCN: 这里 adjunct 是「附加成分」（第 2 个义项：语法中可以省略的附加成分）；句意为老师把时间短语标为主句的附加成分。

pos.zh: 名词：附属物；附加成分；助手
形容词：附属的；兼职的；辅助的

derivatives.zh: 由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「附加的；辅助的」
由 adjunctive 加副词后缀构成，义为「作为附加地」
由动词词根加名词后缀构成，义为「附加；添加」

senses.title: Something added but not essential
senses.definition: a thing added to help a main thing but not needed for it to exist
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助主体而添加、但主体缺它也能存在的东西
senses.example: The appendix serves as an adjunct to the main report.
senses.exampleCN: 附录是主报告的附属部分。
senses.why: adjungere is 'to join to', and an adjunct is joined to a main body without becoming its core.
senses.whyCN: adjungere 意为「接上去」，adjunct 被接到主体上，却不会变成主体的核心。

senses.title: An optional grammatical element
senses.definition: a sentence element that adds information but can be removed without breaking the grammar
senses.definitionCN: 为主要结构补充信息、去掉后语法仍成立的句子成分
senses.example: The teacher marked the time phrase as an adjunct to the main clause.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把时间短语标为主句的附加成分。
senses.why: Grammar separates the core clause from what is merely joined on to it.
senses.whyCN: 语法把核心小句与仅仅接上去的成分区分开来。

senses.title: A junior academic post
senses.definition: a teaching or research post attached to a department on a part-time or temporary basis
senses.definitionCN: 以兼职或临时方式挂靠在某个院系的教学或研究职位
senses.example: She taught as an adjunct at the university for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这所大学做了两年兼职教师。
senses.why: The post is attached to the department without being part of its permanent core.
senses.whyCN: 这个职位挂在院系上，却不属于其永久核心。

senses.title: A non-essential property in philosophy
senses.definition: a property that a thing may have or lose without ceasing to be what it is
senses.definitionCN: 某物可以拥有或失去、却不因此改变其本质的属性
senses.example: Colour is treated as an adjunct of the object, not its essence.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色被视为物体的偶性，而非其本质。
senses.why: Philosophy uses the joined-on image for qualities that come and go.
senses.whyCN: 哲学用「接上去」的意象，指那些来来去去的性质。

senses.title: A supporting medical treatment
senses.definition: a treatment added to the main therapy to improve its effect
senses.definitionCN: 加在主要疗法之上以增强疗效的治疗
senses.example: The drug is used as an adjunct to surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药被用作手术的辅助治疗。
senses.why: The main therapy carries the cure, and the adjunct is joined on to help it work better.
senses.whyCN: 主要疗法承担治愈，辅助治疗接上去帮它更好地发挥作用。

senses.title: A person who assists
senses.definition: in older usage, a person who helps another in a task
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，指在任务中帮助另一个人的助手
senses.example: The clerk worked as an adjunct to the chief magistrate.
senses.exampleCN: 这名书记员担任首席治安官的助手。
senses.why: A helper is joined to the main office-holder in the same way as a small part to a body.
senses.whyCN: 助手像一个小部件接在主体上一样，接在主职者身边。

senses.title: An attached condition
senses.definition: a condition or qualification attached to an agreement or a statement
senses.definitionCN: 附加在协议或声明上的条件或限定
senses.example: The permit came with an adjunct requiring monthly reports.
senses.exampleCN: 许可证附带一项要求每月报告的条件。
senses.why: A condition is joined to the main arrangement without replacing it.
senses.whyCN: 条件被接到主要安排上，而不取代它。

senses.title: A physically attached part
senses.definition: a part fixed to a larger structure to extend its function
senses.definitionCN: 固定在较大结构上、用以扩展其功能的部件
senses.example: The pump is an adjunct to the main irrigation line.
senses.exampleCN: 这台泵是主灌溉管线的附属部件。
senses.why: The most literal sense is a piece joined on to a larger machine or building.
senses.whyCN: 最字面的义项就是接在较大机器或建筑上的部件。

intro.en: Adjunct comes from the Latin verb for joining one thing to another, the same root as junction.
intro.cn: adjunct 来自表示「把一物接到另一物」的拉丁语动词，与 junction 同根。

items.en: jungere meant 'to join, yoke', the source of junction, join and junta.
items.cn: jungere 意为「连接、套上轭」，是 junction、join 与 junta 的来源。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus jungere formed adjungere, 'to join to, attach'.
items.cn: ad- 表示「向」，与 jungere 构成 adjungere，意为「接上、附加」。

items.en: The participle adjunctus meant 'joined to', and it became the English noun.
items.cn: 分词 adjunctus 意为「被接上的」，后来成为英语名词。

items.en: The noun adjunctio named the act of adding something on.
items.cn: 名词 adjunctio 指把某物附加上去的行为。

items.en: English adjunct is recorded in the fifteenth century; the grammatical and academic senses develop later, with exact dates uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 adjunct 在十五世纪已有记录；语法义与学术义后来才发展，确切年代不确定。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from grammar and medicine to part-time academic posts and attached parts.
items.cn: 现代用法从语法、医学延伸到兼职学术职位与附属部件。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the jungere family and two different-root neighbours; the near-meaning group gathers additions and supports.
note.cn: 形近组收 jungere 词族与两个不同词根的近邻；近义组收附加物与辅助物。

entries.definition: The act of adding one thing to another.

entries.definition: A place where roads, wires, or parts meet; the same joining root without the prefix.

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「相邻的」；拼写相近，但来自表示「躺在旁边」的动词，而非「连接」动词。

entries.definition: A person dependent on a substance or activity; the spelling is misleading and the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成瘾者」；拼写容易误导，词根不同。

entries.definition: Something put with something else to increase it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「增加物」，与别物放在一起以增加其内容。

entries.definition: Something added to complete or improve a main thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补充物」，为完善或改善主体而添加的东西。

entries.definition: A person or thing that gives secondary help.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「辅助者、辅助的」，提供次要帮助的人或物。

entries.definition: An extra item that adds to the usefulness or appearance of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「配件、附件」，增加实用性或外观的额外物品。

entries.definition: A section added at the end of a book or document.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附录」，加在书籍或文件末尾的部分。

definition_zh: 贸易协定；贸易协议；两国或多国就贸易条件达成的正式约定
definition_en: a formal arrangement between countries setting the terms on which they will trade
core_image: 一张长桌两端各坐一方代表，桌中央摊开一份文件，两枝笔同时落在签名栏上
scene: 部长级会谈结束后，双方代表在同一份文件上签字，约定削减关税并开放部分服务市场。 The two governments signed a trade agreement after three years of talks.
sceneCN: 这里指「国家间达成的贸易约定」，对应第 1 个义项：就关税、市场准入等条件形成的正式协议；句意为两国政府经过三年谈判签署了一份贸易协定。画面要点：长桌、双方代表、摊开的文件、签名栏。

pos.zh: 贸易协定；贸易协议（可数，复数 trade agreements）

derivatives.zh: 协议；同意（agree 加名词后缀，语义从「达成一致」转为「一致的结果」）
同意；达成一致（agreement 的基础动词，源自法语表示「使合意」）
令人愉快的；可接受的（agree 加形容词后缀，语义偏向合人心意）
分歧（dis- 加 agreement，指一致状态被取消）
贸易；交易（短语的前半，源自古英语与低地德语中表示「路径、往来」的词）

senses.title: A formal pact on trade terms
senses.titleCN: 就贸易条件达成的正式约定
senses.definition: a formal arrangement in which countries set the rules and terms of trade between them
senses.definitionCN: 国家之间就贸易规则与条件形成的正式安排
senses.example: The two governments signed a trade agreement after three years of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 两国政府经过三年谈判签署了一份贸易协定。
senses.why: Agreement comes from a French verb meaning to bring two minds into one pleasure, so a trade agreement is two parties brought to one will about exchange.
senses.whyCN: agreement 出自法语动词，意为使两方心意合一；因此贸易协定就是把两方在交易上的意愿合成一个。

senses.title: A bilateral agreement between two countries
senses.definition: an agreement concluded between exactly two countries
senses.definitionCN: 恰好由两个国家缔结的协定
senses.example: The bilateral trade agreement cut tariffs on farm goods.
senses.exampleCN: 这份双边贸易协定削减了农产品关税。
senses.why: Counting the parties is the simplest way to classify agreements, so bilateral names the two-party case.
senses.whyCN: 按缔约方数量分类最为简单，因此双边专指两方的情形。

senses.title: A regional or multilateral agreement
senses.definition: an agreement among several countries, often forming a bloc or a common market
senses.definitionCN: 由若干国家缔结、常形成集团或共同市场的协定
senses.example: The regional trade agreement created a single tariff schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 这份区域贸易协定形成了统一关税表。
senses.why: When more parties join, the agreement becomes a framework that governs a whole region rather than a pair.
senses.whyCN: 当更多方加入，协定就成为治理整个区域而不是一对国家的框架。

senses.title: The legal text itself
senses.definition: the written instrument containing the agreed terms
senses.definitionCN: 载有约定条款的书面文书
senses.example: The trade agreement runs to four hundred pages.
senses.exampleCN: 这份贸易协定长达四百页。
senses.why: An agreement can be both the understanding and the paper that records it, so the phrase names the document too.
senses.whyCN: 协定既可是共识，也可是记录共识的纸张，因此这个短语也指文件。

senses.title: The scope of the agreed terms
senses.definition: the subject areas covered, such as tariffs, services, rules of origin or investment
senses.definitionCN: 所覆盖的议题，如关税、服务、原产地规则或投资
senses.example: The trade agreement covers services as well as goods.
senses.exampleCN: 这份贸易协定既涵盖货物，也涵盖服务。
senses.why: Modern agreements are bundles of chapters, so the phrase often appears with covers, includes or excludes.
senses.whyCN: 现代协定是一捆章节，因此这个短语常与「涵盖」「包括」「不包括」搭配。

senses.title: A preferential agreement
senses.definition: an agreement granting lower tariffs or wider access than the general rules allow
senses.definitionCN: 给予比一般规则更低的关税或更宽的准入
senses.example: The preferential trade agreement spared small exporters the full duty.
senses.exampleCN: 这份优惠贸易协定使小出口商免缴全额关税。
senses.why: Preference is the point of most agreements: some partners get better terms than the default.
senses.whyCN: 多数协定的要点就是优惠：某些伙伴得到比默认更好的条件。

senses.title: The stage of ratification
senses.definition: the process by which the agreed text is approved and brought into force
senses.definitionCN: 使议定文本获得批准并开始生效的过程
senses.example: The trade agreement awaits ratification by both parliaments.
senses.exampleCN: 这份贸易协定有待两国议会批准。
senses.why: Signing is only a promise; the phrase also names the instrument during the period before it binds.
senses.whyCN: 签署只是承诺；这个短语也指在生效之前的那份文书。

senses.title: The framework for settling disputes
senses.titleCN: 作为争端解决框架的协定
senses.definition: the agreement viewed as the set of rules and procedures for resolving trade conflicts
senses.definitionCN: 被视为解决贸易冲突的规则与程序集合的协定
senses.example: The trade agreement provides for arbitration when talks fail.
senses.exampleCN: 这份贸易协定规定谈判失败时进行仲裁。
senses.why: A durable agreement outlives its signatories' goodwill, so it must contain a way to settle quarrels.
senses.whyCN: 一份持久的协定要超越签署方的善意，因此必须含有解决争执的办法。

intro.en: Trade agreement joins trade, a Germanic word of path and exchange, with agreement, from French agree, 'to bring to one will'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: trade agreement 把源自日耳曼语、表示「路径与往来」的 trade，与出自法语 agree「使心意合一」的 agreement 组合起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gratus meant pleasing or welcome, and it built words about favour and thankfulness.
items.cn: gratus 意为令人愉快的、受欢迎的，构成一批关于恩惠与感谢的词。

items.en: French agreer, from a phrase meaning 'at pleasure', came to mean to consent or to suit.
items.cn: 法语 agreer 出自表示「随其所愿」的说法，后来意为同意或相合。

items.en: English agree appeared in the fourteenth century with the sense of coming to one mind.
items.cn: 英语 agree 在 14 世纪出现，意为达成一致。

items.en: The noun agreement named both the state of consent and the document recording it.
items.cn: 名词 agreement 既指同意的状态，也指记录同意的文件。

items.en: As states began to negotiate tariffs systematically, trade agreement became the standard name for the resulting instrument.
items.cn: 随着各国开始系统性地谈判关税，trade agreement 成为这类文书的标准名称。

note.en: The first group shares the pleasing root but has moved into other senses; the second group names other written understandings between states.
note.cn: 第一组共享「合意」词根但语义已转移；第二组是国家间其他形式的书面约定。

entries.definition: Any state of consent or any contract; a trade agreement is the specific case about commerce.
entries.definitionCN: 任何同意状态或任何契约；贸易协定是关于商业的具体情形。

entries.definition: To come to one mind; the noun adds the result and, in this phrase, the trade subject matter.
entries.definitionCN: 达成一致；名词加上结果，在这个短语中再加上贸易主题。

entries.definition: Pleasing or acceptable; it describes a quality, not a negotiated instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的或可接受的；它描述性质，不是谈判达成的文书。

entries.definition: Favour or elegance, from Latin gratia; it shares the pleasing root but has no commercial sense.
entries.definitionCN: 恩惠或优雅，出自拉丁 gratia；共享「合意」词根，却没有商业含义。

entries.definition: A formally concluded and ratified agreement between states; a trade agreement is one kind of treaty or treaty-like instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 国家间正式缔结并批准的协定；贸易协定是条约或类条约文书的一种。

entries.definition: A formal settlement between parties; it often covers a single dispute, while a trade agreement covers continuing trade.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的正式和解；它常针对单一争端，而贸易协定覆盖持续的贸易。

entries.definition: A short word for any agreement, often used in headlines; it lacks the legal precision of a trade agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 任何协定的简短说法，常见于标题；它没有贸易协定那样的法律精度。

entries.definition: A statement of intent that may not be legally enforceable; a trade agreement is normally binding.
entries.definitionCN: 意向声明，未必具有法律约束力；贸易协定通常是约束性的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real consent root, the real trade word and real diplomatic phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「合意」词根、真实的贸易词与真实外交搭配。

normal.en: Agreement is two minds made one; adding trade says what they came to one mind about.
normal.cn: agreement 是两个心意合成一个；加上 trade 说明他们在什么上达成一致。

normal.en: The verb is agree and the noun is agreement, so the pair is transparent.
normal.cn: 动词是 agree，名词是 agreement，两者关系清楚。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the uses: sign a trade agreement, negotiate a trade agreement, a bilateral trade agreement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示用法：签署贸易协定、谈判贸易协定、双边贸易协定。

normal.en: Classify by parties: bilateral for two, regional or multilateral for several.
normal.cn: 按缔约方分类：两国为双边，多国为区域或多边。

normal.en: Signing is not the end: ratification brings the text into force.
normal.cn: 签字不是终点：批准才使文本生效。

abstract.en: Picture two hands reaching across a table to sign the same sheet at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手越过桌面，在同一刻签下同一张纸。

abstract.en: Picture two markets joined by a bridge whose planks are numbered clauses.
abstract.cn: 想象两个市场被一座桥连起，桥板就是一条条编号的条款。

abstract.en: Picture a rulebook kept on the table even after the signatories stop liking each other.
abstract.cn: 想象一本规则书一直放在桌上，即使签字方后来互不友好。

examples.en: The two countries are negotiating a trade agreement on services.
examples.cn: 两国正在就服务贸易谈判一份贸易协定。

examples.en: The trade agreement lowered tariffs on machinery.
examples.cn: 这份贸易协定降低了机械关税。

examples.en: Farm groups opposed the trade agreement's import rules.
examples.cn: 农业团体反对这份贸易协定的进口规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「把贸易条件谈成一致」——agree 是达成一致，加 trade 就是关于贸易的一致约定 → 贸易协定

root: trade 源自古英语与中古低地德语中表示「路径、往来」的词；agreement 出自法语 agreer「使合意」，源自拉丁 gratus「令人愉快的」。合指就贸易条件达成的正式约定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one instrument: the pact itself, its two-party and multi-party forms, the document, its scope, its preferential terms, its ratification and its dispute rules.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一份文书展开：约定本身、双边与多边形式、文件、覆盖范围、优惠条款、批准程序，以及争端规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two delegations signing one sheet at the same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个代表团在同一刻签下同一张纸。

branches.en: BASE CONSENT: two parties are brought to one will about trade.
branches.cn: 基础合意：两方在贸易上被合成一个意愿。

branches.en: COUNTING PARTIES: two countries, or several forming a region.
branches.cn: 缔约方计数：两个国家，或若干国家组成区域。

branches.en: DOCUMENT AND SCOPE: the text records what the chapters cover.
branches.cn: 文件与范围：文本记录了各章覆盖的内容。

branches.en: TERMS AND VALIDITY: preferences are granted, then ratification makes them bind.
branches.cn: 条款与效力：先给优惠，再经批准使其生效。

branches.en: DURABLE RULES: the agreement must outlast goodwill and settle quarrels.
branches.cn: 持久规则：协定必须超越善意，并能解决争执。

intro.en: Trade agreement is a phrase of two free words, one Germanic and one built on a Latin root of favour.
intro.cn: trade agreement 由两个自由词构成，一个源自日耳曼语，一个建立在拉丁「合意」词根上。

latinIntro.en: Latin gratus 'pleasing' gives grace, grateful, gratify and, through French, agree and agreement; trade gives trading, trader and trademark.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gratus「令人愉快的」衍生 grace、grateful、gratify，并经由法语衍生 agree 与 agreement；trade 衍生 trading、trader 与 trademark。

items.example: The root builds words of favour.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根构成一批表示恩惠的词。

They reached an agreement.

items.exampleCN: 配额上的分歧拖延了谈判。

items.exampleCN: 该条款被保留为宽限期。

items.exampleCN: 他们之间的贸易翻了一番。

items.example: Trading resumed after the vote.
They signed a border treaty.
A trade agreement was signed.

definition_zh: 预测；预言；预报
definition_en: a statement about what will happen in the future, especially one based on evidence, a model or reasoning
core_image: 一个人站在河边，手里拿着一张写着明天水位高度的纸条，纸条边缘还标着刻度
scene: 这里指「预测」。 The model's prediction was wrong by only two centimetres.
sceneCN: 这里 prediction 是「预测结果、预报」（第 1 个义项：关于未来的陈述）；句意：这个模型的预测只差了两厘米。图中可辨识物件：写有水位的纸条、刻度线、河岸与水位标尺。

senses.title: A statement about the future
senses.titleCN: 预测：对将发生之事的说法
senses.definition: a statement that something will happen, made before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 在某事发生之前说明它将会发生的陈述
senses.example: Her prediction that the bridge would fail proved right.
senses.exampleCN: 她关于这座桥会垮塌的预测被证明是对的。
senses.why: prae- means 'before' and dicere means 'say'. A prediction is literally something said before the event.
senses.whyCN: prae- 意为“在前”，dicere 意为“说”。prediction 字面上就是在事件之前说出的东西。

senses.title: The act of foretelling
senses.definition: the act or practice of saying what will happen, rather than the content said
senses.definitionCN: 说明将会发生什么的行为或做法，而非说出的内容本身
senses.example: Prediction is easy; being right is hard.
senses.exampleCN: 预言很容易，说准却很难。
senses.why: The -ion suffix can name an action. English keeps both readings, the act and its product, in one noun.
senses.whyCN: -ion 后缀既可命名动作。英语把“行为”与“产物”两种读法都留在同一个名词里。

senses.title: Scientific forecast
senses.titleCN: 科学预报：可检验的说法
senses.definition: a precise statement derived from a theory or model that observation can confirm or refute
senses.definitionCN: 由理论或模型推出、可被观察证实或否证的精确陈述
senses.example: A good theory yields predictions that can be tested.
senses.exampleCN: 好的理论会产生可被检验的预测。
senses.why: Science turns prophecy into a test: a prediction that cannot fail is not a scientific prediction.
senses.whyCN: 科学把预言变成检验：不可能失败的预测算不上科学预测。

senses.title: Model output
senses.titleCN: 模型输出：算出来的那个数
senses.definition: the value or outcome produced by a statistical or computational model for an unknown case
senses.definitionCN: 统计或计算模型对未知情形给出的数值或结果
senses.example: The prediction for next quarter is a small rise in demand.
senses.exampleCN: 对下季度的预测是需求小幅上升。
senses.why: Models produce numbers, and the industry borrowed the everyday word for them. The output inherits the word's forward-looking direction.
senses.whyCN: 模型产出数字，业界借用了日常词来称呼它。这个输出继承了该词“朝前看”的方向。

senses.title: Forecast of a trend
senses.definition: an estimate of a future quantity based on extending a current pattern
senses.definitionCN: 通过延长当前模式而得到的未来数量估计
senses.example: Population predictions suggest the town will shrink after 2030.
senses.exampleCN: 人口预测显示该镇在 2030 年后会萎缩。
senses.why: Extending a line is the simplest picture of prediction, and it explains why forecasters speak of trends rather than events.
senses.whyCN: 把线延长是预测最简单的画面，也解释了为什么预报者谈趋势而不谈单个事件。

senses.title: Prophecy and omen
senses.definition: in older usage, a declaration of future events attributed to inspiration or divine knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 较旧用法中指被认为来自灵感或神启的未来事件宣告
senses.example: The prediction in the old chronicle was read as a warning.
senses.exampleCN: 旧编年史中的那则预言被解读为警告。
senses.why: Before statistics, prediction belonged to prophets. The word still carries a faint trace of that authority.
senses.whyCN: 在统计学之前，预测属于先知。这个词仍带着一点那种权威的痕迹。

senses.title: Prediction in betting
senses.definition: a guess about a result on which money or reputation may be staked
senses.definitionCN: 对某个结果作出的判断，可能据此押上金钱或名誉
senses.example: His prediction of the final score won him the office pool.
senses.exampleCN: 他对最终比分的预测让他赢下了办公室的赌局。
senses.why: A bet makes a prediction costly. The word gains weight when being wrong has a price.
senses.whyCN: 下注让预测有了代价。当猜错要付钱时，这个词就变得有分量。

senses.title: Prediction versus explanation
senses.titleCN: 与解释相对：说将来而非说为何
senses.definition: in philosophy of science, the forward-looking counterpart of an explanation of what has already happened
senses.definitionCN: 在科学哲学中，与对已发生之事的解释相对的那个朝前的部分
senses.example: The same law can serve as explanation and as prediction.
senses.exampleCN: 同一条定律既可作解释，也可作预测。
senses.why: Philosophers split the two directions of a theory: backward to causes, forward to predictions. One law, two uses.
senses.whyCN: 哲学家把理论的两个方向分开：向后找原因，向前作预测。同一条定律，两种用途。

intro.en: Prediction comes from Latin praedicere 'to say beforehand', from prae- 'before' plus dicere 'to say, tell'. The noun is praedictio.
intro.cn: prediction 来自拉丁语 praedicere“预先说出”，由 prae-“在前”加 dicere“说、告诉”构成，名词为 praedictio。

items.en: dicere meant 'to say, tell, declare'. It is the source of dictate, dictionary and verdict, and it is not the same root as dicare 'to dedicate'.
items.cn: dicere 意为“说、告诉、宣告”。它是 dictate、dictionary、verdict 的来源，与 dicare“奉献、宣布”并非同一词根。

items.en: prae- 'before' plus dicere produced praedicere, 'to say beforehand, foretell'. The prefix is temporal, not spatial.
items.cn: prae-“在前”加 dicere 构成 praedicere“预先说出、预言”。这个前缀是时间性的，不是空间性的。

items.en: The action noun praedictio covered both 'a foretelling' and 'a proclamation'. Church Latin used it for prophetic declaration.
items.cn: 动作名词 praedictio 兼指“预言”与“宣告”。教会拉丁语用它指先知式的宣告。

items.en: English borrows prediction in the 1500s, first in religious and astrological writing about foretelling the future.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 prediction，最早见于关于预言的宗教与占星写作。

items.en: From the 17th century the word moves into natural philosophy, where a prediction must be testable against observation.
items.cn: 17 世纪起，这个词进入自然哲学，预测必须能被观察检验。

items.en: In the 20th century prediction becomes the standard term for a model's output, and machine learning makes it routine.
items.cn: 20 世纪，prediction 成为模型输出的标准说法，机器学习让它成为日常用语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -dict- stem or the pre- prefix; the near-meaning group shares the forward look but differs in basis and certainty.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -dict- 词干或 pre- 前缀；近义组都朝前看，差别在依据与确定性。

entries.definition: to say in advance that something will happen. The verb names the act; the noun names the act or its content.
entries.definitionCN: 预言；预测。动词命名行为，名词命名行为或其内容。

entries.definition: able to be foreseen because it follows a pattern. It describes the thing, not the forecast.
entries.definitionCN: 可预测的。它描述被预测之物有规律，而非描述预报。

entries.definition: dependence on a substance or habit. It shares dicere 'say' through Latin addictio 'a handing over', but has nothing to do with foretelling.
entries.definitionCN: 上瘾；成瘾。它经由拉丁 addictio“交出”共享 dicere，但与预言无关。

entries.definition: a statement of what is expected, usually from present data. It is close to prediction but commoner in weather and finance.
entries.definitionCN: 预报；预测。常指天气或金融，接近 prediction 但更常用于这两个领域。

entries.definition: an estimate of a future value obtained by extending current trends. It stresses method, not certainty.
entries.definitionCN: 推算；预计。强调延长现有趋势的方法，而非确定性。

entries.definition: a prediction claimed to come from divine or special insight. It carries authority that a scientific prediction does not.
entries.definitionCN: 预言。声称来自神启或特殊洞察，带有科学预测所没有的权威。

entries.definition: an opinion offered without firm evidence. It lacks the evidential base that prediction usually implies.
entries.definitionCN: 猜测。指没有坚实证据的看法，缺少 prediction 通常暗含的证据基础。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: pre- 'before' plus dict 'say' gives 'said before it happens', which is the whole meaning in two pieces.
normal.cn: pre-“在前”加 dict“说”，就是“在发生之前说出”，整个词义由两块拼成。

normal.en: The family predict, predictable, prediction and predictor all keep the same dict stem.
normal.cn: predict、predictable、prediction、predictor 全族保留同一 dict 词干。

normal.en: Scientific usage adds a test: a prediction must be able to fail.
normal.cn: 科学用法加了一条检验：预测必须有可能失败。

normal.en: Model prediction and weather forecast are the same forward arrow, one computed, one observed.
normal.cn: 模型预测与天气预报是同一支前箭头，一个算出来，一个看出来。

normal.en: The opposite word is retrodiction, a statement about the past made from present evidence.
normal.cn: 反面的词是 retrodiction（逆测），即用现在证据推断过去。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow drawn from today into an empty box marked tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭从今天射进标着“明天”的空格。

abstract.en: Picture a weather map where the isobars continue past the right edge of the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张天气图，等压线一直画到纸的右边缘之外。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player saying the next three moves out loud.
abstract.cn: 想象棋手把接下来三步大声说出来。

examples.en: The report's prediction of a dry summer was correct.
examples.cn: 报告关于干旱夏季的预测是正确的。

examples.en: Every prediction from the model comes with an error range.
examples.cn: 模型的每一个预测都附带误差范围。

examples.en: A theory is valued for the predictions it makes possible.
examples.cn: 一个理论的价值在于它能带来哪些预测。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑瑞迪克”音近 prediction：扑上去、锐利地、迪克先开口——抢在事情前头说 → prediction 预测

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前”+ dicere“说、告诉”→ praedicere“预先说出”→ praedictio；英语取 predictio(n-) 词干 + -ion。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all point one arrow forward in time, but differ in who is speaking and what backs the claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把同一支箭指向未来，差别在谁在说、凭什么说。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a note about tomorrow written today.
core.cn: 核心意象：今天写好的一张关于明天的纸条。

branches.en: STATEMENT AND ACT: the noun names both what is said and the saying of it.
branches.cn: 陈述与行为：这个名词既指说出的内容，也指说的行为。

branches.en: SCIENCE: a testable forecast and the philosophical pairing with explanation are the same demand for evidence.
branches.cn: 科学：可检验的预报与哲学上同解释的配对，都是同一个证据要求。

branches.en: CALCULATED FUTURE: model output and trend extension both produce a future number from present data.
branches.cn: 算出的未来：模型输出与趋势延长都用现在数据算出未来数字。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: prophecy is prediction backed by claimed inspiration rather than evidence.
branches.cn: 权威：预言是靠声称的灵感而非证据支撑的预测。

branches.en: STAKES: betting turns a prediction into a commitment with a cost.
branches.cn: 代价：下注把预测变成带成本的承诺。

intro.en: Prediction is pre- plus the dic- stem plus -ion. The prefix marks time, the stem marks speech, and the suffix turns the act into a noun.
intro.cn: prediction 由 pre- 加 dic- 词干加 -ion 构成。前缀标记时间，词干标记言说，后缀把行为变成名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin line is dicere 'say' → praedicere 'foretell' → praedictio 'a foretelling'. The same dicere also yields diction, verdict and contradict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁线为 dicere“说”→ praedicere“预言”→ praedictio“预言”。同一 dicere 还产出 diction、verdict、contradict。

items.example: No one can predict the winner.

items.meaningCN: 预测；预言（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: The prediction failed within a week.
items.exampleCN: 这个预测一周内就落空了。

items.example: The test has predictive value.
His reaction was entirely predictable.
items.exampleCN: 他的反应完全可以预料。

items.meaning: a person who predicts, or a variable used to predict
items.meaningCN: 预测者；预测变量（-or 施事或工具名词）
items.example: Age was the strongest predictor of relapse.
items.exampleCN: 年龄是复发最强的预测变量。

items.example: The weather here is unpredictable.
The two reports contradict each other.
The jury reached a verdict at noon.
items.exampleCN: 陪审团中午作出了裁决。

definition_zh: 学业成就；学习成绩
definition_en: the level of learning a student has reached, usually shown by grades, test scores and completed work
core_image: 一张成绩单与一摞作业本并排放在桌上，旁边贴着逐年上升的折线图
scene: 一所乡镇中学把连续三年的毕业成绩贴在走廊尽头，来访者一眼就能看出变化。 Academic achievement rose steadily after the tutoring programme began.
sceneCN: 学校把三年毕业成绩贴在走廊，变化一眼可见；句中的 academic achievement 指「以分数与作品体现的学业水平」（第 1 个义项：可测量的学习成果）。图中可辨识物件：成绩单、作业本、折线图、走廊公告板。

senses.title: Measured learning outcomes
senses.definition: the level of learning shown by grades, marks and test results
senses.definitionCN: 由等级、分数与测验结果体现的学习水平
senses.example: Academic achievement rose steadily after the tutoring programme began.
senses.exampleCN: 辅导计划开始后，学业成绩稳步上升。
senses.why: achievement names something brought to a head or completed, so the phrase measures how much learning has actually been finished and shown.
senses.whyCN: achievement 指被做到头、被完成的事，因此这个短语衡量的是学习究竟完成了多少并显现出来。

senses.title: Accomplishment at school
senses.definition: a notable success in school, such as a prize, a finished project or a completed course
senses.definitionCN: 在学校的显著成绩，如获奖、完成课题或读完课程
senses.example: Her academic achievement included a national science prize.
senses.exampleCN: 她的学业成就包括一项全国科学奖。
senses.why: the phrase also carries the older sense of achievement as a feat, so it can name a single honour rather than a score.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语还带着 achievement「功业」的旧义，因此可以指一项荣誉而非一个分数。

senses.title: Research accomplishment
senses.definition: the record of research a scholar has produced, judged by publications and grants
senses.definitionCN: 以论文与经费衡量的研究者成果记录
senses.example: The department reviews academic achievement through publications.
senses.exampleCN: 该系通过发表成果来评议科研成就。
senses.why: inside universities the phrase shifts from students to staff, and achievement then means published work rather than examination marks.
senses.whyCN: 在大学内部，这个短语从学生转到教师，achievement 也就指已发表的工作而非考试分数。

senses.title: An attainment level for comparison
senses.titleCN: 用于比较的 attainment 水平
senses.definition: a standard measure that lets schools or regions be set side by side
senses.definitionCN: 使学校或地区可以并排比较的标准化衡量
senses.example: The report compares academic achievement across districts.
senses.exampleCN: 报告比较了各学区的学业水平。
senses.why: measurement makes the phrase political: once results are comparable, they become a ranking of places as well as of pupils.
senses.whyCN: 可测量性使这个短语政治化：结果一旦可比较，它就不只是学生的排名，也成了地区的排名。

senses.title: The achievement gap
senses.definition: the persistent difference in results between groups of students
senses.definitionCN: 不同学生群体之间持续存在的成绩差异
senses.example: The district targeted the academic achievement gap in reading.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区把阅读方面的学业差距作为重点。
senses.why: the phrase is often used in a compound with gap, where the focus moves from one pupil's result to a difference between groups.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语常与「差距」构成复合形式，焦点于是从单个学生的成绩转到群体之间的差异。

senses.title: Honours and recognition
senses.definition: public recognition of scholarly work, such as scholarships or awards
senses.definitionCN: 对学业成果的公开认可，如奖学金或奖项
senses.example: A scholarship recognised her academic achievement in mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 一项奖学金表彰了她在数学上的学业成就。
senses.why: recognition is achievement as a social fact: someone else has judged the work and said so publicly.
senses.whyCN: 表彰使成就成为社会事实：由他人评判并公开说出。

senses.title: Progress over time
senses.definition: the growth in a student's learning measured from one point to another
senses.definitionCN: 从某一时点到另一时点所测得的学业增长
senses.example: The chart tracks academic achievement from year to year.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图逐年追踪学业进步。
senses.why: growth adds a time axis, so the same phrase can praise improvement even when the absolute score stays modest.
senses.whyCN: 加入时间轴之后，同一个短语即使在绝对分数不高时也能表彰进步。

senses.title: Learning beyond scores
senses.definition: the wider development of a learner, including curiosity, method and independence
senses.definitionCN: 学习者更广的发展，包括好奇心、方法与独立性
senses.example: The school counts curiosity as part of academic achievement.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校把好奇心也算作学业成就的一部分。
senses.why: the broad sense pushes back against measurement, insisting that what is learned includes habits that no paper can capture.
senses.whyCN: 宽义是对测量的反弹，坚持所学之中包含纸笔无法捕捉的习惯。

intro.en: The phrase joins academic, from Greek Akadēmeia, the garden where Plato taught, and achievement, from Old French achever 'to finish', literally 'to come to a head'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由 academic 与 achievement 组成。academic 来自希腊 Akadēmeia，即柏拉图讲学的那座园林；achievement 来自古法语 achever「完成」，字面意思是「到达头部」。年代为约数。

items.en: Akadēmeia was the name of the grove outside Athens where Plato taught; it was named after a local hero, Akadēmos.
items.cn: Akadēmeia 是雅典城外柏拉图讲学的那片园林之名，得名于当地一位英雄 Akadēmos。

items.en: Latin academicus meant 'of the Academy', and English academic first described the school of Plato before widening to universities in general.
items.cn: 拉丁 academicus 意为「学园的」，英语 academic 最初指柏拉图的学园，后来扩展到泛指大学。

items.en: Achever 'to finish' came from the phrase a chief 'to a head', built on Latin caput 'head'. To achieve was to bring something to its head, that is, to completion.
items.cn: achever「完成」来自古法语短语，字面义为「到达头部」，其词根是拉丁 caput「头」。achieve 即把某事做到头，也就是完成。

items.en: Both words settled in English by the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, academic as an adjective of the schools and achievement as the act of finishing.
items.cn: 两个词在十四、十五世纪先后进入英语：academic 是学校的形容词，achievement 是完成的行为。

items.en: From the nineteenth century, as mass schooling spread, the two words were paired to name a pupil's measured results, and the phrase became standard in reports.
items.cn: 十九世纪大众教育普及后，两词被组合起来指学生可测量的成绩，这个短语遂成为报告中的标准说法。

items.en: The origin of the name Akadēmos is uncertain; proposals linking it to a district name or to a personal name are hypotheses. The deeper pre-Latin origin of caput is also unsettled, and forms offered for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: Akadēmos 这个名字的来源不确定；把它与某个地名或人名相联的说法均属假说。caput 在拉丁语之前的更深来源亦无定论，为其给出的形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the school-root family and its look-alikes; group two holds words for results and attainment, each measuring a slightly different thing.
note.cn: 第一组是「学园」词根的词族与形近词；第二组是表示成绩与水平的词，各自衡量的东西略有不同。

entries.definition: A learned society or school; it shares the Greek name but names a body, not a result.
entries.definitionCN: 指学术团体或学校，与希腊原名同源，但指机构而非成绩。

entries.definition: Describes study or a teacher; alone it says nothing about how well anyone did.
entries.definitionCN: 描述学业或教师，单用并不说明成绩好坏。

entries.definition: The collective world of universities and research, a place rather than a measure.
entries.definitionCN: 指大学与研究的整体世界，是场所而非衡量。

entries.definition: A member of a learned academy, a title rather than a score.
entries.definitionCN: 指学术团体的成员，是头衔而非分数。

entries.definition: The standard reached in a subject, common in British school reporting; it is close to the score sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某学科达到的水平，常用于英国学校报告，接近分数义。

entries.definition: How well someone carries out a task, which may be judged by observation rather than papers.
entries.definitionCN: 指完成任务的表现，可能靠观察而非纸笔评判。

entries.definition: A stated result of a course, often broader than a single grade.
entries.definitionCN: 指课程设定的学习结果，通常比单一分数更宽。

entries.definition: The accumulated file of marks and reports, rather than the achievement itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指积累起来的分数与报告档案，而非成就本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the two real source words, their real history and the real settings in which the phrase appears.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自两个真实来源词、它们真实的历史，以及这个短语真实出现的场合。

normal.en: Akadēmeia was a garden of learning, so academic points back to a place.
normal.cn: Akadēmeia 是一座求学园林，因此 academic 指向一个场所。

normal.en: a chief 'to a head' gave achieve: to bring work to completion.
normal.cn: 古法语短语「到达头部」造出 achieve：把工作做到完成。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark measurement: achievement scores, achievement gap, achievement standards.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出测量：成绩分数、成就差距、成就标准。

normal.en: The phrase pairs with verbs of change: improve, raise, measure, close the gap.
normal.cn: 这个短语常与变化类动词连用：提高、拉升、衡量、缩小差距。

normal.en: Reports use it with comparisons: across districts, over time, between groups.
normal.cn: 报告用它作比较：跨学区、随时间、在群体之间。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn upward on a wall chart while the corridor stays exactly the same.
abstract.cn: 想象墙图上的线在上升，而走廊本身毫无变化。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of exercise books standing as tall as the child who filled them.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞作业本，高度抵得上写它的那个孩子。

abstract.en: Picture a single prize medal lying on top of a thick file of reports.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚奖牌搁在厚厚一叠报告上。

examples.en: The programme raised academic achievement among first-year students.
examples.cn: 该计划提高了新生的学业成绩。

examples.en: Academic achievement is one measure of a school, not the only one.
examples.cn: 学业成绩是衡量学校的一项指标，而非唯一指标。

examples.en: Researchers studied the academic achievement gap between language groups.
examples.cn: 研究者考察了不同语言群体之间的学业差距。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「academic（学业的）+ achievement（达成）」——在学业上达成的东西 → 学业成就、学习成绩

root: 希腊 Akadēmeia（柏拉图讲学的园林，得名于 Akadēmos）→ 拉丁 academicus「学园的」→ 英语 academic；拉丁 caput「头」→ 古法语短语（字面义「到达头部」）→ achever「完成」→ 英语 achieve／achievement。Akadēmos 之名与 caput 的更早来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one measured climb: learning is finished and shown, then the showing becomes an honour, a research record, a comparable number, a gap, a public recognition, a curve over time and finally a claim that some growth cannot be scored.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述同一条被测量的攀升：学习被完成并显现，显现随后变成荣誉、科研记录、可比较的数字、差距、公开表彰、时间曲线，最后变成一句主张——有些成长无法打分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall chart rising year by year above a stack of completed exercise books.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张逐年上升的墙图，悬在一摞已完成的作业本上方。

branches.en: WORK AND HONOUR: finished learning shows as marks, and an especially finished piece shows as a prize.
branches.cn: 学业与荣誉：完成的学习表现为分数，格外出色的一件则表现为奖项。

branches.en: STAFF AND SCALE: the same phrase judges publications, then turns results into comparable numbers.
branches.cn: 教师与规模：同一短语先评论文，再把结果变成可比较的数字。

branches.en: THE GAP: comparison hardens into a persistent difference between groups.
branches.cn: 差距：比较硬化成群体之间持续存在的差异。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF TIME: a public award fixes one moment, a chart records many.
branches.cn: 两种时间：公开奖项固定一个时刻，折线图记录许多时刻。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: the broad sense insists that curiosity and method never fit a single score.
branches.cn: 限度：宽义坚持好奇心与方法无法塞进一个分数。

intro.en: The phrase is two whole words, each with a real root and suffix history, and each root also builds a family of English words.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个完整的词，各有一个真实的词根与后缀史，每个词根又各造出一族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Greek Akadēmeia and Latin academicus supply the first word; Latin caput, through Old French, supplies the second.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 Akadēmeia 与拉丁 academicus 提供第一个词；拉丁 caput 经古法语提供第二个词。
