definition_zh: 物种形成；新物种的产生
definition_en: the process by which new biological species arise from existing populations
core_image: 一条河把同一群鸟分成两岸两支，许多代以后它们再相遇却已不再互认
scene: 一条宽阔的河流改道，把同一群鸟分成东西两支，长期隔离之后它们逐渐形成不同的物种，这一过程就是物种形成。 A wide river changed course and split one bird population into an eastern and a western branch; after long isolation they gradually became different species, a process called speciation.
sceneCN: 这里 speciation 是「物种形成」（第 1 个义项：新物种从既有群体中分出的整个过程）；句意：河流改道把同一群鸟分成东西两支，长期隔离后逐渐形成不同物种，这一过程叫物种形成。

pos.zh: 物种形成；物种分化（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 形成物种；发生物种分化

senses.title: The rise of a new species
senses.definition: the whole process by which a lineage splits into distinct species that no longer share one gene pool
senses.definitionCN: 一个谱系分化为若干不再共享同一基因库的物种的整个过程
senses.example: Speciation begins when gene flow between two populations stops.
senses.exampleCN: 当两个群体之间的基因流停止时，物种形成便开始了。
senses.why: Species plus -ation makes a noun of process: the category 'kind' is turned into the event of a new kind coming into being.
senses.whyCN: species 加 -ation 构成过程名词：把「种类」这一范畴变成「新种类产生」这一事件。

senses.title: Allopatric speciation by geography
senses.titleCN: 异域物种形成：地理隔离导致分化
senses.definition: speciation that follows when a physical barrier divides one population into separate ranges
senses.definitionCN: 物理屏障把一个群体分隔到不同分布区之后发生的物种形成
senses.example: Allopatric speciation began when the valley cut the population in two.
senses.exampleCN: 当河谷把这个群体切成两半时，异域物种形成开始了。
senses.why: Allo- 'other' plus patria 'fatherland' names the geography: each daughter population evolves in another homeland.
senses.whyCN: allo-「别的」加 patria「故土」点明地理条件：每个子群体都在另一片故土中演化。

senses.title: Sympatric speciation without a barrier
senses.titleCN: 同域物种形成：无地理屏障
senses.definition: speciation within one continuous area, driven by factors such as polyploidy, host shift or assortative mating
senses.definitionCN: 在同一连续区域内，由多倍化、寄主转换或选型交配等因素驱动的物种形成
senses.example: Sympatric speciation can follow a shift to a new host plant.
senses.exampleCN: 同域物种形成可以随着转向新的寄主植物而发生。
senses.why: Syn- 'together' plus patria 'homeland' says the opposite of the allopatric case: the two forms diverge while living in the same place.
senses.whyCN: syn-「共同」加 patria「故土」与异域情形正好相反：两个类型在同一地点生活却发生分化。

senses.title: Parapatric speciation along a gradient
senses.titleCN: 邻域物种形成：沿环境梯度分化
senses.definition: speciation across a partial barrier or a steep environmental gradient, with limited gene flow at the contact zone
senses.definitionCN: 在部分屏障或陡峭环境梯度两侧发生的物种形成，接触带仍有有限的基因流
senses.example: Parapatric speciation proceeds along the steep gradient of the mountain slope.
senses.exampleCN: 邻域物种形成沿着山坡陡峭的环境梯度推进。
senses.why: Para- 'beside' plus patria marks neighbouring ranges: the populations touch at a border but do not freely mix.
senses.whyCN: para-「旁侧」加 patria 表示相邻分布区：群体在边界相接，却不自由混合。

senses.title: Reproductive isolation as the decisive step
senses.titleCN: 生殖隔离作为决定性一步
senses.definition: the point at which two diverging forms can no longer interbreed successfully, so the split is complete
senses.definitionCN: 两个分化中的类型不再能成功互交、分化由此完成的那个节点
senses.example: Speciation is complete only when the two forms no longer interbreed.
senses.exampleCN: 只有当两个类型不再互交时，物种形成才算完成。
senses.why: A species is a breeding community, so the process is finished when that community has become two; isolation is the test, not the scenery.
senses.whyCN: 物种就是一个繁殖共同体，因此当这个共同体变成两个时过程即告完成；生殖隔离是判据，而不是背景。

senses.title: Polyploid speciation in a single generation
senses.titleCN: 多倍体物种形成：一代之内完成
senses.definition: the origin of a new species through a change in chromosome number, often instant and common in plants
senses.definitionCN: 通过染色体数目变化产生新物种，常在一代之内完成，在植物中很常见
senses.example: Polyploid speciation produced a fertile hybrid within a single generation.
senses.exampleCN: 多倍体物种形成在一代之内就产生了可育的杂种。
senses.why: When chromosome doubling makes a hybrid fertile with its own kind but not with its parents, the new species appears at once rather than gradually.
senses.whyCN: 当染色体加倍使杂种能与同类可育、却不能与亲本可育时，新物种立刻出现，而非逐渐形成。

senses.title: Speciation rate in macroevolution
senses.titleCN: 宏观演化中的物种形成速率
senses.definition: the frequency with which new species arise in a lineage over geological time, often measured as events per million years
senses.definitionCN: 某一谱系在地质时间尺度上新物种产生的频率，常以每百万年的事件数计
senses.example: The fossil record shows bursts of speciation after each mass extinction.
senses.exampleCN: 化石记录显示，每次大灭绝之后都出现物种形成的爆发。
senses.why: Once the process is dated in the rock record, speciation becomes a rate: how many splits per unit time a clade produces.
senses.whyCN: 当这一过程能在岩石记录中定年时，物种形成就变成了速率：一个支系在单位时间内产生多少次分裂。

senses.title: Speciation observed in the laboratory
senses.titleCN: 实验室中观测到的物种形成
senses.definition: the experimental production of reproductive isolation between laboratory populations, as in long-running selection lines
senses.definitionCN: 在实验条件下使实验室群体之间产生生殖隔离，例如长期选择实验中的品系
senses.example: Speciation in the laboratory was documented when two fly lines stopped mating.
senses.exampleCN: 当两个果蝇品系不再交配时，实验室中的物种形成得到了记录。
senses.why: Experimental evolution makes the process observable within a career: the split is measured as a mating preference rather than inferred from fossils.
senses.whyCN: 实验演化使这一过程在一个人一生之内可被观察：分裂以交配偏好的形式测量，而不必从化石推断。

intro.en: Speciation is a nineteenth-century noun made from species, the Latin word for 'kind, appearance', plus the process suffix -ation. The date is approximate, and the deepest Indo-European layer is a reconstruction.
intro.cn: speciation 是 19 世纪由 species（拉丁语「种类、外观」）加过程后缀 -ation 构成的名词。年代为约数，最深层印欧语层属于重构。

items.en: Species in Latin meant 'sight, appearance, form, kind'. It was a fifth-declension noun, and its plural was also species.
items.cn: 拉丁语 species 意为「视觉、外观、形态、种类」，是第五变格法名词，复数形式同样是 species。

items.en: The noun rests on specere 'to look, to see'; the same root gives specimen, spectacle and spectrum.
items.cn: 该名词基于 specere「看、观看」；同一词根还给出 specimen、spectacle 与 spectrum。

items.en: The Latin suffix -atio(n)- named an action or its result; English -ation turned species into the name of a process rather than a category.
items.cn: 拉丁后缀 -atio(n)- 表示动作或其结果；英语 -ation 把 species 由类别名称变成过程名称。

items.en: The noun speciation is recorded in English from the mid-nineteenth century, when evolutionary biology needed a word for the origin of species.
items.cn: 名词 speciation 于 19 世纪中叶见于英语，当时演化生物学正需要一个词来指物种的起源。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was divided by geography into allopatric, sympatric and parapatric modes, each with its own prefix.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词按地理条件被分为异域、同域与邻域三种模式，每种都带各自的前缀。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first citation of speciation is not fixed here, and the pre-Latin origin of specere is a reconstruction rather than an attested form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：speciation 最早书证的确切年份此处无法确定；specere 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式，而非有据可查的形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the Latin spec- stock that look alike; group two holds processes that are close in meaning but not identical.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 spec- 词干、外形相近的词；第二组是意思接近但并不相同的各种过程。

entries.definition: The category itself, whose plural is unchanged. Speciation is the process by which a new species comes into being.
entries.definitionCN: 物种这一范畴本身，复数形式不变。speciation 则是新物种产生的过程。

entries.definition: A single sample used for study, from the same specere 'to look'. It names an object, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 供研究用的单个样本，同出 specere「看」。它指实物，不指过程。

entries.definition: A detailed statement of requirements, from species in its 'kind' sense plus facere 'to make'. It has no evolutionary meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 对要求的详细说明，由 species 的「种类」义加 facere「做」构成，没有演化含义。

entries.definition: The development of a form fitted to a particular function, from specialis 'individual, particular'. It is not speciation.
entries.definitionCN: 发展出适应特定功能的形式，来自 specialis「个别的、特定的」，并非物种形成。

entries.definition: Change in heritable traits over generations. Speciation is one kind of evolution, not its synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 可遗传性状在世代间的变化。物种形成是演化的一种，并非其同义词。

entries.definition: The separation of lineages from a common ancestor; it may occur without full reproductive isolation.
entries.definitionCN: 谱系从共同祖先分开；这种分开未必达到完全的生殖隔离。

entries.definition: The rapid diversification of one lineage into many species filling different niches. It is a pattern made of many speciation events.
entries.definitionCN: 一个谱系迅速分化为许多占据不同生态位的物种；它是由多次物种形成构成的格局。

entries.definition: Crossing between distinct taxa, which can sometimes create a new species but is the opposite direction of gene flow.
entries.definitionCN: 不同类群间的杂交，有时能产生新物种，但基因流方向与分化相反。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: species 'kind' + -ation 'process': speciation is literally the process of a new kind appearing.
normal.cn: species「种类」+ -ation「过程」：speciation 字面就是新种类出现的过程。

normal.en: The three geographical modes carry their own prefixes: allo- other land, sym- same land, para- beside land.
normal.cn: 三种地理模式各带前缀：allo- 别的土地、sym- 同一土地、para- 旁侧土地。

normal.en: Reproductive isolation is the finishing line; a species is a breeding community, so two communities mean two species.
normal.cn: 生殖隔离是终点线；物种是繁殖共同体，因此两个共同体就意味着两个物种。

normal.en: Polyploidy can finish the job in one generation, which is why speciation is often instant in plants.
normal.cn: 多倍体可以在一代之内完成这件事，这就是植物中物种形成常常是瞬间发生的原因。

normal.en: Speciation rate is the fossil-record version of the word: splits per million years.
normal.cn: 物种形成速率是这个词在化石记录中的形态：每百万年发生多少次分裂。

abstract.en: Picture a rope fraying into two cords that can no longer be spliced back together.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子分成两股，再也无法重新编回一根。

abstract.en: Picture two dialects drifting apart until neither speaker understands the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两种方言渐行渐远，直到双方都听不懂对方。

abstract.en: Picture a broken bridge between two islands: the same boats can no longer reach either shore.
abstract.cn: 想象两座岛之间的桥断了：同一批船再也到不了对岸。

examples.en: Speciation in island birds followed each colonization of an empty archipelago.
examples.cn: 岛屿鸟类的物种形成在每一次登上空群岛之后发生。

examples.en: The two orchids count as one species until the day their pollinators stop sharing.
examples.cn: 这两种兰花仍算一个物种，直到它们的传粉者不再共享的那一天。

examples.en: Museum collections supply the dates used to estimate speciation rates.
examples.cn: 博物馆藏品提供了估算物种形成速率所需的年代数据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「specia」——一个「种」加一个「过程」，新种就这样生出来 → speciation 物种形成

root: 拉丁 species「种类、外观」+ -ation「过程」；species 出自 specere「看、观看」，同根词有 specimen、spectacle、spectrum。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of speciation all name one event seen at different scales: a breeding community splits, and the split can be caused by a river, by a host shift, by doubled chromosomes, by geological time or by a laboratory cage.
sensesIntro.cn: speciation 的八个义项都指同一事件在不同尺度上的呈现：一个繁殖共同体分裂，而分裂的起因可以是河流、寄主转换、染色体加倍、地质时间或实验室的笼子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one breeding community becoming two that no longer exchange members.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个繁殖共同体变成两个，彼此不再交换成员。

branches.en: THE WHOLE PROCESS: speciation is the name of the split itself, seen from start to finish.
branches.cn: 整个过程：speciation 就是分裂本身的名称，从开头看到结尾。

branches.en: WHERE IT HAPPENS: other land, same land and neighbouring land give the three geographical modes.
branches.cn: 发生在哪里：别的土地、同一土地、相邻土地给出三种地理模式。

branches.en: THE TEST: the split counts as complete only when interbreeding fails.
branches.cn: 判据：只有互交失败时，分裂才算完成。

branches.en: SUDDEN MODE: doubled chromosomes can finish the split within one generation.
branches.cn: 突变模式：染色体加倍能在一代之内完成分裂。

branches.en: MEASURED IN TIME: fossils give a rate per million years, cages give a rate per career.
branches.cn: 在时间中测量：化石给出每百万年的速率，笼子给出每人一生的速率。

intro.en: Speciation is transparent once species and -ation are separated: one Latin noun of kind, one Latin suffix of process.
intro.cn: 只要把 species 与 -ation 分开，speciation 就一目了然：一个表示种类的拉丁名词，一个表示过程的拉丁后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin species gives the English family species, specious and speciose; specere adds specimen, spectacle, spectrum and inspect.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 species 衍生英语的 species、specious 与 speciose；specere 另给出 specimen、spectacle、spectrum 与 inspect。

items.example: Species is both singular and plural in English.
items.exampleCN: species 在英语中单复数同形。

items.example: The root names the visible mark that sorts one kind from another.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指用来区分种类的可见标记。

items.example: Island flies speciate on each newly raised ridge.
items.exampleCN: 岛上的果蝇在每一道新升起的山脊上形成新种。

items.example: The suffix turns a category into an event.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀把类别变成事件。

items.example: Speciation is measured as a rate in the fossil record.
items.exampleCN: 物种形成在化石记录中以速率计量。

items.example: Subspeciation preceded full isolation in the northern range.
items.exampleCN: 在北部分布区，亚种分化先于完全隔离。

items.example: The speciose genus fills every damp hollow.
items.exampleCN: 这个多物种的属填满了每一处潮湿洼地。

items.example: Speciational bursts followed the lake's formation.
items.exampleCN: 物种形成的爆发随湖泊形成而来。

definition_zh: 元素的；基本的；自然力般的；原始的
definition_en: relating to a chemical element, or to basic and powerful forces of nature
core_image: 一堆杂物被拆到只剩四块最基本的积木，其余全都可以由它们再拼出来
scene: 风从山口灌进来，院墙外的树被连根拔起。 Wind and rain are elemental forces that no wall can stop.
sceneCN: 这里 elemental 指自然力般的、狂暴而不可挡的（第 3 个义项：如自然元素之力那样强大）；句意：风与雨是任何墙都挡不住的自然之力。图中可辨识物件：山口、被吹倒的树、断裂的院墙、飞散的枝叶。

pos.zh: 元素的；基本的；自然力般的；原始的

derivatives.zh: 在基本层面；以自然力方式
元素论者；自然力艺术创作者

senses.title: Relating to a chemical element
senses.definition: concerning a chemical element or the elements that a substance contains
senses.definitionCN: 关于化学元素，或关于某物质所含各元素的
senses.example: Elemental analysis showed that the sample was almost pure carbon.
senses.exampleCN: 元素分析显示这个样品几乎是纯碳。
senses.why: the adjective simply attaches the noun element to a method or a result, with no figurative colour at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词「元素」接到方法或结果上，完全没有比喻色彩。

senses.title: Basic and fundamental
senses.definition: forming the simplest necessary part of something, beyond which one cannot go
senses.definitionCN: 构成某物最简单而必要的部分，再不能往下拆
senses.example: The report reduced the problem to a few elemental facts.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把问题归结为几条根本事实。
senses.why: an element is a first principle, so what cannot be reduced further is naturally called elemental.
senses.whyCN: 元素即是第一原理，因此不能再往下拆的东西自然被称为「基本的」。

senses.title: Like a force of nature
senses.definition: as powerful and unstoppable as wind, water, fire or earth
senses.definitionCN: 像风、水、火、土那样强大而不可阻挡
senses.example: Wind and rain are elemental forces that no wall can stop.
senses.exampleCN: 风与雨是任何墙都挡不住的自然之力。
senses.why: the ancient four elements were believed to underlie all matter, so a force that feels older than buildings is called elemental.
senses.whyCN: 古代认为四种元素构成万物，因此那种比建筑更古老的力量被称为「元素般的」。

senses.title: Rough and primitive
senses.definition: simple to the point of crudeness, stripped of comfort or refinement
senses.definitionCN: 简单到粗陋，毫无舒适或精致可言
senses.example: The shelter was elemental: four posts, a roof and a fire.
senses.exampleCN: 那处居所极其原始：四根柱子、一个顶、一堆火。
senses.why: if only the basic elements remain, nothing has been added for comfort, and the adjective records that bareness.
senses.whyCN: 若只剩最基本的要素，就没有为舒适添加任何东西，这个形容词记录的正是这种裸露。

senses.title: Of the four-element theory
senses.definition: belonging to the old theory that all matter is made of earth, water, air and fire
senses.definitionCN: 属于「万物由土、水、气、火构成」这一旧理论的
senses.example: Elemental theory explained burning as the release of fire from wood.
senses.exampleCN: 四元素说把燃烧解释为火从木头中释放。
senses.why: before modern chemistry, element meant one of four substances, and the adjective still labels that system.
senses.whyCN: 在现代化学之前，元素指四种物质之一，这个形容词仍用来标记那套体系。

senses.title: Serving as a basic unit
senses.definition: describing the smallest units out of which a larger whole is built
senses.definitionCN: 指构成更大整体的最小单元
senses.example: The model treats families as elemental units of the settlement.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型把家庭当作聚落的基本单元。
senses.why: the word keeps the image of building blocks: whatever cannot be split further serves as an elemental part.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留「积木」的意象：凡是不能再拆的东西，就充当基本部件。

senses.title: At the level of basic skills
senses.definition: belonging to the first, simplest layer of a skill or subject
senses.definitionCN: 属于某项技能或学科最初、最简单的层次
senses.example: The course covers elemental reading and counting before any theory.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课先讲最基础的读与算，然后才谈理论。
senses.why: schooling speaks of elemental skills where it means the layer below all later ones.
senses.whyCN: 教育说「基础技能」，指的是位于一切后续层次之下的那一层。

senses.title: Simple and uncomplicated
senses.definition: pleasantly plain, without sophistication or hidden layers
senses.definitionCN: 质朴而令人愉快，没有精巧或隐藏的层次
senses.example: Swimming in cold water gave him an elemental pleasure.
senses.exampleCN: 在冷水里游泳给他一种单纯的快乐。
senses.why: the same bareness that can feel harsh can also feel honest, so the adjective carries a second, warmer tone.
senses.whyCN: 同一种裸露既可能显得艰苦，也可能显得诚实，因此这个形容词带有第二种更温暖的语气。

intro.en: Elemental is element plus the Latin adjective ending -alis, English -al. The noun element goes back to Latin elementum, whose own origin is disputed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: elemental 是 element 加拉丁形容词词尾 -alis（英语作 -al）。名词 element 上溯拉丁语 elementum，其本身来源有争议。年代均为约数。

items.en: Elementum meant a first principle or rudiment, and in the plural elementa, the letters of the alphabet, the first lessons of a subject.
items.cn: elementum 意为「第一原理、入门」，复数 elementa 指字母表，也指一门学科最初的课程。

items.en: Medieval and Renaissance Latin used elementum for earth, water, air and fire, the supposed constituents of all bodies.
items.cn: 中世纪与文艺复兴时期的拉丁语用 elementum 指土、水、气、火，即被认为构成一切物体的四种东西。

items.en: English element is recorded from the fourteenth century in both the alphabetical and the material senses.
items.cn: 英语 element 自 14 世纪有记录，兼具字母与物质两种含义。

items.en: Modern chemistry redefined element as a substance that cannot be split by chemical means, and this sense now dominates.
items.cn: 现代化学把 element 重新定义为不能用化学方法再分的物质，这一义项如今占主导。

items.en: Latin -alis made adjectives of relation; English shortened the ending to -al, giving elemental beside elementary.
items.cn: 拉丁语 -alis 构成关系形容词；英语把词尾缩为 -al，于是在 elementary 之外又有了 elemental。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin of elementum): no derivation is established. One old suggestion links it to alere, to nourish; another reads it as a sequence of letters; a third treats it as an Etruscan or otherwise borrowed word. All three are hypotheses.
items.cn: 来源不确定（elementum 的来源）：没有已证实的派生。旧说之一把它与 alere「滋养」相联系；另一说把它读作字母序列；第三说视之为伊特鲁里亚语或其他借词。三者都只是假说。

note.en: The first group shares the element stem and is often confused in writing; the second group names other words for what is basic or raw.
note.cn: 第一组共享 element 词干，写作中常被混用；第二组是其他表示「基本、原始」的词。

entries.definition: The noun itself: a chemical element, a component or a first principle; the adjective only describes such a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词本身：化学元素、成分或第一原理；形容词只是描述这类事物。

entries.definition: From the same stem but with a different ending, it usually means simple, introductory or basic, as in elementary school.
entries.definitionCN: 同词干而词尾不同，通常指简单、入门、基础，如小学。

entries.definition: The adverb form, used when describing how something acts at the level of elements or basic forces.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，用于描述某物在元素或基本力量层面如何起作用。

entries.definition: The plural often means the weather and its forces, as in exposed to the elements, a sense the adjective echoes.
entries.definitionCN: 复数常指天气及其力量，如「暴露在风雨中」，形容词正呼应这一义。

entries.definition: The everyday word for what lies at the bottom of a structure; it lacks the force-of-nature overtone.
entries.definitionCN: 日常用词，指结构最底层的部分；没有「自然之力」那层意味。

entries.definition: From Latin fundus, bottom: it stresses that everything else rests on this, rather than that it cannot be split.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 fundus「底部」：强调其余一切依赖它，而不是强调不可再分。

entries.definition: Of the first age or the earliest layer of feeling; it adds time and instinct, which elemental only suggests.
entries.definitionCN: 指最初的时代或最早的情感层次；加上时间与本能，而 elemental 只是暗示。

entries.definition: Unprocessed, uncovered or harsh; it is close to one sense of elemental but said of materials and weather.
entries.definitionCN: 未经加工、裸露或严酷；接近 elemental 的某一义，但多用于材料与天气。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin noun, the real adjective ending and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁名词、真实的形容词词尾与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Element plus -al: the adjective of first principles.
normal.cn: element 加 -al：第一原理的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs element, elemental, elementary, elementally and elements.
normal.cn: 同族词有 element、elemental、elementary、elementally 与 elements。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show both halves: elemental analysis, elemental forces.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示两面：元素分析、自然之力。

normal.en: Old chemistry counted four elements, which is why the word can mean weather at its worst.
normal.cn: 旧化学只数四种元素，所以这个词也能指最恶劣的天气。

normal.en: Elementary and elemental share a stem but not a job: one means introductory, the other means of elements.
normal.cn: elementary 与 elemental 同词干而分工不同：一个指入门，一个指元素本身。

abstract.en: Picture a child who empties a toy box until only four shapes remain.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子把玩具箱倒空，只剩四种形状。

abstract.en: Picture a storm that treats a brick wall as a curtain.
abstract.cn: 想象一场风暴把砖墙当作帘子。

abstract.en: Picture a meal of bread and water eaten outdoors, tasting better than a banquet.
abstract.cn: 想象在户外吃面包和白水，却比宴席更有滋味。

examples.en: Elemental sulphur is yellow and brittle at room temperature.
examples.cn: 单质硫在室温下是黄色而易碎的。

examples.en: The film reduces the story to an elemental struggle for water.
examples.cn: 影片把故事归结为一场最根本的争水之争。

examples.en: The hut offered elemental shelter and nothing more.
examples.cn: 那间小屋只提供最原始的遮蔽，别无一物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「element（元素）+ al」——像元素一样不可再分、又像自然力一样强大 → 基本的、自然力般的

root: 拉丁 elementum「第一原理、入门（复数指字母）」→ 英语 element「元素」→ 加形容词词尾 -al → elemental；elementum 本身的来源无定论，滋养说、字母序列说、借词说三者并列。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: what cannot be reduced further. The idea serves chemistry, then plain fundamentals, then the four ancient elements, then forces of nature, then bare shelter, basic units, first skills and finally simple pleasure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个想法展开：不能再往下拆的东西。这个想法依次用于化学、一般原理、古代四元素、自然之力、裸露的居所、基本单元、最初技能，最后是单纯的快乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heap of clutter reduced to four building blocks from which everything else can be rebuilt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堆杂物被拆到只剩四块积木，其余一切都能由它们重建。

branches.en: THE ELEMENT ITSELF: a method or result that concerns chemical elements.
branches.cn: 元素本身：涉及化学元素的方法或结果。

branches.en: THE BLOCK: what cannot be split further, and what therefore supports everything else.
branches.cn: 积木：不能再拆的东西，因而支撑其余一切。

branches.en: THE STORM: the old elements imagined as weather with no wall strong enough.
branches.cn: 风暴：把古老元素想象成任何墙都挡不住的天气。

branches.en: BARE LIFE: only the necessary parts left, which can feel harsh or honest.
branches.cn: 裸露的生活：只剩必需的部分，既可能艰苦，也可能诚实。

branches.en: OLD THEORY AND FIRST LESSONS: four substances, and the first layer of a skill.
branches.cn: 旧理论与最初课程：四种物质，以及一门技能的最初层次。

intro.en: Elemental is a Latin-derived noun with a Latin adjective ending; the stem itself is ancient but of disputed origin.
intro.cn: elemental 是拉丁来源的名词加拉丁形容词词尾；词干古老，但来源有争议。

latinIntro.en: Latin elementum and its plural elementa supply the stem, and -alis supplies the adjective pattern shared with many English words in -al.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 elementum 及其复数 elementa 提供词干，-alis 提供与许多英语 -al 词共享的形容词样板。

items.example: The Latin noun already carried the idea of a starting unit.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已带有「起始单元」的意思。

items.example: The plural meant the alphabet before it meant substances.
items.exampleCN: 这个复数先指字母表，后指物质。

items.example: The ending made relational adjectives throughout Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾在拉丁语中构成大量关系形容词。

items.example: English shortened the ending in hundreds of borrowings.
items.exampleCN: 英语在数百个借词中把这个词尾缩短。

items.example: Carbon is an element; water is a compound.

items.meaning: of elements or of basic forces
items.example: Elemental forces shaped the coastline.
items.exampleCN: 自然之力塑造了这段海岸。

items.example: Elementary arithmetic comes before algebra.
The two reactions are elementally different.
items.exampleCN: 这两个反应在元素层面上不同。

items.example: The tent stood against the elements all night.

definition_zh: 页边的；微小的；边缘化的；边际的；以微弱差距的；贫瘠边缘的；生态边缘的；次要的
definition_en: situated at or near an edge, or so small and slight that it barely matters
core_image: 书页正文之外那条窄窄的空白，写满了小字，正文反倒显得像主体
scene: 两种涂料刷在墙上，屋里的人来回看了半天，几乎分不出哪一种更浅。 The difference between the two paints is marginal at best.
sceneCN: 这里指差别小到几乎可以忽略（第 2 个义项：数量上的差异极微小）；句意为这两种涂料的差别充其量也只是微乎其微。

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 margo「边缘」，是该形容词的词基，义为「页边；边缘；差额」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「略微；以微弱差距」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「边缘性；边缘地位」
由该形容词加表示「使……化」的动词后缀构成，义为「使边缘化」
由「使边缘化」的动词加表示动作结果的名词后缀构成，义为「边缘化」

senses.title: Written in the page margin
senses.definition: placed in the blank border of a page rather than in the main body of text
senses.definitionCN: 放在页面的空白边栏里，而不是正文之中
senses.example: A marginal note in pencil corrected the date.
senses.exampleCN: 一条铅笔写的页边注改正了日期。
senses.why: The Latin noun meant edge or border, and a page's border is its most literal margin.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词意为边缘或边界，书页的边栏就是最字面的「边缘」。

senses.title: So small it barely counts
senses.definition: very slight in amount or degree, close to the point of being unimportant
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度上极小，接近无关紧要的地步
senses.example: The second product was only marginally cheaper.
senses.exampleCN: 第二件商品只是略微便宜一点。
senses.why: A difference at the edge of measurement sits just inside or outside the line, so it is barely worth counting.
senses.whyCN: 处于测量边缘的差异，正好贴着界线内外，因此几乎不值得计数。

senses.title: Pushed to the edge of society
senses.definition: having little power, representation or acceptance within a larger society
senses.definitionCN: 在更大的社会中缺少权力、代表性或接纳度
senses.example: The report focuses on marginal groups in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告关注城市里的边缘群体。
senses.why: People placed outside the main body of a society are located at its border, exactly where the word points.
senses.whyCN: 被置于社会主体之外的人，就处在它的边界上，正是这个词所指的位置。

senses.title: The next unit in economics
senses.titleCN: 经济学中再增加一单位
senses.definition: relating to the extra cost, benefit or utility of one additional unit
senses.definitionCN: 与再增加一个单位所带来的额外成本、收益或效用有关
senses.example: Marginal cost rises once the factory nears capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂接近产能上限时，边际成本会上升。
senses.why: Economics looks at the change at the edge of existing output, and that edge is the margin.
senses.whyCN: 经济学看的是现有产出边缘处的变化，而那个边就是「边际」。

senses.title: Decided by a tiny gap
senses.definition: won or lost by a very small number of votes or points, so the result could easily change
senses.definitionCN: 以极少的票数或分数取胜或落败，结果很容易翻转
senses.example: The party holds a marginal seat by two hundred votes.
senses.exampleCN: 该党以两百票的优势握有一个边缘选区。
senses.why: A result sitting on the boundary between win and loss is marginal in the political sense.
senses.whyCN: 停在胜负边界上的结果，在政治意义上就是「边缘的」。

senses.title: Land at the limit of farming
senses.definition: land whose soil or position makes farming only barely profitable
senses.definitionCN: 土壤或位置使耕作只能勉强获利的土地
senses.example: Marginal land is often left to grazing.
senses.exampleCN: 边缘土地常被留作放牧。
senses.why: Such land lies at the edge of what can be cultivated, so it carries the edge word by position.
senses.whyCN: 这类土地处在可耕种的边缘，因此按位置得到「边缘」之名。

senses.title: A habitat at the edge of a range
senses.definition: a habitat where a species survives at the limit of its tolerated conditions
senses.definitionCN: 某物种在可忍受条件的极限处勉强存活的生境
senses.example: Marginal habitats hold fewer species but rare ones.
senses.exampleCN: 边缘生境物种较少，却常有珍稀种类。
senses.why: Ecology maps a range with a centre and a rim, and life at the rim lives on the margin.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把一个分布范围画成有中心有外围，住在外围的生命就处在边缘。

senses.title: Of secondary importance
senses.definition: playing a small or non-central part in a larger matter
senses.definitionCN: 在更大的事务中只起很小的、非核心的作用
senses.example: His role in the negotiation was marginal.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这场谈判中的作用很次要。
senses.why: Anything not in the main body of an affair is pushed to its edge, and the edge is where marginal things sit.
senses.whyCN: 不在事务主体之内的一切都被推到边上，而「边缘」正是这类事物所在之处。

intro.en: Marginal comes from Latin margo, marginis 'edge, border', through the adjective marginalis. English adopted it in the sixteenth century, and economics and politics later gave it precise uses. The Latin source is certain; the earlier origin of margo is reconstructed rather than attested.
intro.cn: marginal 来自拉丁 margo、marginis「边缘、边界」，经形容词 marginalis 进入英语，十六世纪被采用，后来经济学与政治学又赋予它精确用法。拉丁来源确定；margo 更早的来源属于重构，并未留下实证。

items.en: Margo meant edge, border or brink, and it named the rim of a page, a field or a sea.
items.cn: margo 意为边缘、边界或崖沿，可指书页、田地或海的边沿。

items.en: The pre-Latin source of margo is not settled, and proposals for its deeper root remain reconstructions rather than recorded forms.
items.cn: margo 在拉丁语之前的来源尚无定论，对其更深词根的种种设想仍属重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Medieval Latin marginalis meant 'of the margin', first for writing placed at the edge of a page.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 marginalis 意为「页边的」，最初指写在页边上的文字。

items.en: English marginal began with page notes, then widened to anything at an edge or limit.
items.cn: 英语的这个词从页边注开始，随后扩展到任何处于边缘或极限的事物。

items.en: Nineteenth-century economics used marginal for the extra cost or benefit of one more unit, giving marginal cost and marginal utility.
items.cn: 十九世纪经济学用这个词指再加一单位的额外成本或收益，产生「边际成本」与「边际效用」。

items.en: A marginal seat is won by a small gap, and a marginal group sits outside the centre of a society.
items.cn: 边缘选区以极小差距决出；边缘群体处在社会中心之外。

note.en: The first group shares the edge stem; the second group holds words for smallness or secondary position, each with a different reason.
note.cn: 第一组共享「边缘」词干；第二组是表示微小或次要的词，各自的理由不同。

entries.definition: The blank edge of a page, or the amount by which one value exceeds another.
entries.definitionCN: 页面的空白边，或一个数值超出另一个的差额。

entries.definition: Slightly, or by a very small amount; it modifies comparisons.
entries.definitionCN: 略微，或以极小数量；修饰比较。

entries.definition: The condition of being at the edge of a group or system; a sociological noun.
entries.definitionCN: 处于群体或系统边缘的状况；是社会学的名词。

entries.definition: To push a person or group to the edge of influence; it names the act, not the state.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或群体推到影响力的边缘；命名动作，而非状态。

entries.definition: Small in degree; it measures amount only and says nothing about position at an edge.
entries.definitionCN: 程度上很小；只量数量，不涉及是否处于边缘。

entries.definition: Low in importance; it ranks things, while the target word places them at a border.
entries.definitionCN: 重要性低；对事物排序，而目标词把它们放到边界上。

entries.definition: On the outer edge of a system, often beside the main concern; close, but more spatial and less numerical.
entries.definitionCN: 处于系统的外缘，常在主关注点旁边；意思接近，但更偏空间而非数量。

entries.definition: So small that it can be disregarded; stronger than the target word, which still allows the difference to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 小到可以不理会；比目标词更强，因为目标词仍承认这点差别有意义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'edge': marginal things live at the edge of a page, a market or a society.
normal.cn: 词根意为「边缘」：边缘之物活在书页、市场或社会的边上。

normal.en: The family runs margin, marginally, marginality and marginalize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括页边、略微、边缘性、使边缘化。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark economics: marginal cost, marginal utility.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出经济学：边际成本、边际效用。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark politics and society: marginal seat, marginal group.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出政治与社会：边缘选区、边缘群体。

normal.en: Its neighbours differ: slight is only small, negligible is almost nothing.
normal.cn: 近邻有别：slight 只是小，negligible 几乎是零。

abstract.en: Picture a page whose margin is filled while the centre stays blank.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸边栏写满，正文却空着。

abstract.en: Picture a runner finishing one stride behind the winner.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑者比冠军差一步冲线。

abstract.en: Picture a town so close to the border that the sign is on its main street.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小镇贴着边界，界牌就立在主街上。

examples.en: The effect on test scores was marginal.
examples.cn: 对考试成绩的影响微乎其微。

examples.en: Marginal notes in the old book show how it was read.
examples.cn: 这本旧书上的页边注显示了它曾被怎样阅读。

examples.en: The policy did little for marginal communities.
examples.cn: 这项政策对边缘群体帮助甚微。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马挤脑」——马挤在栅栏最边上，只占一线之地，就是边缘的

root: 拉丁 margo、marginis「边缘、边界」→ 中世纪拉丁 marginalis「页边的」→ 英语 marginal；margo 更早的来源属重构，尚未确证。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place something at an edge: the rim of a page, the limit of significance, the border of society, the next unit of output, the line between win and loss, land or habitat at a limit, and a secondary role.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物放在边缘上：书页的边、意义的临界、社会的边界、产出的下一单位、胜负的分界、处于极限的土地或生境，以及次要的角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow strip at the border, where a thing sits just inside the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：边界上一条窄带，事物正贴着界线内侧。

branches.en: THE PAGE SENSE: writing placed in the blank border.
branches.cn: 书页义：写在空白边栏里的文字。

branches.en: THE NUMERICAL EDGE: a difference barely worth counting, and a result decided by a tiny gap.
branches.cn: 数量边缘：几乎不值得计数的差别，以及以极小差距决出的结果。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL EDGE: people outside the centre of a society.
branches.cn: 社会边缘：处在社会中心之外的人。

branches.en: THE ECONOMIC EDGE: the extra cost or benefit of one more unit.
branches.cn: 经济边缘：再加一单位的额外成本或收益。

branches.en: THE LIMITS OF USE: land barely worth farming, habitat barely survivable, and a role barely central.
branches.cn: 使用极限：勉强可耕的地、勉强能活的生境，以及勉强算核心的角色。

intro.en: Marginal is built on Latin margo 'edge' with the adjective ending -al; English adds endings for manner, state and the act of pushing to the edge.
intro.cn: marginal 建立在拉丁 margo「边缘」与形容词词尾 -al 之上；英语再加表示方式、状态与「推至边缘」动作的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Margo, marginis 'edge' gives the stem margin-, and Medieval Latin marginalis gives the adjective; English margin also comes from the same noun.
latinIntro.cn: margo、marginis「边缘」给出词干 margin-，中世纪拉丁 marginalis 给出形容词；英语的 margin 也出自同一名词。

items.example: The noun is the origin of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The stem appears in margin and marginal.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在 margin 与 marginal 中。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成形容词。

items.example: It first described writing in a page margin.
items.exampleCN: 它最初描述写在页边的文字。

items.example: English widened it to economics and society.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它扩展到经济学与社会。

items.example: The noun kept both the page and the arithmetic senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时保留书页与算术两义。

items.example: The suffix makes the comparison adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成比较副词。

items.example: The suffix names the condition of being at the edge.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「处于边缘」的状况。

items.example: The suffix names the act of pushing to the edge.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「推到边缘」的动作。

items.example: The suffix names the process as a whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名整个过程。

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 margo，义为「页边；差额」
由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「略微」
由该形容词加性质名词后缀构成，义为「边缘性」
由该形容词加「使……化」的动词后缀构成，义为「使边缘化」
由「使边缘化」加动作名词后缀构成，义为「边缘化」

definition_zh: 质地；纹理；口感；（音乐、文字的）肌理；织物结构
definition_en: the feel or visible grain of a surface; the way a material or a piece of music or writing is woven together
core_image: 一块布被手指反复摩过，经纬线一高一低，光斜着照过来，表面因此有了起伏
scene: 陶艺工作台上摆着一只刚出窑的粗陶碗，指尖抚过釉面上一圈圈细密的起伏， She runs her thumb along the rim to feel the texture of the glaze.
sceneCN: 这里 texture 指「手触摸到的表面质地」（第 1 个义项：触摸所感的表面质感）；句意为她让拇指沿碗口滑过，去感受釉面的质地。图中可辨识物件：粗陶碗、带细密起伏的釉面、工作台与握着碗的手指。

pos.zh: 使具有某种质感；给……加纹理

senses.title: The feel of a surface under the hand
senses.definition: the way a surface feels when touched, especially its roughness, smoothness or grain
senses.definitionCN: 表面被触摸时的感觉，尤指其粗糙、光滑或颗粒感
senses.example: The texture of the stone wall is rough under her palm.
senses.exampleCN: 石墙的质地在她掌心下显得粗糙。
senses.why: Latin textura meant 'weaving' and 'fabric'; the hand reading a surface repeats the action of fingers reading cloth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 textura 意为「编织、织物」；手去读一块表面，重复的正是手指读布的动作。

senses.title: The visible grain of a surface
senses.definition: the visual quality of a surface as shown by small variations of light, colour or relief
senses.definitionCN: 表面因光线、色彩或凹凸的细微变化而呈现的视觉性质
senses.example: The painter builds texture with short, thick strokes of paint.
senses.exampleCN: 画家用短而厚的笔触堆出纹理。
senses.why: The sense moves from touch to sight: the eye learns to read the same small variations that the fingers feel.
senses.whyCN: 词义从触觉转向视觉：眼睛学会读取手指所感到的同一批细微变化。

senses.title: The woven structure of cloth
senses.titleCN: 织物由纱线交织而成的结构
senses.definition: the way threads are woven together in a fabric, producing its weight and drape
senses.definitionCN: 织物中纱线交织的方式，决定其重量与垂感
senses.example: The coat's heavy texture comes from tightly woven wool.
senses.exampleCN: 这件大衣厚重的质地来自织得紧密的羊毛。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: textura named the act and result of weaving before it named the feel of anything else.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：textura 先指编织的动作与结果，后来才指其他事物的手感。

senses.title: The feel of food in the mouth
senses.definition: the physical quality of food as felt in the mouth, such as creaminess, crunch or grain
senses.definitionCN: 食物在口中被感受到的物理性质，如细腻、酥脆或颗粒感
senses.example: The soup has a silky texture that comes from slow cooking.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤有丝滑的口感，来自长时间的慢煮。
senses.why: The mouth takes over from the hand: chewing and pressing give the same report about grain and resistance.
senses.whyCN: 口取代了手：咀嚼与挤压给出的，是关于颗粒与阻力的同一份报告。

senses.title: The characteristic quality of a sound or a piece of writing
senses.titleCN: 声音或文字特有的质感
senses.definition: the overall character of a sound, a voice or a piece of writing, considered as a fabric of detail
senses.definitionCN: 声音、嗓音或文字整体的特质，被视为由细节织成的织物
senses.example: The cello's low notes give the passage a dark texture.
senses.exampleCN: 大提琴的低音给这段音乐一种暗沉的质感。
senses.why: A voice or a page also has grain: details are woven together, and the ear or reader judges the weave rather than any single thread.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音或书页也有颗粒：细节被织在一起，耳朵或读者评判的是织法，而非某一根线。

senses.title: The interweaving of parts in music
senses.definition: in music, the way voices or instrumental parts are combined and layered across a piece
senses.definitionCN: 音乐中各个嗓音或器乐声部在一首作品里结合与分层的方式
senses.example: The composer thins the texture in the second movement.
senses.exampleCN: 作曲家在第二乐章把织体减薄。
senses.why: Music theory borrows the weaving image literally: separate lines cross and support each other like warp and weft.
senses.whyCN: 音乐理论直接借用了编织的意象：各条线像经线与纬线那样交错、彼此支撑。

senses.title: The grain and structure of a material
senses.titleCN: 材料的颗粒与内部结构
senses.definition: in geology and materials, the size, shape and arrangement of grains that make up a rock, soil or solid
senses.definitionCN: 地质学与材料学中构成岩石、土壤或固体的颗粒大小、形状与排列方式
senses.example: The soil's sandy texture lets water drain quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 这土壤的砂质结构让水很快排走。
senses.why: Science narrows the word to what can be measured: the grains and their arrangement replace the subjective feel.
senses.whyCN: 科学把词义收窄到可测量的部分：颗粒及其排列取代了主观手感。

senses.title: A mapped surface image in computer graphics
senses.titleCN: 计算机图形中贴到表面的图像
senses.definition: in computer graphics, an image wrapped over a three-dimensional surface to give it detail
senses.definitionCN: 计算机图形学中包覆在三维表面上、为其增加细节的图像
senses.example: The game renders a wood texture on every table in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 游戏给房间里的每张桌子渲染了木纹贴图。
senses.why: A digital surface needs the same information the hand once supplied, so an image is stretched over the model and called a texture.
senses.whyCN: 数字表面需要的信息与手曾经提供的一样，于是把一张图铺展到模型上，并称之为纹理。

intro.en: Texture comes from Latin textura 'weaving, fabric', a noun built on texere 'to weave'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: texture 来自拉丁语 textura「编织、织物」，由动词 texere「编织」构成的名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Texere meant 'to weave, to plait, to construct'. Its deeper root is generally reconstructed as *teks- 'to weave, to make', which is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: texere 意为「编织、编结、构造」。其更深的词根一般认为可重构为 *teks-「编织、制作」，这属于重构形式，而非实际书证。

items.en: The suffix -ura named the result of an action, so textura was 'a weaving, a fabric, a woven thing'.
items.cn: 后缀 -ura 表示动作的结果，因此 textura 指「编织、织物、织成之物」。

items.en: The same verb produced textus, 'something woven', which later gave English text; cloth and text share one image.
items.cn: 同一个动词还产生 textus「织成之物」，后来进入英语成为「文本」；布与文本共享同一个意象。

items.en: English took texture in the fifteenth century, generally through Old French, where it still named woven cloth.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪接受 texture，一般认为经由古法语传入，当时仍指织成的布。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the word had moved from cloth to any surface, and touch rather than the loom became the point of reference.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，这个词已从布匹扩展到任何表面，参照点也从织机变成了触摸。

items.en: Source uncertain: whether the first English uses came straight from Latin or through French is not fully established; the French route is generally assumed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语最早的用法是直接取自拉丁语，还是经由法语，尚无定论；一般认为走的是法语路径。

note.en: The first group holds words that look close to texture and come from the same weaving verb but name different things; the second holds words about surface and material quality that differ in focus.
note.cn: 第一组是外形接近、同出编织动词但所指不同的词；第二组指表面与材料性质，在关注点上有别。

entries.definition: Written material; it comes from the same Latin verb texere 'to weave', since a text is a woven thing, but it names words rather than a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 文字材料；出自同一拉丁动词 texere「编织」，因为文本本是被织成之物，但它指文字而非表面。

entries.definition: Cloth or fabric, the original product that textura named; it stays with woven material and does not extend to feel in general.
entries.definitionCN: 布料或织物，正是 textura 最初所指的产物；它停留在编织材料，不扩展到一般手感。

entries.definition: Relating to written text; it belongs to text, not to the feel or grain of a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 与书面文本有关的；它属于 text，而不属于表面的手感或纹理。

entries.definition: The direction and size of fibres or particles in wood, stone or cloth; grain is one cause of texture, not the whole impression.
entries.definitionCN: 木材、石料或布中纤维与颗粒的方向和大小；颗粒只是质地的成因之一，并不等于整体印象。

entries.definition: The final treatment given to a surface, such as matte or gloss; finish names the treatment, texture names the result as felt.
entries.definitionCN: 表面最后的处理方式，如哑光或高光；finish 指处理，texture 指被感受到的结果。

entries.definition: The general impression a surface gives to the hand; a plainer word than texture and often used in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 表面对手给出的总体印象；比 texture 更朴素，多用于口语。

entries.definition: The firmness or thickness of a substance, especially food or paint; it describes body rather than surface detail.
entries.definitionCN: 物质的浓稠或坚实程度，尤用于食物或颜料；它描述的是稠度而非表面细节。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, the real word family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: Texere 'to weave' + -ura 'result' = the result of weaving, a fabric.
normal.cn: texere「编织」+ -ura「结果」= 编织的产物，也就是织物。

normal.en: Texture and textile are close relatives, both coming from the loom.
normal.cn: 「织体」与「纺织品」是近亲，都来自织机。

normal.en: The hand reads texture; the eye reads the same small pattern.
normal.cn: 手读质地，眼读的其实是同一小片纹样。

normal.en: A coarse cloth shows its texture as roughness, a fine one as even grain.
normal.cn: 粗布以粗糙显出其质地，细布则以匀净的颗粒显出质地。

normal.en: In graphics a texture is an image laid over a surface, like cloth over a table.
normal.cn: 在图形学里，纹理是铺在表面上的一张图，像把布盖在桌上。

abstract.en: Picture a single thread pulled out of a weave and laid across the page.
abstract.cn: 想象从织物里抽出一根线，横放在纸页上。

abstract.en: Picture fingertips as small readers that report the height of every bump.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖是小小的读者，逐一报告每个凸起的高度。

abstract.en: Picture a voice with grain, like cloth that is not flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一副带有颗粒的声音，像一块并不平顺的布。

examples.en: The old wooden table has a warm texture worn smooth by years of use.
examples.cn: 那张旧木桌有温润的质地，被多年使用磨得光滑。

examples.en: Add crushed nuts to the dessert for extra texture.
examples.cn: 在甜点里加入碎坚果，增添额外的口感。

examples.en: The novel's texture comes from many short scenes woven together.
examples.cn: 这部小说的肌理来自许多短场景交织在一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贴死扯」——手指贴上去，用力扯一扯布面，粗糙还是顺滑立刻知道，这就是质地。texere 是「编织」，织出来的东西表面自有纹路。

root: 拉丁语 textura「编织、织物」来自动词 texere「编织」；textura 由 texere 加表示动作结果的后缀 -ura 构成。英语经古法语借入，词义由织物结构扩展到任何表面的手感与可见纹理，并进一步用于音乐织体、材料颗粒与数字贴图。texere 更早的词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with the feel of a surface under the hand, then move to visible grain and the woven cloth that gave the word its name, to food and sound, to music and the grain of materials, and finally to the image mapped onto a digital surface.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从手触摸表面的感觉出发，转到可见纹理与给这个词命名的织物结构，再到食物与声音，再到音乐织体与材料颗粒，最后是贴到数字表面的图像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: threads cross and rise, so a surface carries a small repeated relief that the hand and the eye can both read.
core.cn: 核心意象：线交叉、起伏，表面因此带着细小的重复凹凸，手与眼都能读出来。

branches.en: THE CORE TOUCH: texture is first what the hand learns about a surface, its roughness or smoothness.
branches.cn: 核心触感：质地首先是手从表面得知的东西，是粗糙还是光滑。

branches.en: SIGHT AND WEAVE: the word keeps the woven structure of cloth and the visible grain of any surface, two readings of the same small pattern.
branches.cn: 视觉与编织：这个词既保留布的编织结构，也指任何表面的可见纹理，两者是同一小片纹样的两种读法。

branches.en: MOUTH AND EAR: food is judged by the same grain under the teeth, and a voice or a page is read as a fabric of details.
branches.cn: 口与耳：食物靠牙齿下的同一份颗粒感被评判，嗓音或书页则被读成由细节织成的布。

branches.en: THE WEAVE WIDENS: music combines lines like warp and weft, while geology measures the grains that make up a solid.
branches.cn: 织法变宽：音乐像经纬那样把线条结合起来，地质学则测量构成固体的颗粒。

branches.en: THE IMAGE ON THE SURFACE: a digital model receives a picture stretched over it, so the surface detail is supplied as an image.
branches.cn: 表面上的图像：数字模型被铺上一张图，表面细节于是以图像的方式供给。

intro.en: Texture can be read as a Latin verb, a Latin noun suffix and a Latin noun, with a small English adjective family built on top.
intro.cn: texture 可以读作一个拉丁动词、一个拉丁名词后缀和一个拉丁名词，再加上一小族英语形容词派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin texere 'to weave' with -ura 'result' produced textura 'fabric'; English borrowed it and later added -al and -ed for the adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 texere「编织」加 -ura「结果」构成 textura「织物」；英语借入后，又加两个形容词词尾构成形容词。

items.structure: texere, texui, textum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.meaning: to weave, to plait, to construct
items.example: The verb supplies the action behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供整个词族的动作来源。

items.meaning: the result or product of an action
items.example: The suffix turns the act of weaving into the thing woven.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把编织的动作变成织成之物。

items.example: Latin used the noun for cloth and for the way it was woven.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语用这个名词指布，也指它的织法。

items.meaning: the feel or grain of a surface; to give a surface such a quality
items.meaningCN: 表面的手感或纹理；使表面具有这种性质
items.example: English widened the noun from cloth to every surface.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个名词从布匹扩展到一切表面。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun of texture into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把表示质地的名词变成形容词。

items.example: Critics praise the textural richness of the painting.
items.exampleCN: 评论家称赞这幅画丰富的肌理。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of possession.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表示拥有的形容词。

items.example: The walls are textured with coarse plaster.
items.exampleCN: 墙面用粗灰泥做出了纹理。

derivatives.meaning: the noun of surface quality shifts to an adjective describing what belongs to texture
derivatives.meaningCN: 由表示表面性质的名词转为描述「属于质地」的形容词

derivatives.meaning: the noun shifts to an adjective meaning 'provided with a texture'
derivatives.meaningCN: 由名词转为形容词，表示「带有某种质地」

definition_zh: 组织的；组织结构的；组织管理的；活动筹备的；工会组织的；组织研究的；生物组织层次的；组织单元的；有组织能力的
definition_en: relating to an organization as a body, to the way its parts are arranged and managed, to the work of arranging an activity, or to a person's ability to put work in order
core_image: 把散乱的人和事装进一张画好的架构图，每一格都标明谁向谁报告
scene: 公司搬进新楼的第一天，行政把一张画满方框和向下箭头的图贴在走廊墙上，每个格子下面都写着负责人的名字。 The chart shows the organizational structure of each department.
sceneCN: 这里 organizational 是「组织结构的」（第 2 个义项：指机构内部层级与分工的排列方式）；句意：这张图显示每个部门的组织结构。

pos.zh: 组织的；组织结构的；组织管理的；有组织能力的

collocations.zh: 组织能力；统筹安排的能力

senses.title: Of the body as a body
senses.definition: relating to an organization as a whole, rather than to one member, one department, or one activity
senses.definitionCN: 指某个组织整体，而不是其中某个成员、某个部门或某项活动
senses.example: The merger changed the organizational name but left the staff in place.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并改掉了组织名称，却把人员原样留了下来。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun organization into a describing word. It points at the body as a body, the way a label on a pen points at the pen rather than at the animals inside it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把名词 organization 变成形容词。它指的是作为一个整体的机构，就像圈栏上的牌子指的是圈栏本身，而不是里面的牲畜。

senses.title: How the parts are arranged
senses.titleCN: 指内部层级与分工排列的
senses.definition: relating to the structure of an organization, especially the way roles, units, and levels are arranged under one another
senses.definitionCN: 指机构的内部结构，尤其是角色、单元与层级之间上下排列的方式
senses.example: A flat organizational structure puts few layers between the intern and the director.
senses.exampleCN: 扁平的组织结构让实习生和总监之间只隔很少的层级。
senses.why: The Greek source organon was a tool whose parts work together. Once the tool becomes a body of people, the adjective can describe the arrangement of those parts.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源 organon 是一件各部分协同工作的工具。当这件工具变成一个由人组成的机构后，这个形容词就可以描述各部分如何排列。

senses.title: Of management and administration
senses.definition: relating to management, decision-making, and the daily running of an organization rather than to its technical work
senses.definitionCN: 指管理、决策与机构日常运转，而不是指机构所做的技术性工作
senses.example: The audit blamed organizational failures rather than individual dishonesty.
senses.exampleCN: 审计把问题归因于管理层面的失误，而不是个人的不诚实。
senses.why: Management is the hand that holds the tool. This sense marks whatever belongs to that hand — budgets, chains of approval, reporting lines — as opposed to the work the tool is meant to do.
senses.whyCN: 管理是握着这件工具的手。这个义项标记的是属于这只手的东西——预算、审批链、汇报线——而不是工具本身要完成的工作。

senses.title: Of arranging an event or task
senses.definition: relating to the work of planning and arranging people or things so that an activity can take place
senses.definitionCN: 指为了让某项活动得以举行而规划、安排人与物的那部分工作
senses.example: The festival's organizational work began nine months before the first ticket was sold.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐节的筹备工作在第一张票卖出前九个月就开始了。
senses.why: Here the adjective points back to the verb organize. It names the labour of drawing the chart, not the body that appears once the chart is drawn.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词回指的是动词 organize。它命名的是画这张架构图的劳作，而不是图画好之后出现的那个机构。

senses.title: Of organized labour
senses.definition: relating to a trade union, or to workers acting together as one body in negotiations
senses.definitionCN: 指工会，或指工人在谈判中以一个整体共同行动的
senses.example: Organizational membership in the union rose sharply after the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工之后，工会的组织成员人数大幅上升。
senses.why: A union is an organization in the plainest sense: workers gathered into one body. The adjective keeps that collective meaning and attaches it to labour rather than to management.
senses.whyCN: 工会是最字面意义上的组织：工人聚合成一个整体。这个形容词保留了这层集体含义，并把它挂到劳工一方，而不是管理层。

senses.title: Of organizational studies
senses.definition: relating to the academic study of how organizations behave, as in organizational psychology, organizational behaviour, and organizational theory
senses.definitionCN: 指对机构如何运作的学术研究，如组织心理学、组织行为学与组织理论
senses.example: She teaches organizational behaviour to first-year management students.
senses.exampleCN: 她给管理专业一年级学生讲授组织行为学。
senses.why: When a field takes the body itself as its object, the adjective enters the field's name. The subject is no longer how to run the tool but the regular patterns the tool shows.
senses.whyCN: 当一门学科把机构本身当作研究对象时，这个形容词就进入了学科名称。研究对象不再是怎样使用这件工具，而是这件工具呈现出的规律。

senses.title: Of levels of biological organization
senses.definition: relating to the nested levels at which living matter is arranged, from molecules and cells up to organs and ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 指生命物质由分子、细胞一直嵌套到器官与生态系统的各个层次
senses.example: Ecologists work at organizational levels above the single organism.
senses.exampleCN: 生态学家研究的是单个生物体以上的组织层次。
senses.why: Biology kept the literal sense of organon: organs are the body's tools. The adjective then names the ladder of parts nested inside larger parts, which is the chart drawn by nature.
senses.whyCN: 生物学保留了 organon 的字面义：器官是身体的工具。这个形容词于是命名部分嵌套在更大整体里的阶梯，也就是大自然自己画出的那张架构图。

senses.title: Of a unit inside a system
senses.definition: relating to a named subdivision inside a computer directory or an administrative filing system
senses.definitionCN: 指计算机目录或行政档案体系中被命名的下级单元
senses.example: Create one organizational unit for each regional office in the directory.
senses.exampleCN: 在目录里为每个地区办事处建立一个组织单元。
senses.why: Software imitates the chart literally: an organizational unit is a box drawn inside a larger box. Here the word names a container in a hierarchy rather than a group of people.
senses.whyCN: 软件把架构图照字面模仿了一遍：组织单元就是画在更大方框里的一个方框。这里这个词命名的是层级中的一个容器，而不是一群真实的人。

senses.title: Good at putting things in order
senses.definition: of a person, able to plan and arrange work so that many parts move in order without confusion
senses.definitionCN: 指人能够规划并安排工作，使许多部分有序推进而不混乱
senses.example: Her organizational ability kept the archive from collapsing into piles.
senses.exampleCN: 她的统筹能力让档案室没有塌成一堆堆纸山。
senses.why: The adjective moves from the thing to the person who makes the thing. A skill is called organizational when it produces the chart in real life, with boxes that actually report to the boxes above them.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从事物转到了制造事物的人身上。当一种本领能在现实里画出那张图、并且方框真的向它上面的方框汇报时，它就被称为组织能力。

intro.en: Organizational is the adjective of organization, built with the Latin suffix -alis (English -al). Organization comes from Medieval Latin organizatio, an action noun from organizare 'to organize', which rests on Latin organum 'instrument, implement, organ of the body'. Organum itself was borrowed from Greek organon 'tool, implement, organ', a derivative of ergon 'work'. The path is therefore 'tool' → 'body part that works like a tool' → 'parts arranged to work together' → 'an institution' → the English adjective.
intro.cn: organizational 是 organization 的形容词，由拉丁后缀 -alis（英语 -al）构成。organization 来自中世纪拉丁语 organizatio，是 organizare“组织”的动作名词，而 organizare 的基础是拉丁语 organum“工具、器具、身体器官”。organum 本身借自希腊语 organon“工具、器具、器官”，由 ergon“工作”派生。因此整条路径是“工具”→“像工具一样工作的身体部件”→“被安排协同工作的各部分”→“机构”→英语形容词。

items.en: Organon means 'tool, instrument, implement' and also 'organ of the body'. It derives from ergon 'work, deed', the same root that gives English energy and ergonomic.
items.cn: organon 意为“工具、器具、器械”，也指“身体器官”。它由 ergon“工作、行为”派生，同一词根还产生英语的 energy 与 ergonomic。

items.en: Latin borrowed organon as organum, widened it to 'musical instrument', and formed the verb organizare in medieval use, 'to furnish with organs, to arrange into a working body'.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 organon 借作 organum，词义扩大到“乐器”，并在中世纪用法中造出动词 organizare，意为“装备器官、安排成一个能运转的整体”。

items.en: English organization first names the act of organizing and the state of being organized; the sense 'an organized body of persons, an institution' is established in the 17th century.
items.cn: 英语 organization 最初指“组织的行为”和“被组织起来的状态”；“由人组成的组织、机构”这一义项在 17 世纪确立。

items.en: The adjective organizational appears in the 19th century, at first in the language of institutions and administration, then spreading to psychology, biology, and computing in the 20th.
items.cn: 形容词 organizational 出现在 19 世纪，最初用于机构与行政语言，20 世纪又扩展到心理学、生物学与计算机领域。

items.en: The family is regular: organ + -ize (from Greek -izein through Latin -izare) makes the verb, -ation makes the action noun, -al makes the adjective, and -ally the adverb. Reorganization adds re- 'again'.
items.cn: 这个词族的构词很规则：organ 加 -ize（经拉丁 -izare 上溯希腊 -izein）构成动词，加 -ation 构成动作名词，加 -al 构成形容词，加 -ally 构成副词。reorganization 则再加 re-“再次”。

items.en: Organic and organism share the same organon root but took the 'living body' branch. By contrast, ornament comes from Latin ornare 'to adorn', and its orn- has nothing to do with organ-; the two only share a few letters at the front.
items.cn: organic 与 organism 共享同一个 organon 词根，只是走了“活体”这一支。相反，ornament 来自拉丁语 ornare“装饰”，其中的 orn- 与 organ- 毫无关系，两者只是词头碰巧相似。

note.en: The first group follows the organon root from tool to body part to institution, and separates one word that only looks similar. The second group compares the adjectives learners use when they mean 'about an institution' or 'about running it'.
note.cn: 第一组沿着 organon 词根，从工具走到身体部件再到机构，并区分一个只是形近的词。第二组比较学习者在表示“关于机构”或“关于管理”时最常替换的几个形容词。

entries.definition: a part of the body that performs a special function, or a musical instrument. It is the literal organon, the tool of the body, from which the institution sense grew.
entries.definitionCN: 身体中执行特定功能的部件，或指乐器。它就是字面的 organon——身体的工具，机构义正是从这里长出来的。

entries.definition: relating to living things or to food grown without chemicals. It follows the 'organ of the body' branch of organon rather than the 'arranged institution' branch.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物有关，或指不用化学物质种植的食物。它走的是 organon 中“身体器官”那一支，而不是“被安排好的机构”那一支。

entries.definition: the act of arranging parts into a working whole, or the body so formed. The adjective adds -al to this noun and simply means 'of such a body'.
entries.definitionCN: 把各部分安排成一个能运转的整体的行为，或由此形成的机构。形容词只是在名词后加 -al，表示“属于这种机构的”。

entries.definition: a decorative object. Its root is Latin ornare 'to adorn', so the orn- resembles organ- only in spelling and shares no meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰品。它的词根是拉丁语 ornare“装饰”，所以 orn- 只在拼写上像 organ-，意义上毫无关联。

entries.definition: relating to a long-established body such as a university, bank, or hospital, often stressing its formal, slow-moving character. Organizational is neutral and can describe any body, including a new one.
entries.definitionCN: 指大学、银行、医院这类长期存在的机构，常强调其正式、迟缓的特征。organizational 是中性的，可以描述任何机构，包括刚成立的。

entries.definition: relating to the work of managing records, rules, and procedures. Organizational can cover culture, structure, and psychology as well as administration.
entries.definitionCN: 指管理记录、规则与程序的工作。organizational 除行政外，还可以涵盖文化、结构与心理层面。

entries.definition: relating to managers and their duties. It names one rank inside the body, while organizational can describe the whole body or its arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指管理者及其职责。它命名机构内部的一个层级，而 organizational 可以描述整个机构或其排列方式。

entries.definition: relating to a business corporation, often with a tone of large-scale commercial identity. Organizational is wider and applies to schools, charities, and unions too.
entries.definitionCN: 指商业公司，常带大型商业主体的语气。organizational 范围更广，也适用于学校、慈善机构与工会。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: organon 'tool', ergon 'work', the -ize/-ation/-al chain, the organ that gives the family its name, and the ornare trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：organon“工具”、ergon“工作”、-ize/-ation/-al 词缀链、给整个词族命名的 organ，以及 ornare 陷阱。

normal.en: Organon is Greek for 'tool'; an organization is a tool made of people, and organizational describes whatever belongs to that tool.
normal.cn: organon 是希腊语“工具”；organization 是一件由人做成的工具，organizational 则描述属于这件工具的一切。

normal.en: Organon comes from ergon 'work', the root behind energy: a tool is what does work, and an institution is a tool that does work through people.
normal.cn: organon 出自 ergon“工作”，也就是 energy 的词根：工具就是干活的东西，而机构是通过人来干活的工具。

normal.en: The suffixes stack in order: organ → organize (verb) → organization (noun) → organizational (adjective) → organizationally (adverb).
normal.cn: 后缀按顺序叠加：organ → organize（动词）→ organization（名词）→ organizational（形容词）→ organizationally（副词）。

normal.en: An organ is a body part that works like a tool; the same word moved from the body to the body of people, which is why 'organizational structure' sounds anatomical.
normal.cn: organ 是像工具一样工作的身体部件；同一个词从身体挪到了人的集合体，所以 organizational structure 听起来像在讲解剖。

normal.en: Ornament looks close but comes from ornare 'to adorn'; a decoration adds beauty, while an organization adds order.
normal.cn: ornament 看起来相近，但出自 ornare“装饰”；装饰增添美，而组织增添秩序。

abstract.en: A chart on a wall is only ink, yet people arrive at nine and leave at six because the boxes on it agree with one another.
abstract.cn: 墙上的架构图只是墨水，可人们九点来、六点走，只因图上的方框彼此对得上。

abstract.en: An orchestra needs a score, chairs, and a conductor; none of them makes music, but together they let the players do it.
abstract.cn: 管弦乐团需要总谱、座椅和指挥；这些东西都不演奏音乐，但合在一起才让乐手奏出音乐。

abstract.en: A library's shelf numbers do not read the books, but without them no reader finds a book; structure is invisible work.
abstract.cn: 图书馆的架号不读任何一本书，但没有它读者就找不到书；结构是一种看不见的劳动。

examples.en: The study found that organizational culture mattered more than pay.
examples.cn: 研究发现，组织文化比薪酬更重要。

examples.en: She was praised for her organizational skills during the conference.
examples.cn: 会议期间，她的统筹安排能力受到了称赞。

examples.en: The software stores each department as a separate organizational unit.
examples.cn: 该软件把每个部门存成一个独立的组织单元。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥格耐贼」——奥格把散乱的人“摁”进一张格子图，一人一格，谁向谁汇报都写清楚 → organizational 组织结构的；有组织能力的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 organizare「组织」，基础是 organum「工具、器官」，再上溯希腊语 organon「工具、器官」，由 ergon「工作」派生；后缀为 -ation 与 -al。核心是「把散开的部件装成一件能干活的工具」。同族的 organic、organism 走“活体”一支，ornament（ornare「装饰」）只是形近，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of organizational all point at one drawing: scattered people and tasks fitted into a chart. What shifts is where the eye lands — on the body itself, on the lines between its boxes, on the hand that draws them, or on the skill of drawing.
sensesIntro.cn: organizational 的九个义项都指向同一张图：散乱的人与任务被装进一张架构图。变化的是视线落点——落在机构本身、落在方框之间的连线、落在画图的那只手上，还是落在画图的本领上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered people and tasks fitted into a drawn chart, each box marked with the box it reports to.
core.cn: 核心意象：散乱的人与任务被装进一张画好的架构图，每个方框都标明它向哪个方框汇报。

chain: A BODY THAT ACTS AS ONE
AND THE SKILL OF DRAWING IT

branches.en: THE BODY AND ITS LINES: the institution as a whole, and the hierarchy of roles and units inside it.
branches.cn: 机构与连线：作为整体的机构，以及其内部角色与单元的层级。

branches.en: THE HAND: management and administration, and the planning labour that arranges an event before it happens.
branches.cn: 那只手：管理与行政，以及活动发生之前的筹备劳作。

branches.en: THE COLLECTIVE BRANCH: workers gathered into a union, the body as a bargaining unit.
branches.cn: 集体分支：工人聚成工会，机构成为谈判单位。

branches.en: THE STUDY OF THE BODY: organizational psychology, behaviour, and theory take the chart itself as the object.
branches.cn: 对机构的研究：组织心理学、组织行为学与组织理论把这张图本身当作研究对象。

branches.en: NESTED AND PERSONAL: levels of biological organization, a unit inside a directory, and the personal skill that produces order.
branches.cn: 嵌套与个人：生物组织层次、目录中的组织单元，以及产生秩序的个人能力。

intro.en: Organizational is not a Latin word: it is English organization plus the Latin adjective ending -alis. The Latin core sits underneath, organum < Greek organon 'tool'. The family is built by regular suffix stacking rather than by new prefixes.
intro.cn: organizational 不是拉丁词：它是英语 organization 加拉丁形容词词尾 -alis。拉丁内核在其下方，即 organum < 希腊语 organon“工具”。这个词族靠规则的后缀叠加而建成，没有另加新前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer contains organum 'instrument', organizare 'to arrange into a working body', and organizatio 'arrangement'. Behind organum is Greek organon 'tool', from ergon 'work'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层包含 organum“工具”、organizare“安排成能运转的整体”、organizatio“安排”。organum 背后是希腊语 organon“工具”，再上溯 ergon“工作”。

items.meaning: of or belonging to an organized body
items.meaningCN: 属于某个被组织起来的机构的（-al 形容词后缀）
items.example: The organizational chart lists every reporting line.
items.exampleCN: 组织架构图列出了每一条汇报线。

items.meaning: the act of arranging parts, or the body so arranged
items.meaningCN: 安排各部分的行为，或由此形成的机构（-ation 动作／结果名词）
items.example: The organization has three regional offices.
items.exampleCN: 这个机构有三个地区办事处。

items.meaning: to furnish with parts and set them working together
items.meaningCN: 给事物配备部件并使其协同运转；组织（-ize 动词后缀）
items.example: They organized the files by year and by author.
items.exampleCN: 他们按年份和作者整理文件。

items.meaning: a person who arranges an event, or a container that keeps things in order
items.meaningCN: 安排活动的人，或使物品有条理的收纳盒（-er 施动者）
items.example: The conference organizer sent the schedule by email.
items.exampleCN: 会议组织者通过邮件发来了日程。

items.meaning: a body part with a special function, or a musical instrument
items.meaningCN: 有特定功能的器官，或乐器
items.example: The liver is the largest internal organ.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏是最大的内部器官。

items.meaning: of living bodies, or grown without chemical inputs
items.meaningCN: 与生物体有关的，或不用化学投入物种植的（-ic 形容词）
items.example: The farm sells organic vegetables.
items.exampleCN: 这个农场出售有机蔬菜。

items.meaning: in terms of the way an institution is arranged
items.meaningCN: 从机构安排的角度来说（-ly 副词后缀）
items.example: The two units are organizationally separate.
items.exampleCN: 这两个单位在组织上是分开的。

items.meaning: a fresh arranging of an existing body
items.meaningCN: 对现有机构重新进行安排；改组（re- 再次）
items.example: The reorganization merged two departments.
items.exampleCN: 这次改组把两个部门合并了。

items.meaning: lacking order, with parts not fitted together
items.meaningCN: 缺少秩序、各部分未配合好的（dis- 否定）
items.example: His desk was disorganized but his notes were exact.
items.exampleCN: 他的书桌很乱，笔记却很精确。

latinEntries.meaning: to furnish with organs, to arrange into a working body
latinEntries.meaningCN: 装备器官；安排成能运转的整体

latinEntries.meaning: an arranging, the state of being arranged
instrument, implement, musical instrument, organ of the body
latinEntries.meaningCN: 工具、器具、乐器、身体器官

definition_zh: 遵守；持续存在；居住
definition_en: the act of obeying a rule, continuing in a state, or dwelling somewhere
core_image: 一个人稳稳站在规则划出的圈内不动
scene: 质检员把手册翻到最后一页，合上了。 Compliance depends on the abidance of every workshop by the safety rules.
sceneCN: 这里 abidance 是「遵守」（第 1 个义项：依规行事）；句意为达标取决于每个车间对安全规则的遵守。

derivatives.zh: 词基动词，义为「遵守；忍受；持续；居住」
由现在分词转形容词，义为「持久的」
加否定前缀 non- 构成，义为「不遵守」

senses.title: Obedience to rules
senses.definition: the act of acting in accordance with a law, rule, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 依照法律、规则或协议行事的行为
senses.example: The contract requires abidance by all local regulations.
senses.exampleCN: 合同要求遵守所有地方性法规。
senses.why: To abide originally meant to wait or stand firm; keeping a rule is standing inside its lines.
senses.whyCN: abide 本义为等候、坚持；守规则就是在规则划出的线内站立不动。

senses.title: Continuance in a state
senses.definition: the fact of continuing in a condition, place, or office
senses.definitionCN: 在某种状态、地点或职位上继续存在
senses.example: His abidance in the chairmanship surprised the younger members.
senses.exampleCN: 他继续担任主席让年轻成员感到意外。
senses.why: The waiting sense grows into lasting; to stay put through time is to abide and its noun abidance.
senses.whyCN: 「等候」之义延伸为「持久」；在时间中停在原处，就是 abide，其名词即 abidance。

senses.title: Dwelling
senses.definition: the act of living or staying in a place, an older use
senses.definitionCN: 在某地生活或停留，属较旧用法
senses.example: Their abidance in the mountain village lasted thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在山村一住就是三十年。
senses.why: Standing firm in a rule and standing firm in a place share one verb; residence is only the place-shaped version.
senses.whyCN: 坚守规则与坚守一地共用同一个动词；居住只是其「场所化」的版本。

intro.en: Abidance is the noun of abide, an Old English verb for waiting and enduring, plus the noun ending -ance.
intro.cn: abidance 是 abide 的名词形式；abide 是古英语表示等候、忍受的动词，加名词后缀 -ance 构成。

items.en: A root meaning to wait or persist is reconstructed for the Germanic family.
items.cn: 日耳曼语族重构出一个意为等候、持续的词根。

items.en: Abidan meant to wait for, to endure, to remain.
items.cn: 古英语 abidan 意为等候、忍受、留下。

items.en: Abiten widened to dwelling and tolerating.
items.cn: 中古英语 abiten 扩展出居住与容忍之义。

items.en: Abidance was formed with the French-style suffix -ance.
items.cn: 近代英语以法语式后缀 -ance 构成 abidance。

items.en: The noun is now rare; abide by the rules lives on as a phrase.
items.cn: 如今该名词少见；abide by the rules 作为短语沿用。

note.en: Abidance stands with the abide family, whose members are far more common.
note.cn: abidance 与 abide 词族并列，该词族成员远比它常用。

entries.definition: the verb meaning to stay, endure, or obey
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为停留、忍受、遵守

entries.definition: lasting, as in abiding memory
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为持久的，如 abiding memory

entries.definition: a dwelling, the place-noun of the family
entries.definitionCN: 住所；该词族的场所名词

entries.definition: obedience to a rule
entries.definitionCN: 遵守；现代语域中最常用

entries.definition: the keeping of laws or customs
entries.definitionCN: 遵行；稍显正式

entries.definition: acting according to standards
entries.definitionCN: 符合；强调与标准一致

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abidance to the standing figure.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abidance 与站立不动的人绑在一起。

normal.en: abide + ance: the noun of standing firm.
normal.cn: abide ＋ ance：「坚持站立」的名词。

normal.en: abide by the rules is the living phrase.
normal.cn: 活着的是短语 abide by the rules。

normal.en: abiding memory: a memory that stays.
normal.cn: abiding memory：留得住的记忆。

normal.en: abode is the family's house word.
normal.cn: abode 是这个词族的「住所」词。

normal.en: Abidance itself sounds bookish and rare.
normal.cn: abidance 本身听上去书面且少见。

abstract.en: See chalk lines drawn on a courtroom floor.
abstract.cn: 看见法庭地板上画出的粉笔线。

abstract.en: Feel one foot planted through a long wait.
abstract.cn: 感到长久的等待中一只脚稳稳踏住。

abstract.en: Watch a flagpole holding through the storm.
abstract.cn: 看旗杆在风暴中纹丝不动。

examples.en: Award of the licence is conditional on abidance by the zoning rules.
examples.cn: 执照的颁发以遵守分区规划规则为条件。

examples.en: The treaty praised the abidance of both states by the ceasefire.
examples.cn: 条约赞扬两国对停火协议的遵守。

examples.en: Their long abidance in the old mill house became local legend.
examples.cn: 他们对老磨坊宅的长久居住成了当地传说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我白等死」——我宁可白等也不离开，坚守到底

root: 古英语 abidan「等候；忍受；留下」＝ a-（加强或方位前缀）＋ bidan「等候、期待」，出自原始日耳曼语重构词根「等候」。abidance 为近代英语以 -ance 后缀构成的名词化形式。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses keep one stance: standing within a rule, a state, or a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项保持同一种姿态：站在规则之内、状态之内、地点之内。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing inside a chalked circle, unmoved.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在粉笔圈内，纹丝不动。

branches.en: THE RULE LINE: obedience is standing inside the lines.
branches.cn: 规则之线：遵守就是站在线内。

branches.en: THE TIME LINE: continuance is standing through the years.
branches.cn: 时间之线：持续就是经年站立。

branches.en: THE PLACE LINE: dwelling is standing in one spot.
branches.cn: 地点之线：居住就是站在一处。

branches.en: FIRMNESS: both senses take the unyielding posture.
branches.cn: 坚定：这两个义项都取不肯退让的姿态。

branches.en: ONE STANCE: rule, time, and place are three frames of staying.
branches.cn: 同一姿态：规则、时间、地点是「停留」的三种框架。

intro.en: An Old English verb wears a French-style noun ending.
