definition_zh: 合同法；契约法
definition_en: the branch of law governing agreements that courts will enforce, including how they are formed, read and remedied
core_image: 两份对折的契约并排摊开，中间压着一枚印章，边缘用一条细线把双方连成一份可执行的义务
scene: 法学院把要约、承诺与违约救济编成一门课，学生先学契约如何成立。 The law school teaches offer, acceptance and remedies for breach as one course, so students first learn how contracts are formed under contract law.
sceneCN: 这里指「规范合同成立、解释与救济的法律部门」，对应第 1 个义项：关于契约的整体规则体系；句意为法学院把要约、承诺与违约救济编成一门课。画面要点：两份摊开的契约、中间的印章、连接双方的细线。

pos.zh: 合同法；契约法（不可数，作学科或法律部门名称）

derivatives.zh: 合同的；契约上的（名词加形容词后缀，指由合同约定或与合同有关的）
依合同地（形容词加副词后缀，指以合同条款为依据）
承包人；订约方（动词加表施事的名词后缀，指承接工程或服务的一方）
收缩；缩略（动词加表行为的名词后缀，语义由「拉到一起」转为「体积变小」或「词形缩短」）

senses.title: The branch governing enforceable agreements
senses.titleCN: 规范可执行协议的法律部门
senses.definition: the body of rules that decides which promises the law will enforce and what happens when they are broken
senses.definitionCN: 决定哪些承诺法律会强制执行、以及承诺被违反时如何处理的那套规则
senses.example: The law school teaches offer, acceptance and remedies for breach as one course, so students first learn how contracts are formed under contract law.
senses.exampleCN: 法学院把要约、承诺与违约救济编成一门课，学生先学合同法下契约如何成立。
senses.why: The phrase joins a word for drawing two parties into one bond with a word for laid-down rules, so the subject is the rules of that bond.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表示「把双方拉到一起」的词与表示「被定下的规则」的词连在一起，因此这门学科就是那种绑定的规则。

senses.title: How an agreement comes into being
senses.definition: the rules on offer and acceptance, and on the moment at which a binding agreement arises
senses.definitionCN: 关于要约与承诺、以及有约束力的协议在何时产生的规则
senses.example: A contract is formed when acceptance reaches the offeror.
senses.exampleCN: 承诺到达要约人时，合同即告成立。
senses.why: A bond needs two hands to tie it, so the subject begins with the exchange that turns two intentions into one obligation.
senses.whyCN: 一根绳子需要两只手来系，因此这门学科从那个把两个意图变成一个义务的交换开始。

senses.title: Consideration and cause
senses.definition: the requirement that each side give something in exchange, so that a promise is not a bare gift
senses.definitionCN: 要求双方各给出某种交换物，使承诺不只是一份空手赠予
senses.example: A promise without consideration is generally not enforceable in that system.
senses.exampleCN: 在该法系中，没有对价的承诺一般不可强制执行。
senses.why: Law will not bind a person who received nothing, so the doctrine asks what each hand put into the knot.
senses.whyCN: 法律不愿绑住一个什么也没得到的人，因此这一学说追问每只手在绳结里放了什么。

senses.title: Reading the words of the agreement
senses.definition: the rules courts use to decide what the words of a contract mean when the parties disagree
senses.definitionCN: 当事人发生分歧时，法院用来判定合同文字含义的规则
senses.example: The court applied the ordinary meaning rule of contract law.
senses.exampleCN: 法院适用了合同法中的通常含义规则。
senses.why: Once a bond is written, its words can be pulled in two directions, and the subject must supply a method for reading them.
senses.whyCN: 一旦绳子被写成文字，文字就可能被往两个方向拉扯，这门学科必须提供一种读法。

senses.title: Breach and the remedy
senses.definition: the rules on what counts as breaking a promise and what the injured party may recover
senses.definitionCN: 关于什么构成违反承诺、以及受害方可以取得何种补偿的规则
senses.example: Damages are the usual remedy for breach under contract law.
senses.exampleCN: 在合同法下，损害赔偿是违约的通常救济。
senses.why: A tie that cannot be broken without consequence is what makes the bond real, so remedy is the enforcement half of the subject.
senses.whyCN: 一根被扯断就要承担后果的绳子，才使绑缚成为真实，因此救济是这门学科的强制执行那一半。

senses.title: Defences that undo the bond
senses.definition: grounds such as fraud, duress, mistake or incapacity on which a party may escape the agreement
senses.definitionCN: 欺诈、胁迫、错误或无行为能力等理由，当事人可据此脱离协议
senses.example: Duress is a defence that removes the contract altogether.
senses.exampleCN: 胁迫是一种使合同整体失效的抗辩。
senses.why: A bond tied by a hand that was forced or deceived was not freely tied, so the subject must provide ways to untie it.
senses.whyCN: 被强迫或被欺骗的手系出的绳结并非自由系成，因此这门学科必须提供解开它的方式。

senses.title: Form and formalities
senses.definition: the cases in which writing, signature, seal or registration is required before an agreement binds
senses.definitionCN: 在哪些情形下协议须有书面、签名、盖章或登记才产生约束力
senses.example: Some sales require a written record as a formality of contract law.
senses.exampleCN: 某些买卖依合同法的形式要求须有书面记录。
senses.why: Some ties must be made in public to be trusted, so the subject keeps a list of knots that need witnesses or paper.
senses.whyCN: 有些绳结必须在人前系成才可信，因此这门学科保留了一份需要见证人或纸面的清单。

senses.title: Rules across borders
senses.definition: the international conventions and standard terms that govern agreements between parties in different countries
senses.definitionCN: 管束不同国家当事人之间协议的国际公约与标准条款
senses.example: Two firms in different states may choose a convention of contract law.
senses.exampleCN: 分处两国的两家公司可以选择适用某项合同公约。
senses.why: Trade crosses borders faster than legislatures write rules, so the subject acquires an international layer of agreed texts.
senses.whyCN: 贸易跨过国界的速度快于立法者写规则的速度，因此这门学科获得了一层国际商定的文本。

intro.en: Contract descends from Latin contrahere 'to draw together', built on trahere 'to draw'. Law comes from Old Norse lag 'something laid down', not from Latin. The compound is a modern name for a branch of private law.
intro.cn: contract 出自拉丁语 contrahere「拉到一起」，建立在 trahere「拉」之上。law 出自古诺尔斯语 lag「被放下的东西」，并非来自拉丁语。这个复合词是近代私法部门的名称。

items.en: Trahere 'to draw, pull' is the verb inside the word; the same root also underlies extract, attract and subtract.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖」，是这个词内部的动词；同一词根还支撑着「抽出」「吸引」与「减去」。

items.en: Contrahere joined the prefix for 'together' with trahere, literally 'to draw together', and it came to mean making an agreement between parties.
items.cn: contrahere 把表示「共同」的前缀与 trahere 结合，字面为「拉到一起」，后来指在双方之间订立协议。

items.en: Contractus, the past participle used as a noun, meant a drawing together and hence a compact or agreement.
items.cn: contractus 是作名词用的过去分词，意为「拉在一起」，因而指一项协议或约款。

items.en: Law descends from Old Norse lag 'something laid down', related to the verb lay; it replaced an older English word for law.
items.cn: law 出自古诺尔斯语 lag「被放下的东西」，与动词「放置」相关；它取代了英语中较早表示法律的那个词。

items.en: English joined the borrowed noun for agreement to the northern word for law, and the compound named the rules about agreements.
items.cn: 英语把借来的「协议」名词与北方传入的「法律」一词结合，这个复合词指关于协议的规则。

items.en: The phrase became the name of a teaching subject and a branch of private law in the nineteenth century. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 这个短语在十九世纪成为一门教学科目与私法分支的名称。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for drawing and has split into a noun, an agent and a quite different physical sense; the second group places the subject among neighbouring branches of law.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「拉」的拉丁动词，并分成名词、施事者与一个相当不同的物理义；第二组把这门学科放进相邻的法律分支中。

entries.definition: The agreement itself, or the verb meaning to enter such an agreement, and separately to shrink; the entry phrase names only the law about it.
entries.definitionCN: 协议本身，或表示订立协议的动词，另有「收缩」一义；本短语只指关于它的法律。

entries.definition: A person or firm that takes on a contract to do work; the ending marks the agent rather than the legal subject.
entries.definitionCN: 承接合同工作的人或公司；词尾标示施事者，而不是法律部门。

entries.definition: The process of shrinking, or a shortened word form; it keeps the literal image of drawing together.
entries.definitionCN: 收缩的过程，或缩略的词形；它保留了「拉到一起」的字面形象。

entries.definition: To break a rule or law; it is built on a different Latin verb and has no link to drawing a bargain.
entries.definitionCN: 违反规则或法律；它建立在另一个拉丁动词上，与「拉成交易」无关。

entries.definition: The field covering duties that arise from agreements and from wrongdoing; the entry phrase is one part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖由协议与不法行为产生的义务的领域；本短语只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: The branch dealing with civil wrongs independent of any agreement; it sits beside the entry phrase rather than inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 处理与协议无关的民事侵害的部门；它与本短语并列，而不在其内。

entries.definition: The law of trade, firms and transactions; it uses contract rules but also covers companies, credit and sale of goods.
entries.definitionCN: 关于贸易、企业与交易的法律；它使用合同规则，但也涵盖公司、信贷与货物买卖。

entries.definition: A written law passed by a legislature; contract rules may come from statutes or from case law, so the two terms are not equivalents.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关通过的成文法律；合同规则可能来自成文法或判例法，因此两者并不对等。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb for drawing together, the northern word for law, real derived words and real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「拉到一起」的动词、北方传入的「法律」一词、真实派生词与真实法律用语。

normal.en: The core picture is two hands pulling a single knot tight.
normal.cn: 核心画面是两只手把同一个绳结拉紧。

normal.en: The family runs contract, contractual, contractually, contractor and contraction.
normal.cn: 同族词包括合同、合同的、依合同地、承包人与收缩。

normal.en: The subject follows a bargain through four stages: formation, consideration, interpretation and remedy.
normal.cn: 这门学科把一笔交易走过四步：成立、对价、解释与救济。

normal.en: Law did not come from Latin; it came from the north and meant something laid down.
normal.cn: 表示法律的这个词并非来自拉丁语；它来自北方，意为「被放下的东西」。

normal.en: A promise with nothing given in return is the classic example of a bond the law will not enforce.
normal.cn: 没有任何回报的承诺，是法律不予强制执行的绑缚的典型例子。

abstract.en: Picture two sheets of paper joined by a single thread, and a seal sitting exactly where the thread crosses.
abstract.cn: 想象两张纸被一根细线连起，印章正压在线交叉的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a knot that can be untied only by showing that one hand was forced.
abstract.cn: 想象一个绳结，只有证明其中一只手是被强迫的，才能解开。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge of agreed words spanning two countries whose statutes never meet.
abstract.cn: 想象一座由商定文字搭成的桥，横跨两个法律从不相遇的国家。

examples.en: The case is studied in every introductory course on contract law.
examples.cn: 这个案例在每一门合同法入门课中都会被研读。

examples.en: Without consideration, the promise raises a question of contract law rather than of morality.
examples.cn: 没有对价时，这个承诺引出的是合同法问题，而不是道德问题。

examples.en: The two firms agreed to submit the dispute to a rule of contract law.
examples.cn: 两家公司同意把争议提交给某项合同规则处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捆得牢」——把双方捆在一起的约定，配上被定下的规矩，就是管着契约的那套法。

root: contract 出自拉丁语 contrahere「拉到一起」，由表示「共同」的前缀与 trahere「拉」构成，过去分词 contractus 指「协议」；law 出自古诺尔斯语 lag「被放下的东西」，与动词「放置」同源，属日耳曼语词。两者合成近代私法部门名称。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings follow one bargain from knot to courtroom. The branch itself comes first; then the making of the bond through offer and acceptance and consideration; then how its words are read and what form it must take; then breach and remedy, the defences that untie it, and finally the international layer that lets bargains cross borders.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一笔交易从绳结走到法庭。先是这门学科本身；其次是通过要约、承诺与对价把绳结系成；再其次是文字如何被解读、需要何种形式；然后是违约与救济、解开绳结的抗辩，最后是让交易跨越国界的国际层面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two signed sheets joined at a seal, each side held by the same thread.
core.cn: 核心意象：两份签名的纸在印章处连成一体，双方被同一根线系住。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: the body of rules that decides which promises the law will hold.
branches.cn: 学科本身：决定哪些承诺会被法律抓住的那套规则。

branches.en: FORMATION: the exchange of offer and acceptance, and the requirement that something be given on each side.
branches.cn: 成立：要约与承诺的交换，以及双方各须给出某物的要求。

branches.en: READING AND FORM: how the words are interpreted, and when paper, signature or seal is required.
branches.cn: 解读与形式：文字如何解释，以及何时需要纸面、签名或印章。

branches.en: REMEDY AND DEFENCE: what a broken promise costs, and the grounds that undo the bond entirely.
branches.cn: 救济与抗辩：违背承诺的代价，以及使绑缚整体失效的理由。

branches.en: ACROSS BORDERS: conventions and standard terms for parties in different countries.
branches.cn: 跨境：为不同国家当事人准备的公约与标准条款。

intro.en: Two different histories meet: a Latin verb for drawing, which supplies the agreement half, and a Norse word for what is laid down, which supplies the law half.
intro.cn: 两段不同的历史在此相遇：一个表示「拉」的拉丁动词提供「协议」那一半，一个古诺尔斯语中表示「被放下之物」的词提供「法律」那一半。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below belong to the agreement half only; the law half is Germanic and has no Latin source in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式只属于「协议」那一半；「法律」那一半属日耳曼语，在这个家族中没有拉丁语来源。

items.meaningCN: 把一个数从另一个数中减去
items.example: Subtract the costs from the revenue.

definition_zh: 五重奏；五重唱；五人一组；五件一套
definition_en: a group of five performers, or a piece written for five
core_image: 五把椅子围成半圆，五个人各自拿着乐器，等着同一个起拍
scene: 小剧场的舞台上摆了五把椅子，五个人准备合奏一支曲子。 Five chairs stood on the small stage, and the group was about to play a quintet.
sceneCN: 这里 quintet 指五重奏（第 1 个义项：五人合奏的乐曲）；句意为小剧场的舞台上摆了五把椅子，五个人准备合奏一支曲子。

pos.zh: 五重奏；五重唱；五人一组；五件一套

senses.title: A string quintet
senses.definition: a piece written for five string players
senses.definitionCN: 为五名弦乐手写的作品
senses.example: Five chairs stood on the small stage, and the group was about to play a quintet.
senses.exampleCN: 小舞台上摆着五把椅子，五个人准备合奏一首五重奏。
senses.why: The first sense is a musical work, not the players.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项是音乐作品，而不是演奏者。

senses.title: A jazz quintet
senses.definition: five jazz musicians who play as one band
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个乐队演奏的五名爵士乐手
senses.example: The jazz quintet toured for a decade without changing a member.
senses.exampleCN: 这支爵士五重奏巡演十年，成员一个没换。
senses.why: The same word names the group when used of people.
senses.whyCN: 指人时，同一个词命名的是团体。

senses.title: A quintet of singers
senses.definition: five voices trained to blend
senses.definitionCN: 五个训练有素、彼此融合的嗓音
senses.example: The quintet of singers held the last chord for a full breath.
senses.exampleCN: 五人合唱组把最后一个和弦拖了整整一口气。
senses.why: Voice replaces instruments, the count stays.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音替换了乐器，数目不变。

senses.title: A quintet of dancers
senses.definition: five dancers whose steps depend on one another
senses.definitionCN: 五个彼此依存完成舞步的舞者
senses.example: The quintet of dancers moved as a single body.
senses.exampleCN: 五人舞群像一具身体那样移动。
senses.why: The word extends beyond music to any five-part group.
senses.whyCN: 这个词越过音乐，指任何五人组合。

senses.title: The starting quintet
senses.definition: the five players who begin a basketball game
senses.definitionCN: 篮球比赛开场的五名球员
senses.example: The coach changed the starting quintet after three losses.
senses.exampleCN: 三连败之后，教练换掉了首发五人。
senses.why: Sport borrows the musical number word.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了这个音乐数字词。

senses.title: A quintet of problems
senses.definition: a set of five things considered together
senses.definitionCN: 被放在一起考虑的五件事
senses.example: The report listed a quintet of failures in the same paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 报告在同一段里列出了五个一组的问题。
senses.why: The word can count anything, not only performers.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以数任何东西，不只是表演者。

senses.title: A quintet in chamber music
senses.definition: the specific form with five parts and no conductor
senses.definitionCN: 五个声部、没有指挥的特定形式
senses.example: Chamber music treats the quintet as a conversation of equals.
senses.exampleCN: 室内乐把五重奏当作一场平等的对话。
senses.why: The sense is technical and refers to the form.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是技术性的，指这种形式。

senses.title: Versus quartet
senses.definition: five, as opposed to four, in the same musical frame
senses.definitionCN: 同样音乐框架里的五，与四相对
senses.example: A quartet leaves one fewer voice to answer.
senses.exampleCN: 与四重奏相比，五重奏少了一个应答的声部。
senses.why: The pair marks one added voice and a different balance.
senses.whyCN: 这一对词标记多出的一个声部与不同的平衡。

intro.en: Quintet comes from Italian quintetto, built on Latin quintus, 'fifth'.
intro.cn: quintet 来自意大利语 quintetto，词根是拉丁语 quintus（第五）。

items.en: Quintus was the ordinary word for fifth.
items.cn: quintus 是拉丁语里普通的「第五」。

items.en: Italian named a group of five in music.
items.cn: 意大利语命名音乐中的五人组合。

items.en: English borrowed the term for chamber works.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词指室内乐作品。

items.en: Jazz kept the label for five-piece bands.
items.cn: 爵士乐沿用它指五人乐队。

items.en: Today it names any five-part set.
items.cn: 今天它命名任何五件一套。

note.en: The look-alike group is the quint- family; the near-meaning group separates quartet, trio, ensemble and sextet.
note.cn: 形近组是 quint 词族；近义组把「四重奏」「三重奏」「合奏团」「六重奏」分开。

entries.definitionCN: 统计上的五个切点之一。

entries.definition: one of five born together.
entries.definitionCN: 五胞胎之一。

entries.definitionCN: 三人或三件的组合。

entries.definition: a group performing together.
entries.definitionCN: 一起表演的团体。

entries.definition: a group of six.
entries.definitionCN: 六人一组。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of five chairs set in a half circle.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「五把椅子围成半圆」的画面。

normal.en: Quintet carries quint, five: count the chairs before you listen.
normal.cn: quintet 里有 quint（五）：听之前先数椅子。

normal.en: Picture five musicians waiting for the same downbeat.
normal.cn: 想象五名乐手在等同一个起拍。

normal.en: Say kwin-TET; the stress falls on the last syllable.
normal.cn: 读 kwin-TET，重音在最后一个音节。

normal.en: The -et ending marks a group, as in quartet and trio's cousin sextet.
normal.cn: 词尾 -et 标记一个团体，如同 quartet 与 sextet。

normal.en: The word can count singers, dancers or even problems.
normal.cn: 这个词可以数歌手、舞者，甚至问题。

abstract.en: A quintet is a small democracy: five voices, no conductor.
abstract.cn: 五重奏是一个小型的民主：五个声部，没有指挥。

abstract.en: Adding a fifth player changes the conversation more than the arithmetic suggests.
abstract.cn: 增加第五个演奏者，对对话的改变大于算术所暗示的。

abstract.en: The word turns a number into a social form.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一个数字变成一种社会形式。

examples.en: The jazz quintet toured for a decade without changing a member.
examples.cn: 这支爵士五重奏巡演十年，成员一个没换。

examples.en: The quintet of singers held the last chord for a full breath.
examples.cn: 五人合唱组把最后一个和弦拖了整整一口气。

examples.en: The coach changed the starting quintet after three losses.
examples.cn: 三连败之后，教练换掉了首发五人。

dict_mnemonic.text: quint（五）+ et（小团体）→ 五个人组成的小团体。

root: 拉丁语 quintus（第五）→ 意大利语 quintetto

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses count five in different rooms: strings, jazz, voices, dancers, a basketball court, a list, chamber form and the contrast with four.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在不同的房间里数到五：弦乐、爵士、人声、舞者、篮球场、清单、室内乐形式，以及与四的对照。

core.en: FIVE CHAIRS IN A HALF CIRCLE
core.cn: 半圆里的五把椅子

branches.en: The written work and the chamber form.
branches.cn: 写成的作品与室内乐形式。

branches.en: Bands of instruments and of voices.
branches.cn: 乐器与人声的组合。

branches.en: Dancers and a starting five on court.
branches.cn: 舞者与球场上的首发五人。

branches.en: Any set of five considered together.
branches.cn: 任何被放在一起的五个。

branches.en: One added voice against the quartet.
branches.cn: 与四重奏相比多出的一个声部。

intro.en: The quint- family counts five: quint, quintet, quintile and quintuplet all divide or gather by five.
intro.cn: quint 词族数到五：quint、quintet、quintile、quintuplet 都以五来分或聚。

latinIntro.en: Latin quintus gives the stem, Italian -etto the diminutive ending that makes a group sound small and warm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quintus 提供词干，意大利语 -etto 提供指小词尾，让一个团体听起来小而温暖。

Two quintets competed.
A quint of cards.

Costs quintupled.

definition_zh: 土壤发生层；土壤剖面中因成土作用而形成的一层
definition_en: a layer within a soil profile, roughly parallel to the surface and distinguished by colour, texture or composition
core_image: 剖面上一条深褐色与浅黄色之间的清晰界线，铲尖正沿着这条线划过
scene: 剖面上深褐色的一条带在浅黄砂层处突然收住，界线十分清楚，老师说 The dark band marks the bottom of a soil horizon where clay has collected.
sceneCN: 这里 soil horizon 指「剖面中因成土作用形成的一层」，取第 1 个义项（发生层本身）；句意为这条深色带标出一个土壤层的底部，那里聚集了黏土。图中可辨识物件：层界、深色土带、浅黄砂层、取样铲。

pos.zh: 土壤发生层、土层（可数，复数 soil horizons）

derivatives.zh: 土层分化；剖面中各发生层形成与分异的过程

senses.title: A layer formed by soil processes
senses.definition: a layer in the profile whose features result from soil-forming processes rather than from the original rock
senses.definitionCN: 剖面中其特征由成土过程而非原岩决定的一层
senses.example: Each soil horizon carries evidence of how water has moved through it.
senses.exampleCN: 每个土壤层都带着水如何穿过的证据。
senses.why: Horizon in Greek meant a bounding circle, so a soil horizon is a band bounded off from the bands above and below.
senses.whyCN: horizon 在希腊语中意为「划界的圈」，因此土壤层就是与上下两层划开的一条带。

senses.title: The surface mineral layer
senses.definition: the upper mineral layer darkened by organic matter and worked by roots and soil animals
senses.definitionCN: 被有机物染深、受根系与土壤动物扰动的上部矿质层
senses.example: The surface soil horizon is where most roots and seeds are found.
senses.exampleCN: 表土层是大多数根与种子所在之处。
senses.why: Because life is concentrated at the top, the uppermost mineral band is the first one named in any description.
senses.whyCN: 由于生命集中在上部，最上的矿质带在任何描述中总是第一个被命名。

senses.title: The leached layer
senses.definition: a pale layer from which clay, iron and organic matter have been washed downward
senses.definitionCN: 黏土、铁与有机物被向下淋洗后留下的浅色层
senses.example: The pale soil horizon below the surface is a sign of strong leaching.
senses.exampleCN: 表层之下那条浅色土层是强烈淋溶的标志。
senses.why: Water moving down carries fine particles away, leaving the sand grains behind and the band bleached.
senses.whyCN: 下渗的水带走了细颗粒，留下砂粒，于是这一带被漂白。

senses.title: The accumulation layer
senses.definition: a layer enriched in clay, iron or carbonate that arrived from above
senses.definitionCN: 由上方迁入的黏土、铁或碳酸盐富集而成的层
senses.example: The red soil horizon owes its colour to iron deposited from above.
senses.exampleCN: 那条红色土层的颜色来自从上面积淀下来的铁。
senses.why: Whatever the upper layers lose has to arrive somewhere, so the band below becomes the store.
senses.whyCN: 上层失去的东西总要落到某处，因此下面那条带就成了仓库。

senses.title: The parent-material layer
senses.definition: weathered rock or sediment that has been little altered by soil processes
senses.definitionCN: 受成土过程影响很小的风化岩石或沉积物
senses.example: The lowest soil horizon still looks like the rock it came from.
senses.exampleCN: 最下面的土层看起来还像它原来的岩石。
senses.why: This layer marks the boundary between soil and geology, which is why descriptions often stop there.
senses.whyCN: 这一层标出土壤与地质的界线，因此描述常在此止步。

senses.title: The organic layer
senses.definition: litter and partly decayed plant matter sitting above the mineral soil
senses.definitionCN: 覆在矿质土壤之上的枯落物与部分腐解的植物残体
senses.example: A thick organic soil horizon keeps the ground cool and damp.
senses.exampleCN: 厚厚一层有机土层让地面保持阴凉潮湿。
senses.why: Forest floors accumulate litter faster than it decays, so a separate organic band forms above the mineral layers.
senses.whyCN: 林地枯落物堆积快于分解，因此在矿质层之上形成了一个独立的有机带。

senses.title: Transitional boundaries
senses.definition: a mixed band between two horizons, or the sharpness of the boundary itself
senses.definitionCN: 两层之间的混合带，或界线本身的清晰程度
senses.example: The boundary between these soil horizons is abrupt rather than gradual.
senses.exampleCN: 这些土层之间的界线是突变的，而不是渐变的。
senses.why: Layers rarely stop sharply, so surveyors describe both the mixed zone and the kind of boundary.
senses.whyCN: 土层很少陡然终止，因此调查者既描述混合带，也描述界线的类型。

senses.title: A diagnostic horizon
senses.definition: a horizon whose specific features are used to assign the soil to a taxonomic class
senses.definitionCN: 以其特定特征把该土壤归入某一分类单元的土层
senses.example: A clay-enriched soil horizon is diagnostic for the order it belongs to.
senses.exampleCN: 富黏土的土层是该土所属纲的诊断依据。
senses.why: Classification needs features that can be checked in the field, and a named horizon supplies exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 分类需要能在野外核对的特征，而一个有名字的土层正好提供这种特征。

intro.en: The phrase joins soil, from Latin solum through Old French, with horizon, from Greek horizōn, the bounding circle. Soil science took the word in the twentieth century for a layer marked off inside a profile.
intro.cn: 这个短语把 soil 与 horizon 结合：soil 经古法语上溯拉丁 solum，horizon 出自希腊 horizōn「划界的圈」。土壤学在二十世纪把这个词用于剖面内部被划出的一层。

items.en: Horos meant a boundary or a marker stone, and the verb horizein meant to bound or separate.
items.cn: horos 意为边界或界石，动词 horizein 意为划界、分开。

items.en: The phrase horizōn kyklos, the bounding circle, named the line where earth and sky appear to meet, and the noun horizon was kept from it.
items.cn: horizōn kyklos「划界的圈」指天地看似相接的那条线，名词 horizon 即由此截取而来。

items.en: English horizon arrived through Latin and French with the geographical sense, and later gained figurative uses such as a horizon of possibilities.
items.cn: 英语 horizon 经拉丁与法语传入，先有地理义，后来又获得「可能性的视野」这类比喻用法。

items.en: Twentieth-century soil survey applied horizon to layers that are bounded above and below, matching the original sense of a bounding line.
items.cn: 二十世纪的土壤调查把 horizon 用于上下都有界线的土层，正与原义「划界的线」相合。

items.en: The soil half of the phrase descends from Latin solum, ground or sole, by way of Old French.
items.cn: 短语中的 soil 一半经古法语上溯拉丁 solum「地面、脚底」。

note.en: Group one holds terms for layers and their arrangement; group two holds words sharing the horizon form but meaning something else.
note.cn: 第一组是表示土层及其排列的术语；第二组是共用 horizon 形式但含义不同的词。

entries.definition: The complete vertical section, of which each horizon is one band.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的垂直断面，每个土层只是其中一条带。

entries.definition: A neutral word for any band of soil; horizon implies it was formed by soil processes and can be named.
entries.definitionCN: 任何土带的中性说法；horizon 暗含它由成土过程形成、可以命名。

entries.definition: A layer of rock or sediment, usually geological rather than pedological.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石或沉积物的一层，通常属地质学而非土壤学。

entries.definition: A visible stripe of colour; it may cut across horizons rather than follow their boundaries.
entries.definitionCN: 可见的色带；它可能横切土层，而不沿层界分布。

entries.definition: The line where sky meets land, or a limit of experience; the soil sense is a technical narrowing.
entries.definitionCN: 天地相接的线，或经验的范围；土壤义是技术性的收窄。

entries.definition: The uppermost fertile layer, one particular horizon in most profiles.
entries.definitionCN: 最上部肥沃的一层，在多数剖面中是某一个特定土层。

entries.definition: The layer beneath the topsoil, often corresponding to the accumulation horizon.
entries.definitionCN: 表土之下的一层，常对应淀积层。

entries.definition: The rock or deposit from which the soil formed; it may sit below the lowest horizon or be the lowest one.
entries.definitionCN: 形成土壤的岩石或沉积物；它可能位于最低土层之下，也可能就是最低那层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek boundary word, the real letter names used in descriptions and real paired terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊「界线」词、描述中真实使用的字母代号，以及真实的成对术语。

normal.en: Horizon means a line that bounds: a horizon bounds the soil above from the soil below.
normal.cn: horizon 意为划界的线：一个土层把上面的土与下面的土分开。

normal.en: Leached above, accumulated below: the pale and the red layers come as a pair.
normal.cn: 上面淋走，下面淀积：浅色层与红色层成对出现。

normal.en: Litter on top, parent material at the bottom: the profile has two fixed ends.
normal.cn: 顶部是枯落物，底部是母质：剖面两端是固定的。

normal.en: Boundaries are described as sharp, gradual or mixed.
normal.cn: 层界被描述为突变、渐变或混合。

normal.en: A diagnostic horizon is the one a classifier points to when naming the soil.
normal.cn: 诊断层就是分类者给土壤命名时所指的那一层。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of coloured papers where each sheet ends exactly where the next begins.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠彩色纸，每张纸结束的地方正是下一张开始的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a sieve that keeps the sand and lets the clay fall to the shelf below.
abstract.cn: 想象一只筛子留下砂，让黏土落到下面那一层。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn on a wall so clean that nobody argues where one band ends.
abstract.cn: 想象在墙上划的一条线干净利落，没人争论一条带在哪里结束。

examples.en: The clay-enriched soil horizon was almost a metre thick.
examples.cn: 这个富黏土的土层差不多有一米厚。

examples.en: Colour alone is not enough to identify a soil horizon.
examples.cn: 仅凭颜色不足以辨认一个土壤层。

examples.en: Water stops at the boundary of the dense soil horizon.
examples.cn: 水在那个紧实土层的界线上停住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「土 + 地平线」——剖面里也有一条条像地平线的分界，跨过去就换了一层土

root: soil（古法语 soil，上溯拉丁 solum「地面」）+ horizon（希腊 horizōn「划界的圈」，源于 horos「边界」）；「剖面中被界线划出的一层土」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move down a profile: the general layer, the surface layer, the leached layer, the accumulation layer, the parent material, the organic layer on top, the boundary itself, and the diagnostic layer used in classification.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着剖面自上而下推进：总称的层、表层、淋溶层、淀积层、母质层、顶部的有机层、界线本身，以及分类所用的诊断层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sharp line on a pit wall where dark soil ends and pale sand begins.
core.cn: 核心意象：坑壁上一条清晰的界线，深色土到此为止，浅黄砂从此开始。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES: a layer is defined by the lines above and below it, and by how sharp those lines are.
branches.cn: 界线：一层由上下两条线界定，也由这两条线的清晰程度界定。

branches.en: LIFE AT THE TOP: roots and animals mix organic matter into the upper mineral band.
branches.cn: 顶部的生命：根系与动物把有机物混进上部矿质带。

branches.en: MOVEMENT: one band loses clay and iron, the band beneath stores them.
branches.cn: 迁移：一条带失去黏土与铁，下面那条把它们存起来。

branches.en: GEOLOGY: the lowest band is rock that soil processes have barely touched.
branches.cn: 地质：最下面那条是成土过程几乎未触及的岩石。

branches.en: BOOKENDS: litter above, and the diagnostic layer that gives the soil its name.
branches.cn: 两端：上方是枯落物，而诊断层则给这种土壤定名。

intro.en: Soil horizon joins a Latin-derived noun with a Greek-derived one: soil from solum, horizon from horos plus the ending -izōn.
intro.cn: soil horizon 把拉丁来源的名词与希腊来源的名词结合：soil 出自 solum，horizon 出自 horos 加词尾 -izōn。

latinIntro.en: Only the soil half has Latin ancestry; horizon is Greek and Latin borrowed it rather than inheriting it, so no genuine Latin entry exists for that half.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 soil 一半有拉丁语来源；horizon 是希腊语词，拉丁语是借用而非继承，因此该一半没有真正的拉丁词条。

items.example: Soil descends from solum through French.
The horizon element originally named a boundary.
items.exampleCN: horizon 这一成分原指一条边界。

items.example: The verb supplies the participle behind horizon.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了 horizon 背后的分词形式。

items.example: The horizon between the bands was easy to follow.
items.exampleCN: 两条带之间的界线很容易跟着看。

items.example: Soil horizons are roughly horizontal.
Water moved horizontally along the boundary.
Topsoil is the first horizon in the description.
items.exampleCN: 表土是描述中的第一个土层。

items.example: The subsoil horizon held most of the clay.
items.exampleCN: 底土层含住了大部分黏土。

items.meaning: the line where one layer ends
items.example: The boundary was sharp and easy to trace.

latinEntries.example: The soil half of the term comes from this noun.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 该术语中 soil 一半来自这个名词。

definition_zh: 含情脉脉的；多情的；表示爱情的；好色的
definition_en: showing love or sexual desire, especially in looks or behavior
core_image: 眼波流转的目光：眼里藏不住爱意
scene: 烛光晚餐上，他望着爱人，眼里满是温柔笑意。 He gave his wife an amorous glance across the candlelit table.
sceneCN: 这里的 amorous 是「含情脉脉的」（第 1 个义项：流露爱意的）；句意是他在烛光餐桌对面深情地望了妻子一眼。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「含情地；多情地」
形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「多情；柔情」
加施动者后缀 -ist 构成，义为「写爱情主题的作家；多情的人」

senses.title: Showing love in looks or manner
senses.titleCN: 含情脉脉的：神情举止流露爱意
senses.definition: expressing romantic love through glances, gestures, or words
senses.definitionCN: 以眼神、举止或言语表达浪漫爱意
senses.example: The poet described lovers trading amorous glances.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人描写恋人之间交换含情的目光。
senses.why: From Latin amor, love: whatever love shows on the surface is amorous.
senses.whyCN: 源自拉丁语 amor「爱」：爱流露在表面的一切就是 amorous。

senses.title: Strongly inclined to romance or desire
senses.definition: having or readily showing strong romantic or sexual desire
senses.definitionCN: 具有或易于表现出强烈的浪漫或情欲渴望
senses.example: Spring makes even the oldest tomcat amorous.
senses.exampleCN: 春天连最老的雄猫都动了春心。
senses.why: Love as a force inside a person, not just a gesture, becomes an inclination.
senses.whyCN: 爱不只是流露的姿态，更是体内的力量，于是词义变成一种「倾向」。

senses.title: Concerning sexual desire
senses.titleCN: 情欲的：偏重肉体的渴望
senses.definition: relating to sexual appetite rather than tender affection
senses.definitionCN: 偏指性欲而非温柔爱慕
senses.example: The novel censors blurred its amorous passages.
senses.exampleCN: 书刊审查模糊了小说中的情欲段落。
senses.why: Romance and appetite share the same root word, and usage can tilt to either.
senses.whyCN: 浪漫与欲望共用同一词根，用法的重心可以偏向任何一边。

senses.title: Of love as a literary subject
senses.definition: pertaining to love as a theme in literature or art
senses.definitionCN: 关于文学艺术中爱情主题的
senses.example: The troubadours wrote amorous songs for the court.
senses.exampleCN: 游吟诗人为宫廷谱写爱情歌曲。
senses.why: Once love becomes material for art, the adjective labels the genre.
senses.whyCN: 当爱成为艺术素材，形容词便用来标记这一题材。

senses.title: Eagerly pursuing romance
senses.definition: actively courting or pursuing someone romantically
senses.definitionCN: 主动向人示爱求爱
senses.example: An amorous suitor left flowers at her door daily.
senses.exampleCN: 一位痴情的追求者每天在她门口留下鲜花。
senses.why: Desire presses toward action; the word follows the motion of courtship.
senses.whyCN: 渴望会推动行动，这个词便追随求爱的动作。

intro.en: Amorous comes from Latin amor, love, through Old French amoreus, replacing an older native formation.
intro.cn: amorous 源自拉丁语 amor「爱」，经古法语 amoreus 进入英语，取代了较早的本族构词。

items.en: Root *am-, to love.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *am-「爱」。

items.en: amor, love; amare, to love; also Cupid's title Amor.
items.cn: 拉丁语 amor「爱」；amare「爱」；也是丘比特的别称 Amor。

items.en: amoreus, full of love.
items.cn: 古法语 amoreus「充满爱意的」。

items.en: amorous appears in courtly love poetry.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 amorous 出现在宫廷爱情诗中。

items.en: Chaucer and successors used it for both tender love and appetite.
items.cn: 乔叟及其后继者用它兼指温柔之爱与情欲。

items.en: Now covers romantic expression, desire, love themes, and courtship.
items.cn: 如今涵盖浪漫表达、情欲、爱情题材与求爱。

note.en: Distinguish amorous from amiable and amicable, and from near words of desire and romance.
note.cn: 区分 amorous 与 amiable、amicable，以及表示欲望与浪漫的近义词。

entries.definition: friendly in character; amiable people are pleasant, amorous ones are in love.
entries.definitionCN: 和蔼可亲的；amiable 说性格，amorous 说爱意，同根易混。

entries.definition: without moral sense; from a- plus moral, not from amor.

definition_zh: 工业化；产业化
definition_en: the large-scale development of industry in a country or region, especially the shift from agriculture and craft work to factory production
core_image: 田野上竖起一排烟囱，村庄被厂房和铁轨包围
scene: 这里指「工业化」。 Between 1760 and 1840, industrialization turned British textile towns into smoky factory cities. Families that had spun thread at home moved into mills powered by steam.
sceneCN: 这里 industrialization 是「工业化过程」（第 1 个义项：从农业与手工业转向工厂生产的经济转型）；句意：1760 至 1840 年间，工业化把英国的纺织城镇变成烟雾缭绕的工厂城市；原先在家纺线的家庭搬进了蒸汽驱动的工厂。图中可辨识物件：烟囱、厂房、铁轨、纱线、蒸汽机。

senses.title: The shift from farming and crafts to factory production
senses.titleCN: 工业化：从农业手工业转向工厂生产
senses.definition: the economic process by which a country or region moves from agriculture and handcrafts to machine-based factory production
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或地区从农业和手工业转向机器工厂生产的经济过程
senses.example: Industrialization began with textiles and later spread to iron and transport.
senses.exampleCN: 工业化始于纺织业，后来扩展到钢铁和运输。
senses.why: Latin industria meant 'diligence, activity'; -ize means 'to make', and -ation names the process. So industrialization is literally the process of making an economy industrious in the new, factory sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 industria 意为「勤勉、活动」；-ize 意为「使」，-ation 命名过程。因此 industrialization 字面上就是把经济变成勤勉的、以工厂为核心的经济这一过程。

senses.title: A historical period of industrial growth
senses.definition: a particular historical era in which a country's industry grows rapidly and changes its economy
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家的工业迅速增长并改变其经济的特定历史时期
senses.example: British industrialization is usually placed between 1760 and 1840.
senses.exampleCN: 英国的工业化通常被定在 1760 至 1840 年之间。
senses.why: The suffix -ation can name a whole course of events, not only an abstract process. Because the course has a beginning and an end, it can be dated as a historical period.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ation 可命名一整段事件进程，而不只是抽象过程。因为这段进程有起点和终点，所以可以被确定为历史时期。

senses.title: The state of being industrial
senses.titleCN: 工业化程度；工业化状态
senses.definition: the degree to which a country or region has developed modern industry
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或地区发展现代工业所达到的程度
senses.example: Regions differ widely in their level of industrialization.
senses.exampleCN: 各地区工业化程度差异很大。
senses.why: The same action noun also denotes the result of the action: once the process is complete, what remains is a condition, and one can measure its level.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作名词也指动作的结果：过程完成后留下的是一个状态，而状态是可以测量其程度的。

senses.title: The reorganization of work into factories
senses.definition: the reorganization of production into large units with machines, specialized tasks, and wage labour
senses.definitionCN: 把生产重组为使用机器、分工任务和雇工劳动的大型单位
senses.example: Industrialization separated the worker from the tools he had once owned.
senses.exampleCN: 工业化使工人与他曾拥有的工具分离。
senses.why: industry shifted from 'diligence' to 'systematic manufacturing'. Industrialization is the moment when that system takes over the workshop, gathering tools and workers under one roof.
senses.whyCN: industry 从「勤勉」转向「系统的制造业」。工业化就是这套体系接管作坊的时刻：把工具与工人聚到同一屋顶下。

senses.title: The social change that follows factory growth
senses.titleCN: 工业化带来的社会变迁
senses.definition: the social transformation caused by industrial growth, especially urbanization and the rise of a wage-earning working class
senses.definitionCN: 工业增长引起的社会转变，尤指城市化和挣工资的工人阶级的兴起
senses.example: Industrialization drew peasants into cities and broke up extended families.
senses.exampleCN: 工业化把农民吸引进城市，并拆散了大家庭。
senses.why: A factory gathers many workers at one point. That gathering is a physical fact that becomes a social one: the mill gate produces the city street and the working class by contiguity.
senses.whyCN: 工厂把许多工人聚集在一点。这种聚集是物理事实，却因相邻而成为社会事实：工厂大门催生了城市街道与工人阶级。

senses.title: A phase of building heavy industry
senses.definition: a stage of economic development in which heavy industry such as steel, coal, and machinery is built up on a large scale
senses.definitionCN: 大规模建设钢铁、煤炭、机械等重工业的经济发展阶段
senses.example: The five-year plans pushed a second wave of industrialization centred on steel.
senses.exampleCN: 五年计划推动了以钢铁为核心的第二次工业化浪潮。
senses.why: Once industry means manufacturing in general, adding the idea of scale yields a phase sense: industrialization can proceed by building heavier and larger plants, wave after wave.
senses.whyCN: 当 industry 泛指制造业之后，再加上规模观念就得到阶段义：工业化可以一波接一波地通过建设更重、更大的工厂来推进。

senses.title: A state policy of promoting industry
senses.titleCN: 工业化政策；工业化战略
senses.definition: a deliberate government programme or strategy to build up industry, often by protecting or subsidizing it
senses.definitionCN: 政府有意推动工业建设的计划或战略，常通过保护或补贴工业
senses.example: Import-substitution industrialization protected local factories with high tariffs.
senses.exampleCN: 进口替代工业化用高关税保护本地工厂。
senses.why: An -ation noun can name a programme as well as a natural process. Governments can 'carry out' industrialization, so the word becomes the label of a policy.
senses.whyCN: -ation 名词既可命名自然过程，也可命名计划。政府可以「推行」工业化，于是这个词成为政策的标签。

senses.title: Applying factory methods to another sector
senses.titleCN: 某一部门的工业化（如农业）
senses.definition: the application of industrial methods such as machinery, standardization, and large-scale organization to a non-manufacturing sector
senses.definitionCN: 把机械、标准化和大型组织等工业方法应用到非制造业部门
senses.example: The industrialization of agriculture replaced small farms with mechanized estates.
senses.exampleCN: 农业的工业化以机械化大农场取代了小农场。
senses.why: Because the suffix means 'making X-like industry', it can attach to any sector: to industrialize farming is to make farming behave like industry.
senses.whyCN: 由于该后缀意为「使某部门变得像工业」，它可以附着在任何部门：使农业工业化，就是让农业按工业方式运作。

senses.title: Treating an activity as standardized production
senses.titleCN: 引申：把活动变成标准化的产业流程
senses.definition: the metaphorical reorganization of an activity into standardized, measurable, high-volume stages, as in education or health care
senses.definitionCN: 隐喻性地把某项活动重组为标准化、可计量、大批量的阶段，如教育或医疗
senses.example: Critics speak of the industrialization of care, where patients become units on a spreadsheet.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者谈到照护的工业化，病人变成了表格上的单位。
senses.why: The factory is no longer needed for the metaphor: any activity cut into uniform, countable steps has taken on the shape of industry, so it is said to be industrialized.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻不再需要工厂本身：任何被切成统一、可计数步骤的活动都具备了工业的形态，因此被说成工业化。

intro.en: Industrialization is an English noun built on the verb industrialize, from industrial, from industry. Industry descends from Latin industria 'diligence, activity'; the suffixes -ize and -ation come from Greek and Latin.
intro.cn: industrialization 是在动词 industrialize 上构成的英语名词，industrialize 来自 industrial，industrial 来自 industry。industry 上溯拉丁 industria「勤勉、活动」；后缀 -ize 与 -ation 分别来自希腊语和拉丁语。

items.en: industria meant 'diligence, activity, care'. Its deeper origin is uncertain: it is generally thought to be indu- (a form of in-) plus struere 'to build', but this reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: industria 意为「勤勉、活动、用心」。其更深来源不确定：一般认为是 indu-（in- 的一种形式）加 struere「建造」，但这只是重构，并非定论。

items.en: The adjective industrius meant 'diligent, active'. From it English inherited the sense of hard work that survives in industrious.
items.cn: 形容词 industrius 意为「勤勉的、活跃的」。英语由此继承了「勤奋」这一意义，保留在 industrious 中。

items.en: Old French industrie passed the word to English, where industry first meant 'diligence, skill' and only later 'systematic manufacturing'. The older sense survives in the adjective industrious.
items.cn: 古法语 industrie 把词传给英语；industry 最初意为「勤勉、技艺」，后来才指「系统的制造业」。较古的意义保留在形容词 industrious 中。

items.en: -ize comes from Greek -izein 'to make, cause to be', through Latin -izare. It turns a noun or adjective into a verb of making: industrial → industrialize.
items.cn: -ize 来自希腊 -izein「使某事发生、使成为」，经拉丁 -izare 传入。它把名词或形容词变成表示「使之成为」的动词：industrial → industrialize。

items.en: -ation comes from Latin -atio, the suffix of action and its result. Added to industrialize, it names the whole process and its outcome: industrialization.
items.cn: -ation 来自拉丁 -atio，是动作及其结果的名词后缀。加在 industrialize 上，它命名整个过程及其结果：industrialization。

items.en: Industrialization is generally dated to the 19th century and follows French industrialisation. It became a standard term when economics began describing the shift from farm to factory as a single historical process.
items.cn: industrialization 一般认为是 19 世纪的词，紧随法语 industrialisation 出现。当经济学开始把从农场到工厂的转变描述为单一历史过程时，它成为标准术语。

note.en: Group one shares the Latin base industria; group two is close in meaning but each comes from a different root (modernus, mekhane, urbs, manus + facere).
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词基 industria；第二组意义相近，但各自来自不同词根（modernus、mekhane、urbs、manus + facere）。

entries.definition: manufacturing as a branch of business; also the older sense 'diligent work'. From Latin industria
entries.definitionCN: 作为产业部门的制造业；也有较古的「勤勉」义。来自拉丁 industria

entries.definition: relating to industry or manufacturing; from industry + Latin -alis
entries.definitionCN: 与工业或制造业相关的；由 industry 加拉丁 -alis 构成

entries.definition: a person who owns or manages a large industrial business; -ist marks the person, not the process
entries.definitionCN: 拥有或经营大型工业企业的人；-ist 标记人，而非过程

entries.definition: hard-working and diligent; it kept the original 'diligence' sense of industria and has nothing to do with factories
entries.definitionCN: 勤劳的、勤勉的；它保留了 industria 原初的「勤勉」义，与工厂无关

entries.definition: the process of adopting modern methods and ideas; broader than industrialization, which concerns manufacturing in particular
entries.definitionCN: 采用现代方法与观念的过程；比 industrialization 更广，后者特指制造业

entries.definition: replacing human or animal labour with machines; a part of industrialization, not the whole of it
entries.definitionCN: 用机器替代人力或畜力；是工业化的一部分，而非全部

entries.definition: the growth of towns and cities; often a consequence of industrialization rather than a synonym
entries.definitionCN: 城镇与城市的增长；常是工业化的后果，而非同义词

entries.definition: the making of goods in large quantities; the activity that industrialization expands and reorganizes
entries.definitionCN: 大批量制造商品；工业化所扩大并重组的生产活动

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: industria 'diligence' + -ize 'make' + -ation 'process': the word literally names the making of a diligent, factory-based economy.
normal.cn: industria「勤勉」+ -ize「使」+ -ation「过程」：这个词字面上命名了把经济变成勤勉的、以工厂为基础的经济这一过程。

normal.en: industry first meant diligence; industrialization is the historical process that turned that diligence into mills and machines.
normal.cn: industry 最初意为勤勉；industrialization 是把这种勤勉转成工厂与机器的历史过程。

normal.en: The verb is industrialize and the noun is industrialization, exactly like modernize and modernization.
normal.cn: 动词是 industrialize，名词是 industrialization，正如 modernize 与 modernization。

normal.en: The chain industry → industrial → industrialize → industrialization adds one grammatical layer at a time.
normal.cn: industry → industrial → industrialize → industrialization 这条链每次加一层语法成分。

normal.en: Picture a farm with a mill rising beside it: that single change, seen as a national process, is industrialization.
normal.cn: 想象农场旁立起一座工厂：把这一变化看作全国性的过程，就是 industrialization。

abstract.en: Think of a chimney replacing a church tower as the tallest thing in town; that swap is the visible signature of industrialization.
abstract.cn: 把城镇最高处从教堂尖塔换成一截烟囱；这个替换就是工业化最可见的标志。

abstract.en: Think of a loom moving out of a cottage into a mill: the same motion, but now organized as a system.
abstract.cn: 把织机从农舍搬进工厂：动作相同，但如今被组织成一套系统。

abstract.en: Think of a timeline with fields on the left and factories on the right; industrialization is the arrow between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一条时间线，左边是田野，右边是工厂；工业化就是两者之间的箭头。

examples.en: Japan's industrialization was compressed into a few decades after 1868.
examples.cn: 日本的工业化在 1868 年之后被压缩到几十年内完成。

examples.en: Rapid industrialization polluted the river within a single generation.
examples.cn: 快速的工业化在一代人之内就污染了这条河。

examples.en: The industrialization of higher education has turned courses into standardized products.
examples.cn: 高等教育的工业化把课程变成了标准化产品。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: industry（勤勉／工业）+ -ize（使之化）+ -ation（过程）→ 使国家转为工业体系的过程 → industrialization 工业化；词根本义是「勤勉、活动」

root: 拉丁 industria「勤勉、活动」，一般认为是 indu-（in）+ struere「建造」；经古法语 industrie 进入英语，再加希腊来源的 -ize 与拉丁 -ation，构成表示「使之工业化」的过程名词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all follow one arc: diligence becomes systematic work, systematic work becomes manufacturing, and manufacturing spreads until it reorganizes a whole economy, its cities, its policies, and even its schools.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一条弧线展开：勤勉变成系统化劳动，系统化劳动变成制造业，制造业扩散开来，直到重组整个经济、城市、政策乃至学校。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the farm horizon broken by chimneys and rail lines.
core.cn: 核心意象：农场地平线被烟囱与铁轨切开。

branches.en: THE PROCESS ITSELF: the transition, its historical stages, and the level a country reaches.
branches.cn: 过程本身：转型、其历史阶段，以及一国达到的程度。

branches.en: PRODUCTION REORGANIZED: work gathered into factories, and later whole sectors such as farming run like factories.
branches.cn: 生产重组：劳动集中到工厂，后来农业等整个部门也按工厂方式运作。

branches.en: SOCIETY RESHAPED: mills pull workers into cities and create a new working class.
branches.cn: 社会重塑：工厂把工人拉进城市，造就新的工人阶级。

branches.en: SCALE AND POLICY: heavy-industry phases and state strategies for building an industrial base.
branches.cn: 规模与政策：重工业阶段与国家建设工业基础的战略。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any activity cut into standardized, measurable stages is said to be industrialized.
branches.cn: 隐喻：任何被切成标准化、可计量阶段的活动都被称为工业化。

intro.en: Industrialization is a three-layer construction: industry + -al + -ize + -ation. Each suffix is productive and each adds a clear grammatical step from thing to quality to action to process.
intro.cn: industrialization 是三层构造：industry + -al + -ize + -ation。每个后缀都能产，且各加一个清晰的语法步骤：从事物到性质、到动作、再到过程。

latinIntro.en: Latin industria 'diligence' produced industrious and industry; the later industrial family was built in French and English on the manufacturing sense. The root appears as industr-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 industria「勤勉」产生了 industrious 与 industry；后来的 industrial 词族是在法语和英语中依制造业义搭建的。词根以 industr- 形式出现。

items.meaning: manufacturing as a sector; diligent work
items.meaningCN: 工业；行业；勤勉（经古法语 industrie 来自拉丁 industria）
items.example: The steel industry employs thousands of workers.
items.exampleCN: 钢铁工业雇用了数千名工人。

items.meaningCN: 勤劳的；勤勉的（-ous 形容词后缀）
items.example: She was an industrious student who never wasted an hour.
items.exampleCN: 她是个勤奋的学生，从不浪费一小时。

items.meaningCN: 工业的（-al 形容词后缀）
items.example: Industrial output rose sharply last year.
items.exampleCN: 去年工业产出大幅上升。

items.meaning: an owner or manager of large industry
items.meaningCN: 工业家；实业家（-ist 指人名词）
items.example: The industrialist built a model town for his workers.
items.exampleCN: 这位工业家为工人建了一座模范城镇。

items.meaning: to develop industry in a place
items.meaningCN: 使工业化（-ize 动词后缀）
items.example: The government tried to industrialize the rural south.
items.exampleCN: 政府试图使南方乡村工业化。

items.meaningCN: 工业化（-ation 过程名词后缀）
items.example: Industrialization changed the face of the country.
items.exampleCN: 工业化改变了这个国家的面貌。

items.meaningCN: 工业化的（-ed 形容词后缀）
items.example: Industrialized nations dominate the export market.
items.exampleCN: 工业化国家主导着出口市场。

items.meaning: to reduce industrial activity in a region
items.example: The region deindustrialized after the mines closed.
items.exampleCN: 矿场关闭后该地区去工业化了。

items.meaning: a social order organized around large-scale industry
items.meaningCN: 工业主义（-ism 学说／制度名词）
items.example: Critics attacked the values of industrialism.
items.exampleCN: 批评者抨击工业主义的价值观。
